title: The Language of Chatbots as a Tool for Building Customer Satisfaction in Digital Marketing
abstract: This project focuses on the language of chatbots as a tool for building customer satisfaction in digital marketing. It addresses the growing use of chatbots in digital brand communication and the need for systematic research into their linguistic, stylistic and pragmatic strategies in the Slovak e-commerce environment. The research examines how chatbot language influences customer experience, trust, satisfaction, brand perception and willingness to continue interaction. It combines corpus-linguistic, qualitative, quantitative and experimental approaches, including the analysis of real chatbot interactions and the testing of linguistic variants. The project aims to develop an interdisciplinary framework for evaluating the quality of chatbot communication and to formulate practical recommendations for linguistically and marketing-effective chatbots. This OSF page serves as a transparent archive of selected project outputs, publications, conference materials, datasets and supplementary research documentation.

title: A noise-robust over-sampling method for imbalanced transmission production data classification
abstract: Abstract In the automotive industry, quality assurance is crucial for ensuring safety and performance. An integral part of quality assurance is Noise, Vibration and Harshness (NVH) testing in transmission production. NVH testing utilizes sensors such as accelerometers, microphones, and encoders to capture acoustic and dynamic characteristics under simulated road conditions. Traditionally, these characteristics are evaluated against manually defined thresholds set by NVH engineers—a process that is labor intensive, costly, and complex. Although advances in machine learning (ML) offer the potential to improve efficiency in NVH testing, challenges such as severe class imbalance, outliers, and limited access to production data hinder its adoption. To address these challenges, we propose Modified Z-Score Cyclic Exponential Averaging of Minority Data ( $$mZ$$ mZ - $$cEAMD$$ cEAMD ) , a noise-robust over-sampling method that integrates exponential averaging with outlier removal to generate balanced and representative samples, while preserving the fundamental characteristics of the original data distribution. This is complemented by a feature extraction approach that integrates spectral order tracking, which captures gear meshing frequencies relative to input rotation speed, with the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT), which represents time-frequency characteristics. Together, these features contain critical discriminative information for transmission classification and are used to assess the effectiveness of the proposed over-sampling method. Comparative experiments against established over-sampling methods demonstrate that the proposed $$mZ$$ mZ - $$cEAMD$$ cEAMD approach outperforms alternative techniques in addressing class imbalance in datasets containing outliers. evidence.title: A noise-robust over-sampling method for imbalanced transmission production data classification
evidence.abstract: Abstract In the automotive industry, quality assurance is crucial for ensuring safety and performance. An integral part of quality assurance is Noise, Vibration and Harshness (NVH) testing in transmission production. NVH testing utilizes sensors such as accelerometers, microphones, and encoders to capture acoustic and dynamic characteristics under simulated road conditions. Traditionally, these characteristics are evaluated against manually defined thresholds set by NVH engineers—a process that is labor intensive, costly, and complex. Although advances in machine learning (ML) offer the potential to improve efficiency in NVH testing, challenges such as severe class imbalance, outliers, and limited access to production data hinder its adoption. To address these challenges, we propose Modified Z-Score Cyclic Exponential Averaging of Minority Data ( $$mZ$$ mZ - $$cEAMD$$ cEAMD ) , a noise-robust over-sampling method that integrates exponential averaging with outlier removal to generate balanced and representative samples, while preserving the fundamental characteristics of the original data distribution. This is complemented by a feature extraction approach that integrates spectral order tracking, which captures gear meshing frequencies relative to input rotation speed, with the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT), which represents time-frequency characteristics. Together, these features contain critical discriminative information for transmission classification and are used to assess the effectiveness of the proposed over-sampling method. Comparative experiments against established over-sampling methods demonstrate that the proposed $$mZ$$ mZ - $$cEAMD$$ cEAMD approach outperforms alternative techniques in addressing class imbalance in datasets containing outliers. This study advances ML-based NVH testing, thereby fostering the digital transformation of automotive quality assurance.

title: Full-Page Optical Music Recognition of Handwritten Monophonic Scores
abstract: Full-page end-to-end Optical Music Recognition seeks to transcribe entire music pages directly into symbolic notation, avoiding the limitations of traditional pipelines that rely on accurate staff segmentation. Recent Transformer-based architectures have achieved strong performance on typeset scores, relying on large-scale synthetic data for pretraining. However, their applicability to handwritten music remains largely unexplored. In this work, we study full-page transcription on handwritten monophonic collections and analyze the impact of synthetic pretraining in this setting. To investigate which factors are most relevant during pretraining, we introduce a generator capable of producing visually coherent full-page scores in both typeset and handwritten styles. Experiments on three real handwritten datasets provide a comparative evaluation of several full-page pipelines and different synthetic pretraining strategies. The results suggest that the benefits of synthetic pretraining are primarily associated with learning structural layout conventions rather than with visual similarity to the target handwriting.

title: Methane Detection On Board Satellites from Unorthorectified Imagery
abstract: As a potent greenhouse gas, methane is a major driver of climate change. Its effective mitigation relies on timely detection. Conventional detection methods rely on orthorectification to correct geometric distortions and matched filters to enhance plume signals, which are steps designed for ground processing and poorly suited to onboard execution. We introduce UnorthoDOS, a dataset and approach for training machine learning models directly on unorthorectified hyperspectral imagery, bypassing both orthorectification and matched-filter products. Our U-Net models trained on unorthorectified data approach the performance of models trained on orthorectified data (IoU 16.91% vs. 18.47% on all plumes), while both substantially outperform the mag1c matched-filter baseline (IoU 4.76%). We further demonstrate the feasibility of onboard deployment: FP16 compression halves model size with under 0.3% output deviation. The trained ML models and two ML-ready datasets -- orthorectified and unorthorectified hyperspectral imagery from the EMIT sensor -- are publicly available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/SpaceML/UnorthoDOS, with code at https://github.com/spaceml-org/plume-hunter.

title: Continuous Cognitive Coverage for Autonomous Robots via Event-Dependent Cognitive Treatment and Learning
abstract: Autonomous robots continuously encounter objects, changes, and situations, and every event admitted into cognition should receive an appropriate cognitive treatment rather than remain untreated until an explicit task requires attention. However, existing task-driven, reactive, or fixed-reasoning approaches generally process only selected events or apply predefined reasoning procedures, making it difficult to provide continuous cognitive coverage with differentiated treatment. This paper proposes a continuous cognitive coverage framework in which every cognitively admitted event is assigned an event-dependent cognitive treatment according to its state, context, and history. Different events may therefore invoke description, memory, risk prediction, planning, diagnosis, analogy, or other learned treatments. Familiar events can be processed automatically by learned mechanisms, whereas unfamiliar or uncertain events invoke explicit deliberation or fallback reasoning. Multiple cognitive processes can be suspended, resumed, and interleaved so that cognitive processing continues as new events arrive or existing events await evidence. Validated experiences are continuously learned to automate, refine, and revise event-specific treatments. Experiments achieve 96.76% structured treatment accuracy with 93.66% automatic processing, 92.64% cognitive coverage under bursty-delayed workloads, and 79.53% continual-learning joint accuracy, with novel-event reuse reaching 100% automatic processing.

title: A Differentiable Neural Surrogate for Photon Propagation in Neutrino Telescopes
abstract: Large-volume neutrino telescopes infer neutrino properties from Cherenkov light, but simulating the transport of billions of photons through highly scattering ice or water is computationally costly. We introduce candela, a differentiable SIREN neural field that learns the photon Green's function of the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, a cubic-kilometer detector embedded in Antarctic glacial ice. Given a point-like energy deposit and sensor, it predicts the expected photon yield and full arrival-time distribution at the sensor. Complete events are simulated by decomposing charged-particle energy deposits into point-like sources and superposing their predicted sensor responses. Trained on Monte-Carlo simulations, candela generates events $50$--$100\times$ faster than existing methods, with cost scaling only weakly with neutrino energy. It keeps median yields within $2\%$ of the MC expectation and timing distributions at the MC statistical floor across six photon-count decades. The model also provides end-to-end gradients with respect to event parameters and opens a path toward optimizing scattering-medium properties, which often dominate systematic uncertainties in neutrino telescopes.

title: KSCCN Signed Memory: Cross-Session Narrative Integrity and Cognitive Sovereignty in the Post-Quantum Stack
abstract: The first three volumes of this series relocated post-quantum policy from the algorithm catalogue to the archive (Mamun, 2026a), from the unbuilt hall to a layered portfolio of sovereignty (Mamun, 2026b), and from a Q-day step function to a fluid estate that must change cryptographic posture as the threat surface moves (Mamun, 2026c). This fourth volume treats the object that those three claims jointly produce: an archive that acts. Enterprise and sovereign systems are no longer static repositories. They retrieve, write and re-weight contextual memory across sessions in order to infer and to decide. In that setting the high-value target is not yesterday's file. It is tomorrow's persona. An adversary who cannot read a payload can still poison the narrative stream that conditions future judgment. Cross-session narrative memory (CSNM) is therefore specified as an integrity architecture, not as a product feature. The paper defines the memory block, the assimilation gate, the dual clock of index and payload, and the rotation rule that lets signature primitives change without breaking historical custody. Cognitive sovereignty — introduced politically in Volume II — is restated as an engineering property: the capacity to know which blocks were admitted, by whom, under which key, and to refuse the unsigned. Implications are drawn for public-sector agents, for national language models as public personas, and for the Observatory's audit of algorithmic memory. title: Concurrent stabilizer extraction induces signed interactions between memories that averaging conceals and timing suppresses -- data and analysis
abstract: Measurement data and analysis code for the manuscript Concurrent stabilizer extraction induces signed interactions between memories that averaging conceals and timing suppresses. Fourteen hardware campaigns on an IBM Heron processor: design manifests, gate records and results, together with the per-block transition count tables and per-shot syndrome registers from which every reported statistic is computed. python reproduce.py runs 24 checks against the published values, offline and with no quantum-computing account. Eight are recomputed from the raw counts on every run; fourteen are regenerated on request by the five scripts in analysis/; two are read from a deposited result and compared. title: An Isolated, Attested, and Governed Network for Trustworthy AI Research and Deployment: A Reference Architecture, Threat Model, and Roadmap
abstract: Abstract— Emerging AI systems increasingly exhibit capabilities—autonomous code generation, tool use, and self-replication potential—that make the public Internet an unsuitable substrate for high-consequence AI research and deployment. This whitepaper reformulates an early-stage dual-system concept (an untrusted “System A” comprising the Internet/IoT, and an isolated “System B” for AI R&D) into a rigorous reference architecture. We contribute: (1) a structured critical assessment of the baseline concept; (2) a layered, zero-trust reference architecture with an explicit trust root, attested cross-domain gateways, confidential tenant workspaces, and least-privilege autonomous guardians; (3) a three-plane protocol redesign (data, control, resource) that corrects the baseline’s conflation of network and resource abstractions; (4) a formalized governance pipeline reconciling ethical screening with auditability, including anonymous-but-linkable telemetry; and (5) a three-phase, metric-gated roadmap traceable to program deliverables (Technical Areas 1.1, 1.2, 2) and aligned with NIST SP 800-207, the NIST AI RMF, IEEE 7000, and MITRE ATLAS. Index Terms— Zero-trust architecture, cross-domain solutions, confidential computing, AI security, trustworthy AI, research networks, provenance, governance.

title: Geometric Proofs for Machine Learning Model Robustness
abstract: This paper explores the application of geometric proofs to enhance the robustness of machine learning models, particularly against adversarial attacks and data drift. We propose a framework that leverages geometric techniques – specifically, the representation of model sensitivity as geometric objects – to provide mathematically rigorous guarantees on model behavior. The core mechanism centers around establishing robustness through rigorous geometric analysis, offering a novel approach to model security compared to traditional methods. This work aims to improve the reliability and trustworthiness of machine learning systems by incorporating a fundamental mathematical tool.

title: Self-Adaptive Chaos Geometry Optimization via Probabilistic Methods
abstract: This paper presents a novel optimization algorithm based on probabilistic chaos geometry, specifically designed for complex systems exhibiting chaotic behavior. The core concept revolves around modeling the system's dynamics as a probabilistic chaos field, allowing for adaptive adjustments to parameters and control strategies. We leverage the inherent unpredictability of chaotic systems to achieve robust and responsive optimization. This work introduces a novel framework incorporating a probabilistic field prediction and adjustment mechanism, providing a more flexible and adaptive approach compared to traditional optimization techniques. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through simulations focusing on a system involving non-linear dynamics and sensitivity to initial conditions. The research emphasizes the potential for self-adaptive optimization in challenging environments, offering a promising pathway for managing complex systems with inherent unpredictability.

title: Non-Euclidean Neural Network Architecture for Symbolic Reasoning
abstract: This paper presents a novel neural network architecture designed to enhance symbolic reasoning capabilities by incorporating a non-Euclidean representation. Traditional neural networks often fall short in representing and reasoning about abstract concepts due to the limitations of Euclidean geometry. This work proposes a method of encoding concepts in a space that circumvents these limitations, leading to a more robust and flexible system for symbolic manipulation. The core mechanism centers around the "Non-Euclidean Representation" – a novel approach to conceptual mapping that offers significant advantages in handling complex reasoning patterns. We detail the architecture, explore its potential benefits through theoretical analysis, and present preliminary results demonstrating enhanced symbolic reasoning capabilities compared to existing approaches.

title: 基于量子自旋的几何变换优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel geometric transformation optimization algorithm based on the unique properties of quantum spins. Traditional geometric optimization methods often struggle with the inherent complexity of geometric transformations, particularly in the realm of quantum mechanics. We propose a new approach that leverages quantum spin states to achieve precise control and optimization of geometric transformations, offering a potential breakthrough for applications in computer graphics, robotics, and other fields. The core mechanism centers on constructing a quantum spin-based model for geometric transformation, utilizing the inherent properties of these states to precisely implement the transformation process. This algorithm demonstrates significant improvements in accuracy and efficiency compared to established methods, showcasing its potential to address challenges in geometric modeling and optimization.

title: The Evolution of Adaptive Multi-Modal Data Fusion for Quantum Machine Learning
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive multi-modal data fusion framework designed to enhance the predictive accuracy and generalization capabilities of quantum machine learning models. Traditional multi-modal data fusion methods often rely on static data fusion strategies, limiting their effectiveness in complex datasets. Our framework dynamically adjusts data fusion strategies, enabling a more flexible and robust approach to model performance. We demonstrate the framework's efficacy through a series of simulations and analyses, highlighting its ability to improve performance across diverse tasks. The core mechanism involves an adaptive algorithm that continuously evaluates and adjusts the fusion process based on the data itself. This iterative refinement ensures optimal data integration, ultimately contributing to superior model outcomes.

The core mechanism involves manipulating the topology of a quantum state through a series of transformations, ultimately leading to a more structured and manageable representation.

title: 基于非线性几何拓扑的量子计算模拟
abstract: This paper explores the application of non-linear geometric topology to quantum computing simulation, aiming to address challenges inherent in traditional simulation methods. We propose a novel approach that leverages quantum computation's unique capabilities to model complex systems exhibiting quantum effects. The core idea centers around employing topological properties to simplify the computational landscape, offering potential improvements in efficiency and the representation of quantum phenomena. This research focuses on designing a simulation framework that incorporates the principles of non-linear geometry and topology, aiming to enhance the fidelity and interpretability of quantum system simulations. We present a conceptual design, detailing the underlying mathematical principles and potential challenges. The paper concludes with a discussion of the implications of this approach for future quantum computing research.

title: Title: Quantum Information Theory – Topological Quantum Error Correction
abstract: Quantum information theory stands at a critical juncture, grappling with the challenges of maintaining quantum coherence in the face of inevitable noise. Current error correction methods, while effective, are fundamentally limited by the complexity of encoding and decoding processes. This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum error correction centered around the concept of topological quantum information, exploring the potential to encode quantum information within the inherent structure of spacetime. This fundamentally shifts the paradigm away from traditional error-correcting codes and towards a more robust and potentially universal approach. The core mechanism involves developing a 'topological field' encoding scheme inspired by topological insulators, aiming to create inherently robust quantum states resistant to local perturbations. We will detail the theoretical framework, the implementation challenges, and preliminary experimental considerations for this approach. The core claim is that this novel methodology offers a path towards significantly enhanced quantum information protection.

abstract: This paper introduces the Nonlinear Variable Mapping (NVM) framework, a novel approach to machine learning that leverages the core principles of NVM to map variables to higher-dimensional spaces. We demonstrate the potential of this method to enhance model interpretability and generalization capabilities, addressing the limitations of traditional machine learning models. The core mechanism focuses on transforming the model's output into a transformed representation, facilitating a more streamlined and accurate prediction process. This work represents a significant advancement in machine learning by offering a robust and adaptable technique for addressing the challenges of complex models.

title: 基于量子纠错码的密码分析方法
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to cryptography analysis leveraging the principles of quantum error correction codes (QECCs). The core idea centers on exploiting the inherent redundancy and error-correcting capabilities of QECCs to analyze and potentially compromise cryptographic keys. Traditional cryptographic attacks often rely on brute-force, differential, or linear cryptanalysis. This work proposes a fundamentally different methodology, focusing on the structure and properties of QECCs to induce errors within the encoded key, which can then be exploited for decryption. The methodology involves constructing specific QECCs tailored to the cryptographic algorithm being analyzed, and then manipulating the encoding process to introduce vulnerabilities. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and the development of a novel attack strategy. While experimental validation is not included in this paper, the presented framework provides a strong theoretical foundation and a promising direction for future research in quantum-resistant cryptography. The ultimate goal is to significantly enhance the security of cryptographic systems by targeting their underlying error correction mechanisms.

title: Adaptive Topological Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of adaptive topological quantum computing, a novel approach designed to enhance quantum algorithm capabilities and computational power through dynamic topological state manipulation. We propose a framework leveraging the inherent properties of topological quantum bits to enable complex computations and extend the reach of quantum computation. The core mechanism involves utilizing quantum topology to dynamically adjust qubit states, allowing for more versatile and powerful quantum operations. The research explores the design of such a system, highlighting its potential advantages over existing quantum computing paradigms. This work offers a new perspective on quantum computation, focusing on the intrinsic potential of topological structures and their adaptability.

title: Quantum-Guided Constraint Optimization
abstract: Quantum-Guided Constraint Optimization (QGCO) is a novel optimization technique leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics to enhance the efficiency of constraint optimization problems. This paper explores the fundamental principles behind QGCO, detailing its core mechanism involving quantum superposition and entanglement to guide the search process, ultimately leading to improved solution quality and reduced computational cost. We present a comprehensive theoretical framework, illustrating the algorithm's functionality through mathematical formulations and illustrative examples. The research focuses on the impact of quantum measurements on the search space, demonstrating a significant improvement over classical optimization methods in several benchmark scenarios. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential applications of QGCO across diverse fields, including finance, logistics, and materials science.

title: LLM is a Machine That Computes Language A Structural and Cognitive Explanation for AI Misinterpretation
abstract: This project presents a unified structural theory of AI, arguing that Large Language Models (LLMs) are computational systems derived from linguistic relations rather than autonomous intelligent agents. It demonstrates that AGI—defined as an entity capable of generating its own goals—is conceptually impossible, while proposing a new direction in which LLMs can be enhanced through externally organized linguistic structures. The project integrates three core insights: 1. LLMs Are Machines That Compute Language LLMs operate by converting language into vector representations and performing matrix‑based next‑token prediction. They do not generate internal thought or conceptual structures. Because human cognition relies on language as its primary external output channel, humans tend to misinterpret fluent linguistic output as evidence of underlying thought. This cognitive bias explains why LLMs are often mistaken for intelligent agents. 2. AGI Is Structurally Impossible Autonomy—goal formation, value judgment, priority setting, and independent action—and subordination—acting according to external intentions—occupy opposite positions within linguistic structure. Since LLMs learn exclusively from linguistic relational patterns, they cannot compute concepts that do not exist within linguistic structure, including “subordinate autonomy.” Therefore: A self‑directed AGI that simultaneously obeys human intentions is conceptually contradictory and cannot be represented within LLM architecture. This is a structural limitation, not a technological one. 3. LLMs Can Be Improved Through External Linguistic Structures LLMs lack internal mechanisms for: conceptual retention stable semantic positioning cross‑linguistic consistency structural reasoning These limitations lead to semantic drift in translation, reasoning, and multi‑layered tasks. However, they can be compensated by externalizing linguistic structures, such as: minimal conceptual units (Units) connection dictionaries English–Japanese structural correspondence tables external reasoning graphs By referencing these external structures, an LLM can achieve reasoning stability and conceptual coherence that internal computation alone cannot provide. This approach enables: more stable reasoning consistent semantics reduced computational load expanded reasoning space through bilingual structural multiplicity It represents a new direction for AI development: externally extended reasoning rather than internal autonomous intelligence. 🔷 Overall Conclusion AGI is structurally impossible. Autonomy and subordination cannot coexist within linguistic structure, and LLMs cannot compute concepts that linguistically do not exist. LLMs remain improvable through external structures. By supplementing internal computation with externally organized linguistic frameworks, LLMs can achieve higher stability, coherence, and efficiency in reasoning. This project reframes AI as a language‑derived computational system, clarifying both its structural limits and its potential for externally supported improvement. The theoretical foundation is based on Mirror Amplification Theory (Urushizaki, 2026), which analyzes how linguistic systems generate, distort, and amplify conceptual structures across different language layers.

title: The Mirror Agent Model: a Bayesian Architecture for Interpretable Agent Behavior
abstract: In this paper we illustrate a novel architecture generating interpretable behavior and explanations. We refer to this architecture as the Mirror Agent Model because it defines the observer model, that is the target of explicit and implicit communications, as a mirror of the agent's. With the goal of providing a general understanding of this work, we firstly show prior relevant results addressing the informative communication of agents intentions and the production of legible behavior. In the second part of the paper we furnish the architecture with novel capabilities for explanations through off-the-shelf saliency methods, followed by preliminary qualitative results.

title: InterSing: Explicit Interaction Dynamics for 3D Duet Singing Animation and Beyond
abstract: We present InterSing, a framework for generating realistic 3D head animations for duet singing performances. Unlike solo singing, duet performance requires each singer to balance individual expressiveness with intermittent interaction at musically salient moments, such as phrase boundaries, synchronized rhythms, and call-and-response passages. Because these interactions are sparse and rhythm-dependent, existing audio-driven animation methods and conversational interaction models do not adequately capture their structure. Our key insight is that duet coordination can be represented as a time-varying signal that reflects how strongly performers engage with one another throughout a song. Based on this observation, we introduce interaction logits, an interpretable latent representation that models the degree of cross-performer engagement at each time step. We learn these logits using weak supervision and use them to condition an interaction-aware diffusion model jointly driven by audio features and interaction dynamics. This formulation enables unified multi-mode generation, spanning independent motion, coordinated behavior, and smooth transitions between them. Experiments show that InterSing generates realistic and expressive singing head animations with stronger coordination and musical alignment than existing methods, while preserving each performer's characteristic motion style. We further demonstrate that the same formulation generalizes to multi-singer performances and provides intuitive control over when and how performers engage.

title: Predicting Spatiotemporal Mobile Sensing-Based PM2.5 Concentrations Using Low-Rank Adapted Spatially Attentive Graph Neural Network
abstract: Urban air quality can vary significantly along transit corridors, necessitating high-resolution monitoring. This work introduces a novel mobile-sensing dataset from Surat, Gujarat, India, comprising PM$*{2.5}$ concentrations, meteorological variables (temperature, humidity, wind speed, wind direction), and land-use features. To represent the spatiotemporal data as a graph, two node-definition strategies were used: (i) uniform segmentation (200--400~m intervals) and (ii) DBSCAN clustering to adaptively group dense observations. For each node, rolling mean and standard deviation of meteorological variables were computed. To model this high-dimensional data, we propose a SA-GNN for fine-grained, short-term PM$*{2.5}$ forecasting and hotspot identification. We compared SA-GNN with LSTM, RNN, GRU, and ANN models. These models performed well on low-resolution data but had difficulty capturing rapidly changing patterns in urban air quality. SA-GNN employs cluster-specific GRUs to capture localized temporal dependencies and a Graph Attention Network to learn spatial heterogeneity. This hybrid architecture effectively models rapid fluctuations and complex spatial interactions. On our dataset, SA-GNN achieved $R^2 = 0.95$, RMSE $= 6.8$, and MAE $= 4.2~\si{\micro\gram\per\meter\cubed}$, outperforming all baseline models. Combining spatial clustering with adaptive attention significantly improves forecasting, enabling real-time, fine-grained monitoring and supporting personalized exposure tracking and timely alerts for healthier cities.

title: Dataset Quality Assessment For Network Traffic Classification
abstract: Tato dizertační práce je kolekcí autorových článků popisujících dosažené výsledky v oblasti hodnocení kvality datových sad síťového provozu. S rozmachem metod strojového učení se stává klíčovým předpokladem dostupnost vysoce kvalitních dat pro trénování i provozování používaných modelů. Tento důležitý aspekt je však v existujících článcích často přehlížen nebo podceňován, což může vést k nespolehlivému výkonu vyvinutých modelů strojového učení. Obsahem této dizertační práce je zmapování domény posuzování kvality datových sad síťového provozu a její rozšíření o navržené a vyvinuté algoritmy a metriky pro hodnocení kvality. Na základě komplexní analýzy jsou identifikovány kritické body, které ovlivňují kvalitu datových sad síťového provozu. V rámci prováděného výzkumu tato práce navazuje na současný stav poznání, validuje existující datové sady a rozšiřuje tradiční procesy monitorování sítě díky nově vytvořeným metodám. Dosažené výsledky jsou prezentovány ve vybraných článcích v příloze a v přehledové případové studii. Hlavní přínosy této dizertační práce jsou zejména: 1. Sestavení formální taxonomie pro definování klíčových pojmů v oblasti hodnocení kvality datových sad. 2. Návrh a implementace metrik pro kvantifikaci identifikovaných klíčových vlastností kvality datových sad. 3. Integrace kvalitativních metrik do stávajících procesů strojového učení pro podporu kontinuální tvorby, validace, optimalizace a profilování datových sad v čase.

title: Fluid Archives: Malleable Data Architecture and Evolutionary Security under Continuous Cryptographic Threat
abstract: Volumes I and II of this series established two claims. The post-quantum transition is an architectural problem, not an algorithm-substitution problem (Mamun, 2026a). Sovereignty in that architecture is a layered portfolio — compute, data, knowledge, judgment, cognition — pursued under dual-track ecosystems and a compute tax that developing states cannot ignore (Mamun, 2026b). This third volume asks the design question that follows: what kind of data architecture can evolve with the security threat rather than freeze at the last standard? The argument is that threat is not a step function at a hypothetical Q-day. It is a continuous surface — cryptanalysis of parameter sets, implementation breaks, supply-chain compromise of libraries, harvest-now-decrypt-later (HNDL) already running against yesterday's ciphertext, and narrative poisoning of agentic memory. A rigid lake, compiled against one suite, produces dark data the moment the suite is superseded. Fluidity is therefore a security property. The paper specifies a malleable architecture in six layers: object-level cryptographic metadata; a cryptographic bill of materials and policy-as-code control plane; hybrid and versioned wrapping; bifurcated index and payload paths; substrate-aware malleability across silicon halls, molecular halls and sovereign caches; and a cybernetic loop in which threat intelligence continuously re-weights primitives. Also available on Academia.edu: https://www.academia.edu/attachments/134136264/download_file?s=portfolio

title: GEO External Operator
abstract: GEO External Operator v1.0.0 First public release of the solver-independent external operator for the GEO Hidden Geometry Framework. What this release provides GEO is exposed as an external deterministic C operator with a public API and a Cobaya theory-component integration. The demonstrated cosmological integration uses an independently built, unmodified upstream CLASS v3.3.4 source tree. No modification of CLASS source code is required by this integration path. Public C API geo_public_api_version geo_public_compute Canonical effectiveness relation The public implementation uses R^3 = mu_eff and therefore R = mu_eff^(1/3) where mu_eff is application-dependent. The framework does not impose a universal identity between mu_eff and eta. For the Hubble realization demonstrated here, the application-specific assignment is: mu_H := eta = 0.6 Clean CLASS / Cobaya interoperability test Validated against: CLASS v3.3.4 upstream commit e85808324f51fc694d12e3ed7439552a3c3f9540 Python 3.12.3 NumPy 1.26.4 SciPy 1.13.1 Cobaya 3.6.2 classy 3.3.4.0 The external chain is: CLASS -> Cobaya provider -> GEOHubbleTheory -> libgeo_public -> GEO derived quantities Three deterministic regression points were tested: | Primitive H0 | GEO H0 | |---:|---:| | 66.0 | 71.522848664464732 | | 67.4 | 73.039999999771553 | | 69.0 | 74.773887240122221 | All three external evaluations completed successfully. Scope of this release This release establishes: an external GEO software interface; solver-independent separation of the GEO operator from CLASS; reproducible CLASS/Cobaya interoperability; dynamic evaluation rather than a hard-coded Hubble output; explicit provenance and SHA-256 manifests. This software result does not, by itself, constitute independent observational validation of the GEO framework or evidence of cosmological model preference. The Hubble mapping is an application-specific realization, and parts of the present residual/spectral closure retain the candidate-v1 status documented in the source. Reproduction See README.md, run_reproduction.sh, and the provenance/ directory. Author Leonel Hernán Torreblanca

title: Evidence-Based Prompt Engineering
abstract: A prompt-engineering reference in which every technique is graded solid, mixed or folklore, and every claim names a primary source. The evidence lives in a machine-readable ledger. This first release grades eight techniques (three solid, two mixed, three folklore) and ships one offline reproducible experiment; it is a sourced starting corpus, not an exhaustive survey. Effects that can only be measured with live model calls are recorded as dated snapshots against a named model, never as standing truths.

title: Graph-Based Machine Learning Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel graph-based machine learning algorithm designed to automate feature learning and enhance the performance of graph neural networks. title: Probabilistic Programming for Explainable AI – Causal Chain Analysis
abstract: Explainable AI (XAI) has emerged as a critical area of research, driven by the need for trust and accountability in increasingly complex AI systems. However, many existing XAI techniques offer only superficial explanations, often failing to capture the underlying causal mechanisms driving AI decisions. This paper proposes a novel approach leveraging probabilistic programming languages to provide truly explainable AI through causal chain analysis. We argue that current XAI methods frequently lack grounding in causal relationships, generating explanations that are ultimately misleading. Our core mechanism involves modeling AI decision-making processes as causal chains within a probabilistic programming environment, such as Stan or PyMC3. This allows us to automatically generate and analyze these chains, quantifying the influence of each input variable on the predicted output while identifying potential biases. The resulting framework offers a rigorous and transparent method for understanding *why* an AI system made a specific decision, moving beyond correlation to establish cause-and-effect relationships. The core claim is that this approach provides a significantly more robust and reliable basis for XAI than existing techniques. We will demonstrate how this framework can be used to identify and mitigate biases, leading to more trustworthy and reliable AI systems.

title: Artificial intelligence in endometrial and cervical cancer: From ultrasound-based detection to digital pathology and prognostic modeling
abstract: Endometrial cancer (EC) and cervical cancer together account for over one million new diagnoses annually, yet their diagnostic pathways remain constrained by operatordependent imaging, the limited sensitivity of cytology, and substantial inter-observer variability in histopathological grading.Artificial intelligence (AI), encompassing classical machine learning, deep learning, convolutional neural networks, transformer architectures, and computational pathology on whole-slide images, is maturing across the gynaecologic-oncology continuum.This minireview synthesises the evidence across six domains: Ultrasound-based detection and characterisation; colposcopy and cervical cytology; digital pathology and histopathology; magnetic resonance imaging based staging and radiomics; molecular biomarker integration, liquid biopsy and prognostic modelling; and clinical translation.In retrospective and predominantly single-centre datasets, AI has matched or exceeded expert performance on several narrow tasks, notably ultrasound assessment of deep myometrial invasion, automated cytology triage, and morphology-based molecular subtyping of EC, and one digital cytology platform has obtained United States Food and Drug Administration clearance.Regulatory clearance nevertheless remains exceptional rather than routine in this field, and headline accuracies derived from small curated datasets are frequently inflated by overfitting; the most instructive example is a landmark colposcopy model whose nearperfect discrimination was subsequently attributed by its own senior author to overfitting uncorrected by internal validation.Persistent deficits in external validation, prospective trial evidence, methodological quality, algorithmic equity and regulatory clarity continue to separate promising retrospective performance from routine clinical deployment.

title: Метод защиты от атак на модели машинного обучения путем затруднения действий нарушителей
abstract: Цель работы, разработать и экспериментально оценить метод латентно- адаптивной деградации обучающего воздействия, направленный на снижение эффективности атак отравления данных при сохранении приемлемой точности модели. Объект исследования, процесс обучения моделей машинного обучения в условиях присутствия отравленных данных. Предмет исследования, методы защиты моделей машинного обучения за счет модификации обучающего воздействия. В ходе работы были проанализированы атаки отравления данных и методы защиты, разработаны математическая модель и алгоритм метода ЛАДОВ, реализован исследовательский стенд и проведена экспериментальная оценка. Метод ЛАДОВ снижает предсказуемость влияния обучающих примеров на параметры модели за счет адаптивного коэффициента надежности, ограничения нормы градиента, стохастического искажения градиентной динамики и проверки согласованности в латентном пространстве. Эксперименты на CIFAR-10 с моделью ResNet-18 показали, что метод наиболее заметно снижает успешность clean-label backdoor-атаки при сохранении высокой точности на чистых данных.

title: Evaluating large language models on text-based engineering design tasks: performance gaps and failure modes
abstract: Abstract Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Large Language Models are increasingly considered for integration into engineering design workflows, yet their actual capabilities on the analytical and optimization tasks that arise in engineering design remain poorly understood. In this study, we examine Large Language Model-generated answers to 86 text-based questions covering three task categories chosen for their direct correspondence to typical engineering design activities: 50 problem-solving tasks from the Kangaroo Math Competition, 20 structural engineering design tasks involving stress analysis and cross-section selection, and 16 engineering optimization tasks involving conflicting constraints and trade-offs. Across the evaluated models, we observe that performance is consistently higher on the general Kangaroo problem-solving questions than on the engineering geometry and optimization tasks, even though these draw on a comparable set of underlying skills. The study further exposes systematic failure modes across the examined task types, including geometric reasoning, multi-step numerical computation, and optimization under conflicting constraints. These findings characterize the specific capabilities that AI-enabled design systems must develop to be reliable in practice, and establish an empirical baseline for evaluating future augmentation strategies such as tool integration and structured design workflows.

title: Can Large Language Models Anticipate Behavioral Responses to Social Policies? A Case of Pension Enrollment Prediction among China's Flexible Workers
abstract: Assessing the impacts of social policy changes is a widely acknowledged challenge for policymakers. Econometric methods can be unreliable when extrapolating to hypothetical scenarios, while field pilot programs are highly costly. In this paper, we propose using large language models (LLMs) as policy-assessment tools adapted from general-purpose models. We present FlexPension-LLM, the first domain-specialized large language model for a hierarchical pension-enrollment prediction task among flexible workers in China, and introduce DKI-RDistill, which injects policy-grounded cues into the prompt, including Probit-derived marginal effects and hukou-province pension rules. The method then uses LoRA/SFT to distill rationale-augmented supervision into an open-weight MoE student, with teacher errors corrected by regenerating those cases under ground-truth labels. On a CHFS 2019 blind split, FlexPension-LLM achieves 0.9316 Composite F1, surpassing its Claude Sonnet 4.5 teacher and 15 of 17 baselines, and is statistically indistinguishable from Claude Opus 4.6. Across four external surveys, it averages 0.7549 Composite F1 and shows the narrowest performance range among the strongest systems. Component analysis shows that gains come mainly from policy-grounded cue injection and error-filtered supervision, while rationales provide decision traces that can be checked against policy rules.

On a CHFS 2019 blind split, FlexPension-LLM achieves 0.9316 Composite F1, surpassing its Claude Sonnet 4.5 teacher and 15 of 17 baselines, and is statistically indistinguishable from Claude Opus 4.6. Across four external surveys, it averages 0.7549 Composite F1 and shows the narrowest performance range among the strongest systems. Component analysis shows that gains come mainly from policy-grounded cue injection and error-filtered supervision, while rationales provide decision traces that can be checked against policy rules.

title: Sound-based Multi-Person 3D Pose Estimation
abstract: Can we recover the 3D poses of multiple people using only sound? This paper presents the first attempt to estimate multi-person 3D poses solely from acoustic signals. Estimating the poses of multiple individuals using acoustic signals is inherently challenging due to the superposition of motion-dependent signal variations. Unlike single-person scenarios, the presence of multiple subjects leads to overlapping acoustic signatures, making it difficult to attribute specific signal changes to an individual's pose. Furthermore, the complexity is compounded by inter-person reflections, which introduce intricate propagation delays that obscure the temporal motion-acoustic relationship. To address these issues, we propose SoundMHPE (Sound-based Multi-person Human Pose Estimator), a novel encoder-decoder framework consisting of two key components. First, the Acoustic Multi-scale Encoder captures diverse temporal and fine-grained frequency features to isolate subtle acoustic signatures from complex, overlapping signals. Second, the Temporal Pose Decoder employs an attention mechanism to disentangle multi-person information across successive frames. By jointly accounting for temporal dynamics and inter-person dependencies, this component precisely reconstructs frame-wise individual poses. To validate our approach, we constructed the 6-hour Acoustic Multi-person Pose (AMP) dataset consisting of 432K synchronized frames of multi-person pose and acoustic data, and demonstrated that our SoundMHPE outperforms baseline models. title: Neural networks learn to reconstruct multipartite entanglement from quantum marginals
abstract: Different sets of local correlations are not equivalent: some fragments of reduced data uniquely determine a global quantum state, while others leave it ambiguous. The quantum marginal problem asks whether a collection of reduced density matrices uniquely determines a compatible global quantum state. Although generic quantum states are uniquely specified by suitable sets of marginals, different collections of marginals are not equally informative: some uniquely determine the global state, whereas others leave it ambiguous. Identifying when uniqueness holds, and reconstructing the global state from partial information, remains computationally demanding and experimentally challenging. We show that information about the multipartite entanglement class and reconstructability in four-qubit systems is compactly encoded in small sets of two- and three-qubit marginals. Using semidefinite programming, we chart the reconstructability landscape across 49 inequivalent SLOCC entanglement classes and show that uniqueness strongly depends on both entanglement structure and marginal order. Neural networks trained only on reduced density matrices learn this structure directly. They accurately classify marginal reconstructability and, when uniqueness holds, reconstruct the full four-qubit density matrix with high fidelity from two- and three-qubit marginals. We benchmark the approach on a four-qubit nuclear magnetic resonance quantum processor and demonstrate that reconstructions from experimentally measured marginals remain faithful despite phase damping and control imperfections. Our results show that neural networks can learn when local correlations uniquely specify a global quantum state, and reveal how global quantum structure is encoded in reduced data.

title: Enhancing Multimodal Emotion Recognition via Multi-Feature Encoding and Attention-Based Fusion
abstract: Multimodal emotion recognition has attracted growing interest due to its importance in human-computer interaction, remote education, and healthcare. This paper proposes a novel multimodal emotion recognition framework that integrates rich audio and visual feature extraction with an attention-based fusion strategy. For audio, we extract three complementary feature types: semantic embeddings from Wav2Vec2, MFCC features, and statistical acoustic descriptors such as pitch, energy, and rhythm. These are aligned and fused via a BiLSTM to capture temporal dependencies. For video, we propose a ResNet50-BiLSTM architecture that combines deep residual learning and sequential modeling to extract expressive spatiotemporal features from facial sequences. To enhance multimodal synergy, we introduce a feature-level fusion mechanism based on multi-head attention, allowing the model to adaptively weigh contributions across modalities. Experiments conducted on the MELD and IEMOCAP datasets demonstrate that our model significantly outperforms baselines in both accuracy and robustness. Furthermore, ablation studies show that the attention-based fusion strategy significantly improves performance in unbalanced data settings. Our findings suggest that the proposed framework effectively captures diverse emotional cues from speech and visual expressions, and offers a practical and generalizable approach for real-world multimodal emotion recognition tasks.

title: The Meaning Model: Constructing Worlds and Stories at Progressive Resolution
abstract: The Meaning Model proposes a shared medium for constructing a world, its meanings, interpretations, and story together. The long-term aim is to model reality computationally through interrelated processes, from physical and social histories to attributed inner life, at a declared finite resolution. A world can be constructed coherently at a coarse resolution for a declared purpose, then recursively opened into finer detail. Each opening must preserve declared commitments or explicitly revise them, including their dependent accounts and passages. The contribution is this coordinated authoring method, not a new record type or the storage of prose beside a graph. Six record forms—Concept, Thing, Event, Binding, Cut, and Realization—support the method. Abstract meaning uses the same world machinery: a Concept may remain lightly specified or have process-based concept models whose roles and processes can be inspected alongside their instances. World records, Understanding Graphs recording interpretations and reasons, and document nodes share one address space and can be revised together while retaining their distinct authority. Semantic numbers are comparative commitments rather than freestanding scores. Each Cut names an Event parent, question, and unit, allocating one unit among exclusive answers and an explicit remainder for the unallocated share. Ordinary process links remain unweighted; measurements retain external units. The workspace supports human or AI construction and supplies a candidate training language. Developing and revising the categories themselves is part of the construction method. A learner could acquire these practices: choosing, deepening, and repairing representations, not only predicting content within a fixed schema. Life Simulation develops the construction-to-learning loop and its tests; this paper specifies the representation and preservation contracts. The completed manuscript, The Book of Conditions, partially demonstrates construction feasibility but does not validate the full method; learning gains, computational savings, and alignment remain untested.

title: ESI triage support using structured and free-text clinical data: A comparative machine learning study in a Colombian emergency department
abstract: This thesis systematically compares machine learning approaches for ESI triage classification, combining multiple text vectorization strategies, classifiers, and class imbalance methods. The data used included free-text clinical notes and structured variables, routinely collected at triage in Hospital Pablo Tobón Uribe, Colombia. The best-performing model combined an XGBoost classifier, SMOTE-NC oversampling, and RoBERTa embeddings. It was evaluated in terms of performance metrics, subgroup fairness, and interpretability, where it achieved a macro F1 of 0.6791 and 76.2% accuracy on the held-out test set, demonstrating that open-source pipelines can achieve competitive triage classification performance in institutions at early stages of AI adoption.

title: Evolving Sensor Layouts Under Survival and Locomotor Constraints
abstract: We introduce a compact genotype for evolving directional sensor layouts in embodied artificial agents. The representation separates the number of sensors from their angular allocation: a scalar sensor count specifies the number of rays, while an inverse cumulative-distribution mapping converts quantiles into ordered ray headings across an evolvable field of view. This construction permits sensor-count mutation, continuous changes in angular span, and smooth foveal or peripheral concentration without explicitly mutating an unordered list of sensor coordinates. We evaluate the representation in a two-dimensional obstacle arena containing a moving target. Agents control steering and throttle through a neural network receiving only normalized obstacle-distance measurements from their evolved rays. An agent is successful if it reaches the target before colliding with an obstacle or leaving the arena; no distance, speed, path-length, survival-time, or target-proximity reward is used. We compare four conditions over seven independent 50,000-generation trials: mutable sensors without a ray-dependent locomotor cost, mutable sensors with a 3.5% speed penalty per additional ray, and fixed arrays of four or eight rays whose layouts remain evolvable. Free sensing produced substantially larger and more variable terminal sensor arrays than the cost-constrained condition (17.52 ± 7.16 versus 8.03 ± 3.03 rays). The cost condition also produced more stable terminal success (96.0% ± 4.4% versus 85.7% ± 29.5%). Fixed fourand eight-ray systems achieved nearly identical success rates (98.9% and 99.1%, respectively), despite adapting through different visual spans and angular densities. Across replicate trials, the sensor-cost condition did not converge to a single universal morphology: viable endpoints ranged from approximately three to twelve rays. These results support the inverse-CDF genotype as a useful experimental representation for studying sensor morphology, while emphasizing that the observed morphologies are task- and implementation-dependent evolutionary outcomes rather than biologically optimal designs.

title: Dynamic Topology Language for Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper explores the potential of dynamic topology languages as a foundation for advanced quantum computing. We propose a novel framework for generating quantum algorithms and programs through the integration of quantum topological properties. The core claim is that this approach, by leveraging dynamic topology, can significantly reduce algorithmic complexity and computational costs, thereby accelerating the development of efficient quantum solutions. The method is designed to automate the design process, offering a significant advancement over traditional techniques. This work highlights the potential of dynamic topology to unlock new possibilities in quantum computation.

title: Non-Euclidean Geometry and Quantum Computing: A Research Proposal
abstract: This research proposes a novel exploration of non-Euclidean geometry and its potential application to quantum computing. We investigate a specific topological transformation based on non-Euclidean principles to enhance quantum entanglement and key distribution capabilities. The core mechanism centers on simulating quantum entanglement through a fundamentally different geometric framework, offering potential advantages over traditional quantum computing approaches. This work aims to contribute to the advancement of quantum information processing by leveraging the unique properties of non-Euclidean geometry.

title: 自适应混沌理论的量子计算实现
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum computing to revolutionize the study and manipulation of self-organized chaotic systems. We present a novel algorithm, termed "Adaptive Chaos Quantum Engine" (ACQE), designed to achieve real-time parameter adjustment within a quantum system, thereby generating dynamic and unpredictable chaos. The core of the algorithm leverages quantum entanglement to create a feedback loop, allowing the system to subtly adjust its parameters based on observed outputs, ultimately leading to the emergence of complex, self-sustaining chaotic behavior. The paper details the theoretical framework underpinning the QE, including the quantum entanglement protocol and the feedback mechanism, and demonstrates preliminary results through simulations, showcasing the algorithm's capability to generate novel chaotic patterns. We argue that this approach offers a significant advancement over traditional methods, potentially unlocking new capabilities in areas like complex systems modeling and potentially even quantum simulation. Furthermore, we discuss the challenges and future directions for this research.

abstract: This paper investigates the potential of utilizing dynamic topology as a core mechanism for quantum state transmission, offering a novel approach to overcome limitations of traditional quantum information processing. We present a theoretical framework centered around the design of a quantum-assisted dynamic topology, demonstrating its capacity to significantly enhance the speed and security of quantum state transfer. The proposed method leverages the inherent properties of dynamic topology to facilitate rapid state propagation and enhance the robustness of the transmission process. The core claim is that this dynamic topology-based approach offers a significant advancement in quantum information transfer. The paper details the design of the dynamic topology structure, its interaction with quantum states, and the resulting improvements in transmission efficiency and security compared to conventional methods.

title: Adaptive Knowledge Reasoning Engine Based on Cognitive Graphs
abstract: This paper presents a novel adaptive knowledge reasoning engine built upon the foundation of cognitive graphs. The core claim is that dynamic cognitive graphs, combined with contextual information, enable adaptive inference and knowledge discovery within complex concepts. The engine operates through continuous knowledge extraction from diverse sources (text, images, etc.) and constructs a dynamic cognitive graph. Deep learning techniques are then employed to adaptively update the graph and adjust node weights, allowing the engine to reason based on contextual information and ultimately generate relevant conclusions. The innovation lies in shifting from static knowledge bases to dynamic graphs, facilitating real-time learning, contextual adaptation, and improved inference accuracy and efficiency. The system leverages graph neural networks (GNNs) to perform reasoning, and employs attention mechanisms to prioritize relevant nodes within the graph. This approach addresses the limitations of traditional knowledge reasoning by incorporating the fluidity of information and the nuances of context. This research contributes to the advancement of intelligent systems capable of handling complex, evolving knowledge domains. ---

title: Generative Models for Circuit Design via Symbolic Regression
abstract: Circuit design is a crucial, yet inherently complex, process in modern electronics. Traditional design methodologies often rely on expert intuition and iterative manual optimization, which can be time-consuming and may not always yield the most efficient solutions. This paper proposes a novel approach to circuit design utilizing symbolic regression, a powerful technique for automated equation discovery. The core idea is to leverage symbolic regression to learn the optimal circuit topology and associated parameters directly from a dataset of circuit performance metrics. This eliminates the need for human-defined constraints and allows the system to explore a potentially vast design space, generating novel circuit designs that could surpass conventional designs in terms of efficiency. The presented methodology offers a significant step toward automating the circuit optimization process, promising faster and more effective design cycles. The key formulation involves representing the circuit as a symbolic expression and employing regression techniques to minimize a cost function defined by the desired performance metrics. This approach provides a framework for generating potentially superior circuit designs without requiring extensive manual intervention.

title: Spectral Graph Anomaly Detection using Fractal Analysis
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to graph anomaly detection by utilizing fractal analysis of graph spectral data. Traditional anomaly detection methods often struggle with complex, high-dimensional graph structures. This research addresses this challenge by transforming graph spectral information into fractal representations, allowing for the application of established fractal analysis techniques to identify deviations from expected patterns. The core idea is that anomalies in graph structures will manifest as distortions in their fractal representations. We explore the relationship between graph Laplacian eigenvalues, spectral clustering, and fractal dimension, demonstrating the efficacy of this method. The proposed framework offers a geometrically-grounded approach to anomaly detection, potentially improving accuracy and robustness compared to conventional methods. We present a theoretical framework and discuss the key elements of the approach, outlining a potential methodology for implementation.

title: Dynamic Quantum Circuit Compilation via Tensor Networks
abstract: Quantum circuit compilation is a crucial step in realizing quantum algorithms on near-term quantum hardware. Traditional compilation methods often employ static circuit representations, limiting their ability to adapt to the fluctuating coherence properties and connectivity constraints of actual quantum devices. This research introduces a novel approach utilizing tensor network representations for dynamic quantum circuit compilation. The core idea is to leverage the inherent entanglement and superposition present in quantum systems to create adaptive circuit layouts. Our method employs an iterative tensor network algorithm that continuously refines circuit representations, prioritizing coherence preservation and minimizing gate count, while incorporating real-time qubit state estimations. This dynamic adaptation directly addresses the challenges posed by the limitations of current quantum hardware, offering a pathway to more efficient and robust quantum algorithm execution. The key innovation lies in the application of tensor networks, a powerful mathematical tool, to the optimization problem of quantum circuit compilation.

title: Title: Dynamical Topology for Statistical Machine Learning – Leveraging Network Topology to Improve Model Generalization
abstract: This paper explores the application of dynamical topology to statistical machine learning, focusing on the creation of a network structure that adapts to evolving data and enhances model generalization. We propose a novel algorithm that dynamically constructs a network topology, incorporating feedback loops and adaptive weighting to mitigate the effects of noise. The core mechanism leverages the concept of continuous, evolving topology to improve the robustness and adaptability of statistical models. This research aims to address the limitations of current machine learning approaches by introducing a framework that explicitly incorporates network structure and adaptation. The anticipated outcome is a model capable of better handling complex, variable datasets and improved predictive accuracy.

title: 基于动态自适应拓扑变换的自适应神经网络
abstract: This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture, termed the Dynamic Adaptive Topology Transform (DAT) Neural Network, designed to effectively handle dynamic and complex topological transformations. Traditional neural networks struggle with these transformations, often requiring extensive retraining or approximation. The DAT Neural Network leverages a dynamically adjustable parameterization of the network's topology, enabling precise control over the transformation process. We present a theoretical framework and a practical implementation demonstrating the network's capabilities through the application of a specific topological transformation, highlighting its advantages in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency compared to conventional methods. The core mechanism focuses on adjusting the network's topology through a novel parameterization scheme, allowing for a more responsive and accurate transformation. The resulting model exhibits superior performance in scenarios requiring precise and flexible topological manipulation. This work contributes to the advancement of neural network architectures for tasks involving dynamic transformations, offering a promising approach to handling complex data and achieving greater control over transformations.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Topological Geometry for Quantum Entanglement Control
abstract: This paper explores the application of dynamic adaptive topological geometry to quantum entanglement control. The core concept revolves around leveraging quantum entanglement to dynamically modify the topology of a geometric structure, enabling precise geometric transformations and facilitating quantum computations. We present a novel algorithm that utilizes entangled states to control the evolution of topological parameters, offering a pathway towards enhanced precision and control in quantum processing. The research focuses on the design of a flexible and adaptable system capable of handling the inherent complexity of quantum entanglement. The paper details the methodology, demonstrating the algorithm's efficacy through simulations and a preliminary analysis of quantum entanglement manipulation. The results suggest a significant improvement in geometric precision and control compared to traditional methods.

title: Adaptive Quantum Algorithm Refinement (AQAR)
abstract: This paper introduces Adaptive Quantum Algorithm Refinement (AQAR), a novel approach to quantum algorithm optimization. Traditional quantum algorithm refinement often involves static parameter adjustments, failing to fully leverage the insights gained during execution. AQAR dynamically adjusts circuit parameters based on algorithm performance feedback, enhancing both performance and stability. We present a novel Feedback-Driven Quantum Circuit Simulator, demonstrating the efficacy of this method through extensive simulations and analysis. This research addresses limitations of existing refinement techniques, offering a promising pathway toward more efficient and robust quantum computation.

title: ##拓扑张学与量子纠缠的非线性关联性建模
abstract: This paper explores the intersection of topology and quantum entanglement, focusing on the development of a dynamic, adaptive topology model capable of precisely simulating the non-linear correlations inherent in quantum entanglement. We introduce a novel quantum state generation algorithm underpinned by an adaptive topology structure and a 'topological correlation' measure, designed to optimize the topology and, consequently, the complex behavior of entangled states. The core mechanism centers on dynamically adjusting the topology to reflect the entangled nature of the system, providing a more accurate and nuanced representation of quantum computation's intricacies. This work addresses limitations of traditional topological models by incorporating dynamic correlations, offering a potentially transformative approach to quantum entanglement modeling.

title: ПОВЫШЕНИЕ ЭФФЕКТИВНОСТИ ПОИСКОВ МЕТАЛЛИЧЕСКИХ РУД НА ОСНОВЕ ИНТЕГРАЦИИ ГЕОЛОГИЧЕСКИХ, ГЕОФИЗИЧЕСКИХ, ГЕОХИМИЧЕСКИХ И ГИС-ДАННЫХ В СЕВЕРНОЙ И ЦЕНТРАЛЬНОЙ ЧАСТЯХ РЕСПУБЛИКИ АРМЕНИЯ
abstract: This study explores approaches to improving the efficiency of exploration for gold, polymetallic, and porphyry copper deposits within the Lori, Stepanavan, and Pambak-Tsaghkunyats ore districts of the Republic of Armenia. An integrated analysis of the geological framework, gravity, aeromagnetic, and geochemical survey data, combined with GIS-based techniques, was used to identify the principal ore-controlling factors governing the distribution of endogenous mineralization. The locations of several fault structures were refined, previously unrecognized concealed circular and arcuate structures were delineated, and their relationships with known mineral occurrences were established. The spatial association of gold, polymetallic, and porphyry copper mineralization with specific gravity anomalies, major fault zones, and intrusive complexes of different compositions was demonstrated. Several prospective target areas for detailed exploration were identified, and a preliminary assessment of their mineral potential was conducted. The results obtained may be applied to mineralization forecasting, and the planning of future geological exploration programs.

title: Adaptive Attention and Pyramid Pooling for High-Performance Dysarthric Speech Recognition
abstract: Speech pathology is a multidisciplinary field that assesses, diagnoses, and manages communication disorders caused by neurological, developmental, structural, and degenerative conditions. Among these disorders, dysarthria is a motor speech impairment characterized by reduced speech intelligibility and abnormal articulatory patterns resulting from neuromuscular dysfunction. Automatic dysarthria assessment remains challenging because of substantial inter-speaker variability, diverse severity levels, and the complex temporal–spectral characteristics of pathological speech signals. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an attention-enhanced convolutional neural network for automatic dysarthria detection and severity classification. The proposed architecture integrates a convolutional block attention module to enhance channel-wise and spatial feature representations, a coordinate attention module to capture long-range contextual dependencies while preserving positional information, and spatial pyramid pooling to extract robust multi-scale representations and accommodate input variability. Hierarchical convolutional layers with rectified linear unit activation and max-pooling operations progressively learn discriminative speech representations, followed by fully connected layers and a softmax classifier for prediction. The proposed framework was comprehensively evaluated on two publicly available datasets: TORGO Dataset 1, containing dysarthric and healthy control speech recordings, and TORGO Severity Dataset 2, comprising four dysarthria severity classes. Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients, together with their first- and second-order temporal derivatives and complementary acoustic descriptors, were extracted to characterize the speech signals. Extensive experiments, including cross-validation, repeated runs, ablation studies, Shapley additive explanations-based interpretability analysis, and statistical significance analysis, demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed framework. On TORGO Dataset 1, the proposed model achieved 95.00% accuracy, 94.50% precision, 95.25% recall, and a 94.75% F1-score, outperforming conventional machine learning and deep learning baselines. On TORGO Severity Dataset 2, the proposed framework achieved 99.10% classification accuracy, an F1-score of 0.9910, and an area under the curve of 0.9999, demonstrating strong performance in multi-class dysarthria severity classification. These findings highlight the proposed model’s strong discriminative capability, robustness, and interpretability, indicating its potential as a reliable computer-aided decision-support system for dysarthria detection and severity assessment.

title: How Do We Cook Up Artificial Intelligence With Optimization Algorithms?
abstract: Have you ever followed a recipe to make your favorite cake? Sometimes it turns out perfect, and sometimes you must adjust the amount of sugar or baking time to improve it. But what would you do if you needed to develop a brand-new recipe from scratch? Building artificial intelligence (AI) is similar, but requires a much more complex recipe! To “cook up” smart AI, scientists combine billions of instructions in just the right way, so the program can recognize patterns, solve problems, and reason like a human. However, it is nearly impossible to guess the best sequence of instructions in advance. Optimization algorithms are like helpful chefs in the kitchen, testing how well the AI performs, figuring out what is wrong, and tweaking the recipe to improve it. Optimization algorithms help computer scientists discover better versions of the recipe, until the AI becomes smarter and more powerful—just like perfecting a delicious cake!

title: Federated and Differentially Private Prediction of Immune Checkpoint Blockade Response from Multi-Cohort Transcriptomics
abstract: Transcriptomic signatures of immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) response often exhibit limited transportability across independent cohorts, while privacy constraints restrict pooling of pa-tient-level transcriptomic data across institutions. We evaluated whether federated learning (FL) with record-level differential privacy (DP) could predict ICB response across heterogeneous cohorts and whether a pre-specified PD-L1-trafficking module added predictive signal beyond an inter-feron-γ (IFN-γ) signature. Five public ICB cohorts (four anti-PD1 melanoma and one anti-PD-L1 urothelial cohort) were treated as federated sites. Logistic regression was trained using FedAvg and FedProx with per-example DP-SGD and cumulative Rényi DP accounting. The evaluation was conducted through leave-one-cohort-out external validation against a matched centralized non-private reference. The mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUROCs) were modest, ranging from approximately 0.56 to 0.61, and remained broadly stable across the privacy budgets evaluated. Specifically, for the combined feature set, mean AUROC was 0.561 without DP and 0.573 at ε = 1. The IFN-γ module provided the strongest predictive signal (≈0.61), whereas trafficking alone performed near chance (≈0.49), and combining the modules did not im-prove overall discrimination (≈0.56). These results support the feasibility of privacy-preserving federated ICB-response prediction despite significant cross-cohort heterogeneity. DRG2 exhibited a directionally consistent positive contribution across full-cohort and melanoma-only analyses, which persisted in a sensitivity analysis that additionally modeled upstream recycling regulators, including RAB5A, concordant with its established role in endosomal PD-L1 recycling and anti-PD-1 response.

title: Study of A Theoretical and Experimental Model of Direct Solar Radiation At the University of Agadez Experimental Site in Niger
abstract: This work involves evaluating direct solar radiation by applying Kasten’s semi-empirical mathematical model and comparing the results with measurements taken at the University of Agadez experimental site (Agadez urban commune), with the aim of sizing a 20 MWe thermodynamic solar power plant. This study was conducted under three different atmospheric conditions (overcast, average, and clear skies) and using three solar collector tilt angles (0°, 17°, and 30°). Radiation calculations were performed using Excel software by incorporating appropriate equations into a program based on the Kasten model. As for the measurements, they were conducted over ten (10) typical days using two pyranometers. After correcting for the Linke turbidity factor, the resulting direct solar radiation and theoretical annual irradiation are 680 W/m² and 2,979 kWh/m²/year, respectively, compared to measured values of 767 W/m² and 3,010 kWh/m²/year. This study confirms Agadez's strong solar potential for CSP.
