title: A Stochastic Recursive Gradient Algorithm with Random Barzilai–Borwein Step Size for Convex Optimization
abstract: The StochAstic Recursive grAdient algoritHm (SARAH) has garnered considerable attention owing to its implementation of a straightforward recursive framework for stochastic gradient updates. Motivated by this, we propose to integrate the importance sampling strategy with mini-batch techniques into the SARAH framework, developing a variant termed SARAH-MI-RBB. During each inner iteration of SARAH-MI-RBB, the mini-batch technique and importance sampling method are employed to dynamically adjust the Barzilai–Borwein (BB) step size and update the iterates. We provide a linear convergence in expectation of the outer iterates to the unique optimal solution for strongly convex problems. Furthermore, we provide a complexity analysis of the algorithm. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in its class.

title: Retinal OCTA Phenotyping with LLM Reporting for Alzheimer's Disease
abstract: Early identification of Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains challenging because established assessment methods can be costly, resource-intensive, or unsuitable for population-scale screening. Optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) provides non-invasive visualization of retinal microvasculature, but existing approaches often require diagnostic labels and provide limited measurement-level interpretation. We present an explainable OCTA pipeline that integrates annotation-aware vessel segmentation, layer-specific vascular biomarker extraction, label-free phenotyping, and measurement-grounded LLM reporting. Using 117 ROSE-1 images from 39 subjects, we apply annotation-matched segmentation models to superficial vascular complex (SVC), deep vascular complex (DVC), and combined SVC+DVC representations. The models achieve ROC-AUC values of 0.916-0.970 and Dice scores of 0.695-0.781. Six density and fractal-dimension biomarkers form subject-level profiles for exploratory clustering. Analysis of nine held-out subjects identifies an internally consistent lower-density, lower-fractal-dimension phenotype, although the absence of diagnostic labels prevents clinical interpretation. Reports generated using GPT, Gemini, and Llama are evaluated for measurement grounding, citation faithfulness, and diagnostic caution. Overall, the framework provides a transparent, non-diagnostic connection between retinal vascular measurements, exploratory phenotyping, and evidence-linked interpretation for Alzheimer's research.

title: Causality and Attraction: A Continuum of Steady States - Volume XII: The Signal: AI-Assisted Research Content
abstract: Causality and Attraction: A Continuum of Steady States - Volume XII: The Signal examines AI-assisted research content, authorship, provenance, novelty, detection, watermarking, and fingerprinting. The volume applies Nested Causal Modelling to the relationship among human language, machine-generated text, institutions assigning authorship, and readers determining value. It investigates whether statistical resemblance can establish authorship; follows the reciprocal influence of human and machine language; examines original prompts and DOI chronology as research evidence; and develops an account of responsible AI assistance that preserves human authorship, accountability, and novel ideation. The appendices contain the complete nested causal model, research evidence ledger, completed novelty ledger, statement on artificial-intelligence use, and the originating author prompts that materially directed the inquiry.

title: Boundary Information Theory - BIT-X13.6 ACTC REL-001: Grammar-Neutral Software-State Benchmark and Terminal Result Integration
abstract: Public-audit handoff for the BIT-X13.6 Adaptive Cognitive Topology Computer (ACTC) software-state benchmark. A frozen synthetic benchmark executed 72 cases under 12 policies (864 evaluations). The predeclared load-bearing gate for the Bagua-derived 8/64-state grammar failed, yielding NON_LOAD_BEARING_SYMBOLIC_ENCODING within scope. The terminal integration therefore retains the 8/64 grammar only as a historical-semantic source and optional symbolic encoding, while preserving a grammar-neutral ACTC core: State Estimation → Continuous/Typed Operator Selection → Adaptive Weighted Topology → Thermal/Resource Feedback → Self-Mapping → Counterfactual Evaluation → Readout/Receipt. F2 remains NOT_OPENED. This release makes no hardware, quantum-computing, empirical-superiority, production-readiness, authority, or world-effect claim.

title: It Ran Is Not It Was Right: A Policy-Conditioned Benchmark of Ten Text-to-SQL Architectures on an Enterprise Database
abstract: Enterprise text-to-SQL assistants are usually judged by whether the SQL runs. On a realistic company database that is misleading: a query can run and still be wrong, return rows the asker may not see, ignore a rule in a policy document, or answer a question that should be refused. We build a testbed (59-table oil-and-gas database with role-based access, an approval workflow, nine policy documents) and a gold set of 94 questions labelled with the correct answer, the asking role, and whether to answer or refuse. Scoring ten published architectures on answer correctness, data leakage, policy grounding, and refusal overturns the execution-success ranking: the declared winner is ninth of ten on correctness, every architecture leaks restricted data (37 to 52 percent), almost none refuse, and the best is right about half the time. Results are stable over three runs, and the winner's validator gate does not fix any of these failures. Data is synthetic. We release the testbed, gold set, and scorer.

title: Non-Linear Geometric Topology Quantum Simulation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of non-linear geometric topology as a foundation for quantum simulation, specifically focusing on the study of topological quantum structures. title: Adaptive Quantum Error Correction Protocol
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive quantum error correction protocol designed to dynamically adjust error correction algorithms based on the quantum system's state. The core innovation lies in the implementation of a "quantum state dynamic encoding" mechanism, leveraging the self-correlation of quantum states to construct a flexible and adaptive correction strategy. This approach contrasts with traditional static algorithms, offering significantly improved error correction efficiency and robustness. The paper details the proposed mechanism, its theoretical foundation, and preliminary experimental validation demonstrating its effectiveness in mitigating quantum errors. The focus is on enhancing the system's resilience against noise and decoherence.

title: Based on Information Entropy: Automatic Semantic Evolution of Programs
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to automatic program evolution based on information entropy. The core claim is that program semantics can be automatically evolved through changes in information entropy. Specifically, the entropy of a program's execution results is intrinsically linked to its semantic meaning, and variations in this entropy drive optimization and adjustment of the code. The proposed mechanism utilizes intermediate state information generated during program execution to calculate entropy values. These entropy change quantities serve as optimization objectives, guiding the automatic adjustment of code structure and logic through techniques like genetic algorithms or reinforcement learning, ultimately minimizing entropy fluctuations. This method overcomes the limitations of traditional, human-intervention-dependent program optimization techniques, offering a globally-optimized approach by leveraging the theoretical foundations of information theory. The research presents a new perspective on program optimization, shifting the focus from explicit code modifications to the inherent informational structure of the program's behavior. ---

title: Biofeedback-Driven Adaptive Algorithm Optimization
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to algorithm optimization leveraging biofeedback data. The core concept revolves around dynamically adjusting algorithm parameters and structure in real-time based on physiological signals, specifically focusing on data streams like electroencephalography (EEG) and heart rate variability (HRV). We propose a framework where a machine learning model learns the mapping between these biological signals and performance metrics of the algorithm. This learned relationship is then used to iteratively refine the algorithm's configuration, leading to adaptive optimization. The key distinction from existing methods lies in the direct utilization of biofeedback for algorithmic control, moving beyond simple user interface feedback. The paper details the theoretical framework, outlines potential implementation strategies, and discusses the challenges and future directions of this biofeedback-driven adaptive optimization paradigm. The overarching goal is to create algorithms that are not only optimized for a specific task but also inherently responsive to the user's state and the environment, potentially leading to significant improvements in efficiency and robustness.

title: Algorithmic Transparency via Computational Provenance Tracking
abstract: Algorithmic transparency is increasingly crucial as algorithms permeate various aspects of modern life, impacting decisions with significant consequences. However, the inherent complexity and "black box" nature of many algorithms hinder understanding and trust. This paper proposes a novel approach to enhancing algorithmic transparency: computational provenance tracking. The core idea is to establish a verifiable record of an algorithm's execution history, providing an immutable audit trail that details every step of its operation. This system meticulously tracks data transformations, parameter updates, and intermediate results, moving beyond simple logging to create a truly auditable record. The system's design focuses on creating a verifiable and auditable record, fostering greater transparency and accountability. This approach addresses limitations of existing methods and lays a foundation for improved algorithmic trust and scrutiny. The primary metric for success will be the ability to reconstruct the algorithm's decision-making process with complete fidelity, enabling external verification and validation. ---

title: Towards Enhanced Security in Distributed Storage via Quantum Error Correction Codes
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of utilizing quantum error correction (QEC) codes to significantly enhance the security of distributed storage systems. Traditional cryptographic approaches for securing distributed data are increasingly vulnerable to attacks from quantum computers. This research proposes a novel framework leveraging the inherent error-correcting capabilities of QEC codes to provide robust protection against a wide range of attacks, including those specifically designed for classical cryptographic systems. The core of the approach involves the implementation of a tailored encoding and decoding scheme based on a chosen QEC code. We explore the theoretical foundations of QEC, focusing on key parameters such as code distance, encoding rate, and decoding complexity. The goal is to demonstrate a pathway toward constructing a distributed storage architecture that exhibits significantly improved resistance to data breaches and manipulation, particularly in scenarios where quantum computing capabilities pose a serious threat. This work highlights the emerging role of QEC in securing information infrastructure against the looming challenges of quantum computing.

title: On Differential Geometry-Based Machine Learning Models
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to machine learning model design leveraging concepts and techniques from differential geometry. The core idea is to treat a machine learning model as a differential equation and utilize optimization methods from differential geometry for training. Traditional machine learning model design predominantly relies on linear algebra and probability theory, often neglecting the geometric structure inherent in these models. This approach aims to improve model generalization ability by explicitly incorporating geometric considerations. We present a framework for formulating machine learning models within a differential geometric context, outlining key elements including the model as a Lagrangian, optimization strategies based on Riemannian geometry, and potential benefits for model robustness and adaptability. This work establishes a foundation for a fundamentally new perspective on machine learning model design, shifting the focus from purely statistical approaches to one grounded in the rich mathematical structure of differential geometry. ---

title: Dynamic Adaptive Graph Neural Networks: A Novel Approach to Graph Representation and Reasoning
abstract: Dynamic Adaptive Graph Neural Networks (D-AGNNs) represent a significant advancement in graph neural network design, focusing on the ability to dynamically adjust the graph structure to optimize both representation and reasoning capabilities. This paper introduces a novel algorithmic framework, leveraging adaptive algorithms to dynamically re-shape the graph topology based on the inherent characteristics of the input graph. The core of the system lies in a self-adjusting process, iteratively refining the graph structure to enhance the representation learned by the network. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through extensive experiments on benchmark graph datasets, showcasing a substantial improvement in both accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. Furthermore, we explore the impact of different dynamic adjustment strategies on the network's performance, providing insights into optimal graph structure configuration. The proposed D-AGNNs offer a robust and adaptable solution for a wide range of graph-related tasks.

title: Topological Quantum State Partitioning for Complexity Analysis
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Topological Quantum State Partitioning (TQP) to enhance complexity analysis of quantum systems. Traditional methods often struggle with the sheer scale of quantum computations, necessitating computationally intensive techniques. We propose a novel mapping algorithm based on topological invariants to partition quantum states into smaller, interconnected groups, thereby reducing computational burden and facilitating efficient complexity assessment. The core mechanism hinges on identifying and exploiting these invariants to establish connectivity within the quantum state space. This approach offers a significant advancement in the field, potentially enabling faster and more scalable analysis of complex quantum systems.

title: Bayesian Geometric Modeling for Dynamical Systems Analysis
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Bayesian geometric modeling framework designed for the analysis of complex dynamical systems. Traditional approaches often struggle with the inherent uncertainty associated with these systems, limiting the ability to accurately represent evolution and understand system behavior. Our framework leverages Bayesian inference directly within the geometric modeling process, offering a more robust and mathematically rigorous approach. We present a comprehensive theoretical foundation and a practical implementation demonstrating significant improvements in system stability and uncertainty quantification compared to existing methods. The core mechanism centers around representing system evolution as a probabilistic mapping within a geometric framework, enabling precise quantification of uncertainty.

title: Foundations and Frontiers of Swahili Natural Language Processing
abstract: Swahili serves as a lingua franca for over 200 million speakers across East and Central Africa, functioning as a critical engine for digital societal interaction and economic integration. Despite its extensive demographic prominence, it remains acutely under-resourced within the computational domain of Natural Language Processing (NLP). This article presents a mathematically rigorous, systematic review of the Swahili NLP landscape, charting its historical trajectory from acute data scarcity to an emerging ecosystem of statistically specialised tools and representations. We comprehensively catalogue and mathematically categorise primary labelled datasets deployed for classification and generative tasks, including sentiment analysis, automatic speech recognition (ASR), and abstractive summarisation. Furthermore, we analyse the parameter optimisation, tokenisation dynamics, and architectural efficacy of dedicated foundational language models—such as SwahBERT, AfriBERTa, and specialised Large Language Models (LLMs)—mapping their performance bounds against Swahili’s highly agglutinative morphology. Beyond a mere structural inventory, this review critically exposes the “resource quality gap”, identifying profound statistical deficiencies in domain-specific corpora across high-stakes fields such as healthcare and law, whilst highlighting an acute lack of dialectal variance and fine-grained annotation schemes. The analysis concludes that while generalised parameter spaces have expanded, the absence of unified benchmarking infrastructures impedes systematic algorithmic validation. Finally, we propose actionable, statistically sound methodologies for future research, advocating for the collaborative construction of comprehensive multi-task benchmarks to bridge the digital divide for the Swahili-speaking populace.

title: Hybrid Architecture of Intelligent Systems with a Deterministic Core: from Concept to Prototype
abstract: The rapid development of large language models and autonomous intelligent agents has significantly expanded the capabilities of natural language processing and decision support. However, practical implementation reveals fundamental limitations, particularly in tasks requiring computational robustness, reproducibility of results, and strict information consistency. These issues are particularly critical in fields such as engineering, geometry, and educational systems, where plausible but inaccurate responses ("hallucinations") and unstable behavior undermine system trust. This paper proposes a hybrid intelligent architecture with a deterministic core to address these challenges. Unlike fully autonomous systems, the proposed approach decouples functions: an adaptive agent handles user interaction and its interpretation, while a stationary deterministic core provides robust computation, logical consistency, and graphical display. The architecture introduces a clear distinction between the development phase, which allows for iterative improvement, and the operational phase, characterized by a fixed core that guarantees reproducible and verifiable results. By providing protocol-based interaction between the agent and the deterministic core, the system ensures that all generated output—text, computational, and graphical—remains consistent and adheres to the underlying domain model. This hybrid structure combines the flexibility of modern intelligent agents with the precision and reliability of formal deterministic models, offering a robust foundation for mission-critical intelligent applications.

title: KI im Projektmanagement: Wie Peer-Groups den KI-Einstieg erleichtern
abstract: Künstliche Intelligenz (KI) ist für viele Unternehmen strategisch gesetzt – doch der Weg in konkrete Projekte bleibt oft unklar. Gerade im Mittelstand fehlt es an Orientierung und klaren Ansätzen, wie sich sinnvolle Anwendungsfälle identifizieren und priorisieren lassen. Der Beitrag zeigt am Beispiel einer unternehmensübergreifenden Peer-Group in Kassel, wie gemeinsames Lernen helfen kann, Unsicherheit zu reduzieren und KI-Initiativen schrittweise in das Projekt- und Multiprojektmanagement zu überführen. Durch kollegiale Beratung, Co-Creation-Workshops, Impulsvorträge und Unternehmensbesuche entwickeln sie ein praktisches Verständnis für KI-Vorhaben. Das Ergebnis: Mehr Orientierung, verbesserte Projektpriorisierung, verkürzte Lernzyklen, mehr Mut zum Experimentieren. Aus dem Austausch entstehen konkrete Projekte – teils unternehmensübergreifend.

title: The convergent laboratory: when AI reasoning, autonomous experiments, high performance and quantum computing reshape chemistry
abstract: This Comment emerges from TPC26 (https://tpc26.org), a conference convening leaders from academia, national laboratories, and industry who are reshaping materials science discovery. The meeting explored how AI, autonomous agents, self-driving labs, higher performance and quantum computing converge to amplify their individual impact on materials science discovery. The perspectives here reflect the firsthand experiences of researchers at these frontiers and capture the essence of this global endeavor. title: Measuring the Novelty of Biomedical Papers Using the Latent Distances between Knowledge Units
abstract: Measuring the novelty of scientific papers is a central concern in research evaluation and scientometrics. From a recombination perspective, prior studies have largely focused on the co-occurrence of knowledge units to assess the novelty of scientific papers. However, these studies often overlook other relationships between knowledge units. This narrow view may result in inaccurate or incomplete evaluations of novelty for scientific papers. To fill this gap, this study introduces a comprehensive novelty measurement that incorporates three types of relationships between knowledge units: network, semantic, and hierarchical. These relationships are used to quantify the latent distances among knowledge units. Using a dataset of 142,036 articles published in PLoS ONE and a validation dataset from the H1 Connect platform, our results demonstrate that (1) each relationship type captures distinct latent distances between MeSH terms; (2) compared to the widely used indicators proposed by Uzzi et al. (2013), our measures show stronger alignment with peer judgements; and (3) combining all three distance metrics yields more effective identification of novel papers than using any single perspective alone.

title: RefactorPlatform: An Open-Source Harness for Controlled Evaluation of Repository-Scale Refactoring Agents
abstract: Repository-scale refactoring requires coding agents to propagate a single change across many interdependent files without altering program behavior, yet to our knowledge no existing harness isolates the design choices that determine agent success on this task. We present RefactorPlatform, an open-source evaluation harness that holds the environment fixed and varies each design axis explicitly: model backbone (via OpenRouter and GitHub Copilot CLI), execution regime (baseline, retrieval-augmented, and multi-agent), and prompt specificity. Each run executes in an isolated workspace with live terminal streaming, per-task logging of tokens, diffs, and transcripts, AST-based verification, and exportable telemetry for audit and reproduction. Demonstrating the platform on 100 multi-file RefactorBench tasks across four model families, we illustrate the analyses it supports: AST-aware chunking outperforms naive token-window chunking by 25-30 percentage points (pp) across prompt modes, whereas naive retrieval falls below the retrieval-free baseline; a lean retrieval-augmented single agent (86%) beats the sub-agent configuration we evaluated (66%) on matched tasks with no task passing under delegation that fails under retrieval; and retrieval's accuracy gains absorb its token overhead, leaving cost per successful refactoring unchanged. RefactorPlatform is open-sourced to make refactoring-agent evaluation reproducible and auditable.

title: The Cross-Correlation Distribution of the Niho-Type Decimation $d=4(2^m-1)+1$
abstract: The cross-correlation problem is a classical problem in sequence design. In this paper, we determine the cross-correlation distribution of the Niho-type decimation $d=4(2^m-1)+1$ over $\mathbb F_{2^{2m}}$ for every positive integer $m$. With $q=2^m$, this is equivalent to determining the distribution of the number of roots in $U_{q+1}$ of $f_a(x)=x^7+ax^4+\bar a x^3+1$ for $a\in\mathbb F_{q^2}$, where $U_{q+1}=\{x\in\mathbb F_{q^2}:x^{q+1}=1\}$. The main difficulty is to count the four-element subsets of $U_{q+1}$ that may occur as root sets of $f_a$. We normalize such subsets by their product and study the resulting condition through the associated resolvent. This reduces the required enumeration to several equations over $\mathbb F_q$, which are evaluated by character sums and Kloosterman sums. The remaining mixed Kloosterman sum is related to a Kloosterman sum over $\mathbb F_{2^{2m}}$ and is evaluated using a theorem of Carlitz. Consequently, we obtain explicit formulas for all the frequencies in the cross-correlation distribution.

title: Spin Teleportation via Bell-Triplet States Emergent from Proton-Proton Scattering
abstract: Entanglement is a key resource in quantum information science, yet its properties and applications in nuclear systems remain largely unexplored. Here, using proton-proton scattering as a quantum laboratory, we report the emergence of a near-pure Bell-triplet state at a laboratory energy of 151 MeV and a center-of-mass scattering angle of 90°. In this unique kinematic regime, the scattering amplitude functions as a transition operator connecting distinct Bell states. Building upon this emergent resource, we propose a quantum teleportation protocol for proton spins, exploiting the intrinsic Hamiltonian of the strong interaction to perform the requisite Bell measurement effectively. These findings effectively bridge few-body nuclear physics and quantum technology, establishing proton-proton scattering as both a source of high-fidelity entanglement and a natural processor for quantum information.

title: NeSy-RegReason: A Neuro-Symbolic AI Framework for Interpretable and Adaptive Regulatory Compliance in Financial Services
abstract: Financial compliance systems must identify suspicious behaviour while also showing which legal obligations, facts, and exceptions support each decision. Purely neural models learn complex transaction patterns but usually provide post-hoc explanations that do not constitute legal reasoning; conventional rule engines are inspectable but brittle under behavioural and regulatory change. This study presents NeSy-RegReason, a neuro-symbolic framework combining Transformer and graph neural prediction, a versioned regulatory knowledge graph, OWL/SWRL/Prolog inference, rule-conflict resolution, counterfactual explanation, and an immutable audit trace. Evaluation uses author-supplied results across IEEE-CIS, PaySim, Elliptic, and a 500,000-record synthetic multi-regulation dataset. NeSy-RegReason attained 95.86% accuracy, 0.956 F1-score, 0.986 ROC-AUC, and 0.918 Matthews correlation coefficient. It achieved 98.31% compliance detection with 1.89% false positives, 0.97 explanation fidelity, 99.12% audit-trace completeness, and 98.54% conflict resolution. Wilcoxon comparisons against five principal baselines were significant (p ≤ .002; effect sizes 0.68–0.83). Ablation results show that symbolic reasoning is the most consequential component for explainability and auditability. The findings indicate that compliance performance should be evaluated as a multi-objective problem spanning prediction, rule satisfaction, explanation fidelity, trace reproducibility, and adaptation latency. Because the supplied aggregate results do not include run-level observations, code, or an external replication package, the statistical claims are reported as supplied and require independent reproduction before operational deployment.

title: Classification of Selected Author Styles in Post-Millennium World Literature Based on Stylometric Characteristics
abstract: Bu çalışma, milenyum sonrası dünya edebiyatında öne çıkan yazarların üsluplarını hesaplamalı stilometri, doğal dil işleme ve makine öğrenmesi yöntemleriyle incelemektedir. Çalışma kapsamında J. M. Coetzee, Orhan Pamuk, Herta Müller, Mario Vargas Llosa, Mo Yan, Alice Munro, Kazuo Ishiguro, Olga Tokarczuk, Abdulrazak Gurnah, Annie Ernaux, Jon Fosse, Han Kang ve László Krasznahorkai’nin seçili eserlerinden oluşan çok kültürlü bir edebi korpus oluşturulmuştur. Metinler ön işleme süreçlerinden geçirilmiş, yaklaşık 1000 kelimelik segmentlere ayrılmış ve sözcüksel, biçimsel, sözdizimsel ve n-gram tabanlı stilometrik özellikler çıkarılmıştır. Elde edilen özellikler Linear SVM, Naive Bayes, Random Forest ve Logistic Regression gibi makine öğrenmesi modelleriyle değerlendirilmiştir. Bulgular, özellikle Word TF-IDF özellikleriyle eğitilen Linear SVM modelinin yüksek sınıflandırma başarısı gösterdiğini ortaya koymaktadır. Çalışma, yazar üslubunun hesaplamalı yöntemlerle modellenebilen çok katmanlı bir yapı olduğunu göstermekte; aynı zamanda dijital beşeri bilimler ve kültürlerarası edebiyat araştırmaları için yeni bir analitik çerçeve sunmaktadır.

title: Quantum State-Driven Machine Learning Auto-Selection
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to machine learning, termed Quantum State-Driven Machine Learning Auto-Selection, which leverages the unique properties of quantum states to automate the selection of optimal features and model parameters. The core concept revolves around dynamically adjusting model parameters based on the quantum state, allowing the algorithm to explore the parameter space more efficiently and discover superior model configurations. Traditional machine learning relies heavily on human-defined parameters, while this approach seeks to automate this process through the inherent properties of quantum mechanics. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, the underlying quantum mechanics principles used, and its potential impact on model performance through a detailed analysis. We provide a comprehensive overview of the proposed method, including mathematical formulations and illustrative examples demonstrating its effectiveness. The study explores the potential of this approach to address limitations of conventional machine learning algorithms.

title: Adaptive Self-Organizing Neural Networks (ASNN) Structure Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates and develops an adaptive self-organizing neural network (ASNN) structure optimization algorithm. The core goal is to enhance neural network performance by dynamically adjusting network node connection weights. We introduce a novel mechanism that allows for continuous, real-time weight adjustment during training, leading to improved efficiency and potentially better model generalization. The proposed algorithm focuses on a feedback loop between the network's output and the adjustment of weights, enabling the network to adapt to changing data patterns. This approach contrasts with traditional static optimization techniques, offering a more responsive and potentially superior solution for neural network design. The paper details the algorithm's implementation, analyzes its performance through simulations and a limited experimental setup, and concludes with a discussion of future research directions.

title: Adaptive Quantum Topology Networks
abstract: Quantum topology networks (QTN) represent a promising paradigm for quantum information processing and communication, leveraging the unique properties of quantum geometry to enable enhanced data transmission and manipulation. This paper explores the design and implementation of an adaptive quantum topology network, which dynamically adjusts network topology to optimize quantum information flow and significantly enhance quantum communication capabilities. We present a novel approach utilizing a feedback loop to continuously refine the network's structure, improving the robustness and efficiency of quantum data transfer. The core mechanism involves adjusting node positions, edge weights, and even the topology itself, all guided by a dynamic optimization algorithm. The advantages of this approach – dynamic adaptability, improved communication efficiency, and enhanced robustness – are discussed, highlighting its potential impact on the field of quantum computing.

title: Topological Quantum Error Correction from E8 Root Lattice Self-Duality — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: The 240 E8 root vectors form a self-dual even lattice whose packing geometry naturally encodes a topological quantum error-correcting code, where the 132Hz base frequency establishes the energy gap protecting logical qubits from decoherence. The Tutte polynomial specialization over finite fields classifies error syndrome configurations by mapping combinatorial hyperplane arrangements to lattice defect structures, while the φ^k frequency scaling of modular phase-space coordinates defines the logical encoding manifold. This unifies the phase interference dynamics of quantum tunneling, the combinatorial algebra of characteristic polynomials, and the entanglement-preserving pathways into a single geometric framework for fault-tolerant quantum computation. Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Continuous Learning Model (QCLM)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel Continuous Learning Model (QCLM) leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement to address the challenges inherent in continuous learning scenarios involving multiple, interconnected quantum data sources. The core idea is to establish an entanglement network between these data sources, allowing for the extraction of information and the continuous, high-precision modeling of the overall system state. Unlike traditional machine learning approaches that rely on classical data and discrete training steps, QCLM exploits the non-classical nature of quantum entanglement to facilitate information fusion across data sources and achieve superior performance, particularly in high-dimensional, non-linear, and highly correlated quantum datasets. The model continuously updates its quantum state representation and utilizes the entanglement network for dynamic information integration, resulting in robust and adaptive learning capabilities. Mathematical formulations detail the key components of the QCLM, including the entanglement network structure, the quantum state representation, and the update rules governing the learning process. This approach offers a promising pathway for developing advanced quantum learning systems capable of handling complex, dynamic environments. ---

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Adaptive Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, holds immense potential for revolutionizing information processing and computation. However, harnessing this phenomenon effectively presents significant challenges, particularly in achieving precise measurements and demanding computational tasks. This paper introduces a novel quantum entanglement information adaptive algorithm, designed to dynamically adjust quantum entanglement strength based on environmental noise. This adaptive approach aims to significantly enhance the accuracy of quantum measurements and unlock the full potential of quantum systems. The algorithm leverages the inherent properties of entangled states as information carriers, employing a feedback mechanism to optimize the entangled state and achieve enhanced quantum precision. This research presents a fundamentally new method for controlling and manipulating quantum systems, representing a significant step towards more robust and versatile quantum technologies.

title: Title: Constraint-Based Probability Theory for Complex Systems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to probability theory based on constraint-based methods, designed to effectively model complex systems with intricate interactions and emergent properties. Traditional probability methods often struggle to capture the true dynamics of such systems, requiring assumptions of specific outcomes that may not align with the system's underlying structure. This work proposes a new framework that focuses on *likelihood* – the probability of a system exhibiting a behavior – rather than solely on specific outcomes. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of mathematical proofs and illustrative examples, highlighting its potential to unlock deeper insights into systems exhibiting strong constraints. The core mechanism centers around rigorously defining and proving the *validity* of a system's likelihood based on the imposed constraints, offering a more robust and adaptable framework for analysis.

title: Neural Network Dynamics Simulation – Rule-Based Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel neural network dynamics simulation framework, termed Rule-Based Neural Network Dynamics Simulation (NBNDS), designed to optimize neuronal connections based on a set of predefined rules. The core aim of NBNDS is to enhance system behavior and stability by iteratively refining connection strengths through a rule-driven optimization process. We present a methodology that leverages a hierarchical rule engine to dynamically adjust connection weights, fostering a more robust and predictable neural network behavior. This research offers a new approach to network design, particularly in scenarios requiring enhanced stability and robustness. The work highlights the potential of this framework to address challenges in neural network design and control.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic network structure optimization method leveraging Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). The core principle is to automatically adjust network parameters based on real-time changes in network topology – specifically, node and edge weights – to enhance overall network performance. Traditional network optimization methods often rely on manual adjustments, limiting their adaptability. We propose a GNN-based approach that iteratively learns and adapts network structures, resulting in a more robust and efficient system. The method's effectiveness is demonstrated through a series of experiments across various graph datasets, showcasing its superior performance compared to existing optimization techniques. This work offers a significant advancement in network design and optimization, addressing a critical need for adaptable and automated network structure refinement.

title: Quantum State Representation with Dynamic Kernel Expansion
abstract: Abstract: Quantum state representation is a fundamental concept in quantum information theory, crucial for quantum algorithms and quantum computation. Traditional state representations often rely on fixed dimensionality, limiting the expressiveness of quantum states. This paper introduces a novel quantum state representation that dynamically expands the kernel of a state space, allowing for more expressive representations. We propose a neural network-based approach to learn a dynamic kernel function, enabling a flexible and powerful representation of quantum states. This advancement offers a significant step towards more efficient quantum algorithms and a deeper understanding of quantum phenomena. The proposed method demonstrates improved performance in various quantum state comparison and manipulation tasks.

title: Quantum Topological Simulation: Geometric Transformation Algorithm
abstract: Quantum Topological Simulation (QTS) represents a novel approach to geometric transformation, leveraging the inherent properties of quantum states to achieve precision and efficiency in complex transformations. This paper presents a robust algorithm based on QTS, designed to dynamically adjust the topological structure of a given graph during transformation. We introduce a novel mechanism utilizing quantum state self-adaptation to ensure accurate and efficient transformations across a range of geometric scenarios. The core claim is that the algorithm autonomously adjusts the topological structure, providing unparalleled precision and efficiency compared to traditional methods. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of QTS through rigorous analysis and validation of its performance across diverse geometric transformations.

title: Quantum Algorithm-Based Geometric Optimization
abstract: Quantum Algorithm-Based Geometric Optimization explores the potential of leveraging quantum algorithms to enhance geometric optimization techniques. This paper investigates the inherent advantages of quantum computation over classical computation in optimizing complex geometric structures, with a particular focus on addressing limitations inherent in traditional optimization methods. We examine how quantum algorithms, specifically those designed for optimization, can potentially overcome challenges in finding optimal solutions within constrained spaces. The core mechanism involves systematically exploring and implementing quantum algorithms to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of geometric optimization processes. The paper argues that this approach offers a novel pathway to achieve more robust and precise solutions compared to conventional methods, particularly when dealing with high-dimensional geometric spaces.

title: Enhancing Cross-Cultural Communication Through Innovations in Digital Humans and Generative Art
abstract: This study investigates how digital humans and generative art can enhance inclusive, culturally informed cross-cultural communication. It first notes limitations of traditional AI models—such as cultural bias from skewed training data, poor localization, and rigid feedback mechanisms—that lead to misinterpretations or inauthentic cultural representation. An innovative model integrating multimodal context recognition (capturing language, facial expressions, tone) and dynamic feedback optimization is then proposed, with a multi-loop structure enabling real-time adjustments to cultural cues. Validated across five languages using datasets like MuST-C and real-world case studies, the model outperforms traditional counterparts: it achieves a 90 ms response time, high cultural adaptability, and up to 93.7% user satisfaction. Findings confirm the model's value in facilitating global cultural knowledge transfer and support its potential for educational, heritage, and international collaboration scenarios.

title: Экспериментальное сравнение валидности обработки эллипсисов алгоритмическим подходом и большими языковыми моделями
abstract: Данная работа посвящена исследованию подходов автоматической обработки эллипсисов с целью выявления основы системы генерации заданий для тестирования когнитивных способностей. Объект исследования – процесс генерации и восстановления эллиптических конструкций в русском языке. Задачи, которые решались в ходе исследования: A. экспериментальное исследование способности больших языковых моделей генерировать эллипсис из полных предложений, а также восстанавливать эллипсисы; B. проектирование и разработка системы обработки эллипсисов на основе анализа синтаксического дерева предложений; C. сравнение качества результатов обработки двумя подходами и выделение ядра будущей системы генерации заданий. Методы проведения работы: анализ научной литературы, эксперимент, анализ и синтез результатов эксперимента. В результате были проведены эксперименты с большими языковыми моделями по восстановлению и генерации эллипсисов в русскоязычных текстах. Эксперименты включают взаимодействие с LLM через простой запрос, а также с применением метода с дополненным контекстом RAG. Была разработана система модулей, один из которых восстанавливает эллипсис в предложениях, а другой – генерирует эллипсис. Модули работают на основе синтаксического дерева предложений. Сравнение результатов двух подходов показало, что LLM справляются с задачами обработки эллипсисов лучше, чем алгоритмический подход. Это связано с особенностью построения предложений в русском языке – синтаксический парсер не всегда верно проставляет связи между словами. Целевой областью применения является система генерации задания для тестирования когнитивных способностей. Также полученные результаты можно использовать в задачах автоматической обработки текстов на русском языке, где наличие эллипсиса мешает обработке. Например, построение чертежа по условию геометрической задачи.

title: FedQS: asynchronous federated learning based on queue scheduling
abstract: With the rapid development of the Internet of Things (IoT) and edge computing, Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a promising distributed framework capable of effectively leveraging distributed devices for machine learning tasks while preserving data privacy. However, in practical scenarios characterized by significant device heterogeneity and communication delays, traditional synchronous FL often suffers from inefficiency due to the straggler effect. Although Asynchronous Federated Learning (AFL) has been proposed to mitigate this, it still faces challenges regarding model staleness and training bias, which hinder convergence performance. To address these issues, this paper presents an asynchronous framework named FedQS . First, FedQS employs a multi-dimensional staleness evaluation mechanism that dynamically assesses updates by combining the similarity between local and global models with client latency metrics. Second, to resolve the coupling between training bias and model staleness, we implement a decoupling solution via a queue scheduling algorithm. This algorithm reprocesses high-staleness model parameters on selected faster helper clients using only the helpers’ local private data while preserving the provenance of the original uploading clients, thereby aiming to reduce stale-update effects in aggregation. Finally, during the aggregation phase, the framework recalibrates aggregation weights based on client contributions to reduce training bias and improve global model accuracy. Comparative experiments on Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets demonstrate that FedQS outperforms four evaluated representative baselines—FedAsync, FedBuff, KAFL, and CAFL—achieving an average accuracy improvement of 8.62%.

title: Semantic Web-Based Education with AI in Basic Education with Values and Morals
abstract: The present education is concerned with the formation of the whole person child, rather than on just learning academic skills. In addition to academic achievement and subject knowledge, students' overall development is enhanced through their qualities of integrity, empathy, responsible behavior, ethical thinking and active participation. But, in many current education systems, measurable academic results are more significant and resources are less available for the identification and development of those personal and moral abilities. To fill this gap and meet the need of learning recommendations for individual students, this study proposes an intelligent education model based on the Semantic Web and Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies. The proposed framework is a semantic based framework of RDF, RDFS, and OWL, to present student-related information in a structured and meaningful way. Relationships between various aspects of a learner's academic and behavioral data are established through ontologies and knowledge graph. These learner characteristics are then analyzed using AI and machine learning techniques to derive relevant learning recommendations. An implementation was built using Python, Flask, Scikit-learn, Joblib and RDFLib. It takes into account academic performance along with factors like honesty, empathy and participation in the classroom in order to predict the learning outcomes and create meaningful semantic profiles for students. The proposed system shows that the use of semantic knowledge representation along with AI can facilitate more relevant recommendations and meet individual learners' needs. The method can also help teachers make decision making by offering a wider perspective of the students' growth rather than relying on their academic performance. Furthermore, including aspects related to values in the learner profile provides opportunities to promote values awareness and responsible attitudes. The proposed framework illustrates the potential of the Semantic Web and AI technologies to assist a learning environment that preserves academic outcomes by considering personal, social, and ethical growth.

title: A Nuclear-Norm Lower Bound for Dithered Scalar Quantization of Matrix Products
abstract: We consider the problem of minimizing error in quantized matrix multiplication $C=AB$. Scalar quantization of the factors introduces rounding errors whose scale depends on the maximum absolute entries -- the ranges -- of their rows and columns. These ranges determine the quantization grid steps. To reduce the error, we optimize over product-preserving transformations that alter the factor ranges and grid steps without changing $C$. Specifically, we seek the smallest leading expected squared error over invertible inner changes of basis and orthogonal outer rotations. Under independent, zero-mean subtractive dither noise on an unbounded lattice, we prove the output-only bound $E_{\rm lead} \ge (c_A+c_B)/K \Vert AB\Vert_*^2$, where $K$ is the inner dimension, $c_A$ and $c_B$ are normalized noise variances, and $\Vert AB\Vert_*$ is the nuclear norm. The bound is tight: an SVD-aligned Hadamard construction attains the infimum whenever a Hadamard matrix of order $K$ exists, including every power of two, while an SVD-aligned DCT construction is within a factor of two for every $K$. Without outer rotations, Gram-matrix balancing minimizes factorization energy, and finite-set flattening achieves the bound within $C\log(K(m+n))$. For power-of-two $K$, conditional expectations deterministically select the Hadamard signs in $O((m+n)K^2)$ exact-real operations. Synthetic experiments verify both constructions and illustrate the tradeoff between regularization and conditioning. These results characterize the full-gauge optimum and quantify the cost of preserving row and column indices.

title: Has MIMO decoding been proved hard from lattice problems?
abstract: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) technology is fundamental to modern wireless communication. Physical layer security seeks to protect transmitted information by exploiting properties of the noisy communication channel. Dean and Goldsmith proposed a polynomial time reduction from lattice problems to MIMO decoding by adapting Regev's reduction for learning with errors (LWE). If valid, this reduction would give physical layer security a strong computational foundation based on the hardness of established lattice problems. Subsequent works presented attacks and counterexamples against the resulting construction, casting doubt on its security but leaving the precise validity and limitations of the underlying reduction incompletely understood. We provide a theoretical examination of the revised reduction and identify the structural features of the LWE reduction that fail to carry over to the non-modular MIMO setting, hence showing that its published proof does not establish the claimed hardness of MIMO decoding. Our results distinguish flaws in the hardness proof from direct attacks on particular parameter choices and clarify what would be required of any attempted repair. We do not rule out physical layer security for MIMO systems in general, but show that the claimed lattice hardness guarantee does not follow from the existing reduction.

title: Cache-Aware Joint Router Adaptation for Memory-Efficient MoE Inference
abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models activate few experts per token, yet their full expert sets can exceed GPU memory and require repeated weight transfers during decoding. We formulate expert-cache management as a model-side algorithmic problem and propose cache-aware post-training that jointly adapts the MoE backbone and lightweight auxiliary routers while preserving the native inference-time Top-K rule. The update-only Temporal Router learns same-layer retention across tokens without proactive loading. The full Spatio-Temporal Router adds a Spatio Router that uses the causal predecessor's hidden state to refine the temporal cache before target-layer access. We evaluate both modes on Qwen3 and GPT-OSS across GSM8K, MATH, and CommonsenseQA. Temporal Router consistently improves hit rate and reduces expert-weight traffic over matched LM-only baselines. On Qwen3, the full mode improves adjusted hit rate by 1.15--18.03 points and reduces traffic by 4.6--53.3\% relative to the strongest evaluated prefetching baseline; GPT-OSS results are competitive but task-dependent. Auxiliary-only training preserves baseline accuracy but yields modest coverage gains; joint post-training achieves substantially higher coverage. Sensitivity analyses distinguish the effects of cache capacity, refinement budget, and cache-loss weight on coverage, traffic, and quality.

title: Генерация адаптивных веб-приложений для полиграфических задач с использованием больших языковых моделей в архитектуре Zero-Dependency
abstract: В статье рассматривается практическое применение больших языковых моделей для создания специализированного веб-приложения по генерации кувертных карт для мероприятий. Исследование выполнено в рамках парадигмы Zero-Dependency – полного отказа от внешних библиотек и фреймворков. С помощью методологии итеративного промпт-инжиниринга реализовано многофункциональное приложение, позволяющее создавать карты трёх различных форматов (90×110 мм, 195×110 мм, 195×165 мм) с автоматической раскладкой на листы формата А4. Особое внимание уделено решению задач точной типографики, работе с физическими размерами в миллиметрах и генерации двусторонних развёрток для последующей печати и сгиба. Результаты демонстрируют способность искусственного интеллекта эффективно справляться с задачами, требующими прецизионной работы с размерами, автоматизации рутинных операций и создания интуитивного пользовательского интерфейса. Сделан вывод о высокой перспективности применения генеративных моделей для разработки узкоспециализированных полиграфических инструментов.

С помощью методологии итеративного промпт-инжиниринга реализовано многофункциональное приложение, позволяющее создавать карты трёх различных форматов (90×110 мм, 195×110 мм, 195×165 мм) с автоматической раскладкой на листы формата А4. title: TanglishMedBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs on Tamil-English Code-Mixed Medical Queries
abstract: TanglishMedBench is a gold-standard evaluation benchmark of 700 medical question-answer pairs in Tanglish - romanized, WhatsApp-style Tamil-English code-mixed text, as commonly typed by Tamil speakers in everyday messaging. The dataset is designed to evaluate how well language models handle medical queries posed in this informal, code-mixed register, which differs substantially from the formal Tamil or English text most models are evaluated on. Each entry pairs a Tanglish query with its English equivalent, a gold-standard reference answer, and expert annotations for factual accuracy, safety, and disclaimer presence. The dataset is intended for evaluation and benchmarking only and is not intended for training deployed clinical chatbots

title: Adaptive Machine Learning Neural Architecture
abstract: This paper investigates a novel neural network architecture leveraging adaptive learning to dynamically adjust layer connections and weights. Traditional neural network training often relies on manual tuning, limiting the potential for optimization. This research proposes a system that automatically adapts network parameters based on the data's characteristics, resulting in enhanced model performance. We introduce a novel adaptive learning algorithm, termed "Dynamic Layer Adjustment," which iteratively adjusts layer weights and connections based on a learned metric derived from the data. This approach offers a significant improvement over existing methods by enabling the network to self-optimize its structure. The paper details the implementation of the Dynamic Layer Adjustment algorithm, analyzes its impact on model performance, and concludes with future research directions.

title: Adaptive Graph-Based Machine Learning
abstract: The field of machine learning increasingly relies on complex data structures, particularly graphs. These graphs are often exploited for representing relationships and dependencies within data, leading to powerful algorithms. However, traditional machine learning methods often struggle to effectively utilize these graphs, particularly in scenarios where the graph structure itself needs to be dynamically adjusted. This paper introduces a novel approach – Adaptive Graph-Based Machine Learning – that leverages graph neural networks to automatically adjust the graph's structure and connections, resulting in enhanced model performance and efficiency. We propose a framework that allows the model to adapt to the specific characteristics of the graph data, enabling more robust and scalable learning. This work addresses the limitations of current approaches by providing a flexible and automated mechanism for graph manipulation.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Adaptive Geometry Transformation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers a potential pathway to revolutionize computational methods. This paper explores the application of quantum entanglement to adaptive geometry transformations, aiming to enhance model generalization by dynamically adjusting geometric parameters in response to input data noise. We propose a novel algorithm that leverages entanglement to create a fundamentally more efficient and robust computational process. The core mechanism involves quantifying input data as a quantum state, enabling a process of 'quantum mapping' that automatically adjusts geometric parameters. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, showcases initial results through illustrative examples, and discusses the potential impact of this approach on various fields, including image processing and machine learning.

title: 基于自适应的非线性约束的动态优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic optimization algorithm based on adaptive constraints, designed to improve the efficiency of solving complex optimization problems. Traditional constraint optimization methods often rely on manual adjustment, which can be tedious and suboptimal. This algorithm dynamically adjusts the constraint strength and range based on the problem's characteristics, effectively avoiding local optima. We present a theoretical framework and a practical implementation demonstrating the algorithm's effectiveness on a challenging set of optimization tasks. The core mechanism involves a self-tuning constraint adjustment process driven by a feedback loop that analyzes problem parameters. The resulting algorithm exhibits improved convergence speed and robustness compared to existing approaches. We conclude with a discussion of the algorithm's limitations and potential future research directions.

title: Non-Euclidean Tensor Geometry – Self-Organizing Data Structures
abstract: This paper introduces Non-Euclidean Tensor Geometry (NETG), a novel geometric framework for data representation and manipulation, leveraging self-organizing tensor structures. We propose a set of geometric primitives designed to automatically arrange data points, enabling efficient compression and retrieval. The core claim is that NETG offers a fundamentally different approach to data representation, potentially leading to significant improvements in data compression and efficient data access. This work explores the design and implementation of these primitives, demonstrating their ability to achieve specific data compression ratios through self-organization. We provide a preliminary analysis of the benefits and limitations of NETG, highlighting future research directions.

title: 基于图的知识图谱推理
abstract: This paper introduces a novel knowledge graph reasoning approach leveraging graph structures for predictive modeling. We propose a method centered around representing knowledge graphs as graphs, with nodes representing entities and edges defining relationships. This approach allows for automated prediction of unknown knowledge by traversing the graph and applying inference rules derived from the graph's structure. The core mechanism involves constructing a graph representation, defining inference rules, and applying these rules to identify potential knowledge nodes. We present a practical implementation demonstrating the effectiveness of this method in predicting knowledge based on existing graph data. The paper explores the potential of this technique to enhance knowledge discovery and automation across various domains.

title: Title: Self-Organizing Maps with Dynamic Kernel Adjustment
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-organizing map (SOM) algorithm that dynamically adjusts the kernel weights during training. Traditional SOMs rely on a fixed kernel, limiting their ability to effectively represent complex data clusters. This work proposes a reinforcement learning framework to optimize the kernel weights, resulting in improved clustering accuracy and speed compared to static kernel adjustments. We detail the algorithm's core mechanism, the reinforcement learning agent, and the iterative process of weight adjustment. The resulting SOM demonstrates enhanced clustering performance, particularly with datasets exhibiting non-linear relationships. The proposed method offers a significant advancement in SOM technology by incorporating a dynamic kernel adjustment strategy.

title: Quantum Potential Adaptation via Adaptive Neural Networks
abstract: Quantum potential optimization is a critical challenge in quantum computing, significantly impacting algorithm efficiency and the ability to harness quantum resources. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with the inherent complexities of quantum systems, requiring significant computational resources and fine-tuning of parameters. This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum potential optimization leveraging adaptive neural networks, aiming to address these challenges and enable more efficient quantum computation. The core concept centers around dynamically adjusting the network's parameters based on the quantum potential, fostering a more adaptive and robust optimization strategy. We present a detailed framework for implementing this approach, incorporating key mathematical formulations and demonstrating its efficacy through theoretical analysis and simulations. The research explores the potential of this method to improve the performance of various quantum algorithms, highlighting its promise for advancing the field.

Python import numpy as np import datetime import logging from typing import List, Dict, Union # راه‌اندازی سیستم ثبت لاگ استاندارد صنعتی logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format='[%(asctime)s] [%(levelname)s] : %(message)s') class HamzahGrandUnifiedKernel: """ HamzahXcell: Grand Unified Computational Theory of Everything (Omega Production Grade) Unifies Quantum Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Cognitive Science, and Econophysics via Functorial Mappings. self.integrity_score: float = 1.0 logging.info(f"Initializing Grand Unified ToE Kernel for Cluster: {self.cluster_id}") def quantum_chemistry_functor(self, orbital_electron_density: List[float], energy_potential: float) -> Union[float, str]: """نگاشت تابع موج کوانتومی به انرژی آزادسازی پیوند شیمیایی با فیلتر مقادیر منفی""" if not orbital_electron_density: self.integrity_score -= 0.15 valid_capital: self.integrity_score -= 0.3 return "ERROR: هیچ سرمایه معتبری در مانیفلد یافت نشد." sorted_cap = sorted(valid_capital, reverse=True) slice_idx = max(1, int(len(sorted_cap) * 0.2)) title: Dynamic Probability Distribution Reinforcement Learning: Adaptive Feature Extraction Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel reinforcement learning algorithm based on dynamic probability distributions, designed to overcome the limitations of traditional methods. The core concept is to dynamically adjust feature extraction strategies during the learning process, allowing the agent to adapt to evolving data distributions. We propose a new framework that leverages a probabilistic state space, where the probability of each state is dynamically updated based on incoming data. This dynamic adaptation significantly enhances the algorithm's ability to learn robust and optimal policies. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, demonstrates its effectiveness through simulations, and discusses its potential applications in diverse scenarios. The key contribution lies in the implementation of a novel feature extraction mechanism that continuously optimizes the state representation, fostering a more efficient and adaptable learning process.

title: 基于图的量子计算范式 (QCV)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum computing paradigm, termed "Graph-Based Quantum Computing (QCV)," which fundamentally reimagines the process of quantum computation by modeling it as a graph. We propose a method for efficiently implementing quantum algorithms through the exploitation of graph topology, specifically leveraging concepts like graph traversal and connectivity. The core mechanism of QCV centers around constructing and analyzing quantum circuits as graphs, enabling a more structured and intuitive approach to algorithm design and optimization. This research explores the potential of QCV to surpass traditional quantum computing methods in terms of algorithmic efficiency and robustness. We present a preliminary analysis demonstrating the efficacy of QCV in certain specific quantum algorithms, highlighting the advantages of this approach.

title: Data underlying the publication: "Photonic fusion operations transform partial distinguishability"
abstract: Photonic fusion operations are a central primitive in photonic quantum information processing and are commonly characterized by their success probability and resource cost. Here, we identify an additional way in which different implementations of fusion operations differ, namely in how they transform partial distinguishability. We consider distinguishability originating both from imperfect entangled resource states and from imperfect single photons. We find that different successful fusion events can induce markedly different distinguishability transformations depending on the fusion protocol, heralding outcome, and error model. Under a collective resource-state error model, we identify a modification to an existing fusion protocol that improves the fidelity of the remaining state on average. Generally, however, transformations adversely affect distinguishability, and many successful fusion outcomes are accompanied by distinguishability degradation. Our results show that partial distinguishability is dynamically shaped by interference and measurements and should be considered alongside overall fusion success probability when evaluating photonic fusion protocols.

title: Адаптивная защита нейросетевых моделей от состязательных атак на основе предобработки входных данных
abstract: Объект исследования – процесс обнаружения сетевых атак нейросетевыми системами в условиях состязательных воздействий. Цель работы – повышение устойчивости такой системы к состязательным воздействиям без потери качества на чистом трафике. Задачи, решаемые в ходе исследования: 1. Выполнить аналитический обзор методов защиты. 2. Создать макет системы обнаружения атак. 3. Разработать метод адаптивной предобработки, сочетающий детектор состязательности на автоэнкодере, банк преобразований и автономное пороговое правило выбора. 4. Реализовать метод и интегрировать его в систему обнаружения атак. 5. Выполнить экспериментальную оценку эффективности метода. Методологически работа построена как экспериментальное исследование на CICIDS2017. Был выполнен аналитический обзор методов защиты. В результате работы был создан макет системы обнаружения атак с аппаратно изолированным защитным слоем и разработан метод адаптивной предобработки входных данных. Метод был реализован, интегрирован в систему и оценен экспериментально. Полученные результаты могут быть использованы для защиты нейросетевых систем обнаружения и показывают, что адаптивная предобработка обеспечивает устойчивость без потери качества на чистом трафике.

title: Facial Age Estimation for Age Fraud Detection in National ID Systems
abstract: Identity fraud during biometric enrollment and updates remains a major challenge for large-scale national identity systems. A common fraud vector is misrepresenting one's age to access age-restricted services or welfare schemes. In this work, we present SwinAge, a facial age estimation system designed for use within the Aadhaar biometric enrollment pipeline, to assist quality-check (QC) operators to flag potential age-related fraud. This is critical for a system like Aadhaar (the world's largest national identity programme), that holds about 1.5 billion unique identities, with 22.4 million new enrollments and 283 million updates in the last year. Building upon the SwinFace architecture with landmark-based similarity (warp affine) alignment, we train on a large in-house dataset of 1.45 million face images and evaluate on an independent, age-stratified test set of 283K images, both drawn from an ethnically diverse population of 716K unique subjects. We investigate three Aadhaar-specific operational thresholds (5, 18, and 60 years) and propose a deployment triage framework that flags suspected cases for manual review. Following NIST FATE, we report false acceptance/rejection rates (FAR/FRR) at each threshold rather than aggregate accuracy: at 1% FAR the model achieves an FRR of 3% (<5yrs), 0.4% (>18yrs) and 11.0% (>60yrs). SwinAge achieves a mean absolute error (MAE) of 2.94 years on the same test set, outperforming three zero-shot vision language models on all benchmarks, and improving the state-of-the-art on 5 out of 7 public benchmark datasets. We further report per-gender errors and distill lessons for national identity programs.

We investigate three Aadhaar-specific operational thresholds (5, 18, and 60 years) and propose a deployment triage framework that flags suspected cases for manual review. Following NIST FATE, we report false acceptance/rejection rates (FAR/FRR) at each threshold rather than aggregate accuracy: at 1% FAR the model achieves an FRR of 3% (<5yrs), 0.4% (>18yrs) and 11.0% (>60yrs). SwinAge achieves a mean absolute error (MAE) of 2.94 years on the same test set, outperforming three zero-shot vision language models on all benchmarks, and improving the state-of-the-art on 5 out of 7 public benchmark datasets. We further report per-gender errors and distill lessons for national identity programs.

title: From Language Models to World-Acting Systems: Progress and Limits of Agentic AI across Digital, Social, Virtual, and Physical Environments
abstract: Large language models become consequential agents when surrounding systems let outputs change external state. Models now call tools, operate interfaces, delegate work, retain state, inhabit generated worlds, and control robots or laboratory equipment. Such advances are often narrated as one march toward autonomy, conflating model competence, system integration, persistence, and safe authority. This critical review synthesizes primary research and official technical specifications available by 31 August 2026. We organize the evidence along delegated authority, temporal persistence, and environmental coupling, while separating model, harness, and environment. Within the evidence examined, action-interface expansion is documented more convincingly than robust completion, recovery, authorization, or independent verification. Model Context Protocol and Agent2Agent improve interoperability but do not establish trustworthy delegation; multi-agent organization adds specialization alongside cost and correlated failure. Persistent simulations and world models support training and planning but do not themselves demonstrate agency; robotics and self-driving laboratories establish bounded feasibility rather than unattended open-world reliability. We propose justified delegation as an analytical and normative heuristic, not an observed law or certified score: expand action scope only where evidence supports provenance, bounded authority, failure detection, safe recovery, and calibrated human control. This framing yields a research agenda for coupled model-harness evaluation, capability-based permissions, durable state, cross-agent accountability, and staged physical validation.

title: Beyond Code Generation: Reliability, Verification, and Cost Economics in the Agentic Software Development Lifecycle
abstract: AI coding systems are moving from autocomplete and chat toward agents that can inspect repositories, edit multiple files, run tools, write tests, open pull requests, and work for long periods with limited supervision. This capability changes the bottleneck in software delivery. Recent field studies show meaningful gains in coding activity, but newer evidence also shows that those gains attenuate sharply between writing code and shipping reliable software. Review, integration, testing, security, deployment, and production operations remain constraining stages, while the economics are shifting from predictable per-seat licensing toward variable token, tool, sandbox, CI, and rework costs. This paper synthesizes peer-reviewed software-engineering research, university studies, benchmark audits, production reports from major technology companies, developer telemetry, and cost-management evidence released primarily from 2024 through September 2026. No new model experiment is claimed; numerical findings remain attributed to their original studies. The synthesis proposes four engineering concepts: the Agentic SDLC Throughput Paradox, Production-Qualified Change (PQC), the Verification Tax, and an Agentic SDLC Control Plane that allocates autonomy subject to cost, reliability, and human-attention budgets. An evidence-based horizon then maps today's supervised agents to future policy-bounded software factories. The central research question shifts from how much code an agent can generate to how much production-qualified value an engineering system can deliver per dollar, per reviewer-hour, and per unit of operational risk.

title: A Explainability-Driven Approach to SSD Failure Detection Using LIME and SHAP Analysis
abstract: The Solid-state drives (SSDs) have become critical components of modern computing infrastructures because of their high performance, low latency, and increasing deployment in data-intensive systems. However, SSD degradation and failure can develop through complex interactions among workload characteristics, operational conditions, device behavior, and accumulated wear, making reliable failure detection a challenging predictive task. Conventional machine-learning-based failure prediction can provide accurate classifications while remaining difficult for engineers and system administrators to interpret. This creates an important requirement for explainability, particularly when predictive decisions influence preventive maintenance, storage migration, or system availability. This paper proposes an explainability-driven framework for SSD failure detection that integrates predictive modeling with Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME) and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). The methodology treats explainability not as a post-processing visualization but as an analytical layer connecting SSD telemetry, predictive outputs, feature contributions, and operational decisions. The framework incorporates principles derived from evolutionary optimization, intelligent search, recommender systems, large language model research, and computational materials discovery to establish a broader theoretical foundation for data-driven optimization and interpretable decision support. Particular emphasis is placed on feature-level attribution, local versus global explanations, explanation consistency, failure-risk prioritization, and the trade-off between predictive complexity and interpretability. The resulting framework provides a systematic basis for identifying influential SSD health indicators, validating model behavior, and translating failure predictions into actionable maintenance decisions. The study further identifies limitations associated with explanation stability, correlated telemetry variables, model dependence, and the absence of a standardized explanatory ground truth. The proposed approach contributes an interpretable architecture for trustworthy SSD failure detection and establishes directions for future empirical validation.

title: Intelligent Evaluation and Teaching Improvement Strategies for College Classroom Teaching Quality Based on Multi-source Data Fusion
abstract: There are several drawbacks in the assessment of classroom teaching quality in universities, such as limited data sources, long evaluation cycles, and insufficient diagnostic depth, which make it difficult to provide effective support for teaching improvement decisions.This paper proposes a quality education intelligent evaluation architecture based on multi-source data fusion.Through the complete process of data collection -intelligent analysis -closed-loop improvement, the intelligent evaluation of teaching quality is completed.Through research, it was found that the traditional evaluation method is to rely solely on subjective scores at the end of the semester, lacking objective evidence during the teaching process.By leveraging multi-source data fusion, various types of information such as behavior logs, video semantics, academic performance, and supervision evaluations can be collected, thereby achieving precise description of teaching quality and dynamic detection.Therefore, this paper presents a closed-loop mechanism of "evaluation -intervention -improvement", and explores the guarantee means for teaching improvement from the three levels of system, technology, and culture, hoping to provide some references for the digital transformation of the university's teaching quality improvement system.
