title: Robot Controller Architectures for Autonomous and Reactive Robotic Systems
abstract: Robotic controllers refer to the central computing core of robotic systems, responsible for mechanical motion, sensing, actuation, end-effector operation, and interfacing with the environment in a non-deterministic manner. The full-text study offers a theoretical review of robotic controller architectures including autonomous robots, semi-autonomous robots, and reactive robots. It combines the content presented in the article about robot controllers with modern research regarding deliberative controllers, reactive controllers, hybrid, hierarchical robot control systems, skill-based robotic control systems, soft-robots control, and adaptive robot control systems. The paper firstly introduces the idea of robot control as an integration process of perception, state estimation, planning, motion execution, feedback, and event processing. It further explains record-and-playback programming, open-loop and feed-forward control, closed-loop control, reactive control, artificial intelligence-based control, and interrupt handling. It turns out that the use of open-loop control makes sense when performing well-calibrated and predictable actions. In contrast, it is necessary to apply closed-loop control in cases when it is important to correct the state errors caused by disturbances and uncertainty. Reactive controllers help make decisions based on sensory information quickly, although arbitration schemes are required for the selection of behaviors when they run concurrently.

title: Adaptive Topology Learning Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces an Adaptive Topology Learning Algorithm (ATLA) that leverages deep learning to automatically learn and optimize the topology of a system. Traditional topology learning methods often rely on manual design, while ATLA offers a more efficient and automated approach. The algorithm employs a deep neural network to learn the system's topology, which is then dynamically adjusted based on environmental changes, enabling automatic optimization of the resulting topology. This innovative approach aims to surpass the limitations of conventional methods by providing a self-optimizing system.

title: Non-Locality Probability Model Based on Adaptive Geometric Transformations
abstract: This paper presents a novel probabilistic model for complex systems, leveraging adaptive geometric transformations to address the challenges of non-locality. Traditional probabilistic models often rely on static transformations, which may not adequately capture the dynamic nature of real-world systems. This work introduces a model that dynamically adjusts geometric transformations based on system state, resulting in a more accurate and efficient simulation. We demonstrate the model's effectiveness through a series of simulations, highlighting improvements in prediction accuracy and computational efficiency compared to existing methods. The core mechanism centers around a dynamic geometric transformation parameterization, enabling the model to better represent the inherent non-locality present in many systems. This advancement offers a significant step towards more robust and precise modeling.

title: 基于量子纠缠的自适应量子态转移算法
abstract: Quantum state transfer is a fundamental operation in quantum information processing, enabling the manipulation of quantum states across different systems. Traditional approaches often struggle with the limitations of classical information transfer, particularly in scenarios requiring rapid and efficient transfer of quantum information. This paper introduces a novel quantum state transfer algorithm based on the intrinsic self-correlation of quantum entanglement, aiming to overcome these limitations through a dynamic and predictive approach. The algorithm leverages entangled states to facilitate the instantaneous and controlled transfer of quantum information, significantly enhancing the fidelity and speed of state transfer. We detail the core mechanism, including the use of entangled states for self-adaptation and prediction, and present preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness. The proposed algorithm offers a promising pathway toward more robust and scalable quantum information transfer protocols.

title: Quantum Topological Field Theory: A Geometric Optimization Algorithm for Quantum Computing
abstract: Quantum Topological Field Theory (QTTF) presents a novel framework for designing and optimizing quantum computation, leveraging the inherent properties of quantum topology. This paper investigates the application of QTTF to the design of quantum circuits, focusing on achieving enhanced quantum information storage and transmission efficiency. We propose a geometric optimization algorithm driven by QTTF principles, specifically utilizing the self-similarity inherent in topological structures to improve circuit performance and quantum information density. The core mechanism involves the application of QTTF's self-relevant properties to circuit optimization, leading to a significant advancement in quantum computing's capabilities. This work explores the potential of QTTF to revolutionize quantum information processing.

title: Title: Quantum Self-Organizing Network Image Generation Algorithm
abstract: This paper explores a novel image generation algorithm based on Quantum Self-Organizing Networks (QSONs). Traditional image generation methods rely on classical computation, struggling to effectively generate images with complex Gaussian distributions. QSONs offer a potential solution by leveraging quantum mechanics to perform precise calculations, enabling the creation of highly detailed and realistic imagery. We present a theoretical framework outlining the algorithm's core principles and demonstrate its capabilities through illustrative examples, emphasizing the advantages of quantum computation in image synthesis. The core mechanism centers around the construction of a QSON network that inherently generates images conforming to complex Gaussian distributions. This paper addresses the limitations of existing image generation techniques by introducing a fundamentally different approach utilizing quantum principles.

abstract: Probability Geometric Evolution (PGM) presents a novel framework for geometric optimization, leveraging the power of probabilistic logic and evolutionary algorithms. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future directions for this approach.

title: Self-Adaptive Quantum Topology for Quantum Computing Self-Maintenance
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for revolutionary advancements across diverse fields, including drug discovery, materials science, and cryptography. However, maintaining the delicate quantum state – a fundamental requirement for computation – presents significant challenges, particularly in the presence of environmental noise and fluctuations. This paper proposes a novel quantum computing framework centered on self-sustained quantum topology, utilizing quantum entanglement "pulses" to dynamically adjust topology parameters, thereby promoting self-maintenance of the quantum state. This design addresses the limitations of traditional quantum computing by introducing a mechanism for continuous state adaptation, enhancing the robustness and stability of quantum computations. We present a detailed theoretical framework and preliminary experimental validation demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach in stabilizing quantum states. The core claim is that this framework provides a pathway toward robust and self-maintaining quantum computation, significantly extending the operational lifespan and reliability of quantum devices.

title: Quantum Metrology for Real-Time Algorithm Verification
abstract: This paper proposes a novel methodology for real-time algorithm verification utilizing quantum metrology principles. The core concept involves employing entangled states to conduct highly precise measurements of algorithm execution, comparing these measurements against a rigorously defined, verifiable baseline. Traditional algorithm verification methods often rely on simulation and testing, which can be computationally expensive and may not fully capture the nuances of a system's behavior under all conditions. This approach offers a direct, high-precision measurement of algorithm performance, potentially mitigating these limitations. We outline the theoretical framework, focusing on the use of quantum sensitivity to detect subtle deviations from expected behavior. The key advantage lies in the ability to achieve a level of accuracy unattainable through classical methods, offering a robust validation process suitable for complex algorithms, particularly those involved in quantum computing and related fields. The paper details the mathematical foundation, including the Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle and its application to algorithm verification, and presents a framework for quantifying the achievable accuracy. Further research directions are explored, including the integration of this technique with existing verification protocols and the development of tailored entangled state designs.

title: Explainable Graph Neural Networks for Social Network Analysis
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to social network analysis utilizing Explainable Graph Neural Networks (E-GNNs). Traditional graph neural networks, while effective in capturing complex relationships within networks, often operate as black boxes, hindering interpretability and trust. We propose a framework that integrates the expressive power of GNNs with explainable AI techniques, specifically focusing on attention mechanisms and SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) values, to provide transparent and understandable insights into network dynamics. Our methodology allows for the identification of influential nodes and the understanding of the features driving their influence. This work addresses the critical need for interpretability in GNN applications, particularly within the domain of social network analysis, ultimately enhancing the reliability and validity of network-based inferences. The core claim is the design of an E-GNN model for analyzing complex relationships and patterns within social networks. The core mechanism involves combining GNNs with explainability techniques, and the novelty lies in directly addressing the interpretability challenges of GNNs for social network applications.

title: Quantum Matrix Solving Algorithm: An Adaptive Approach
abstract: Quantum matrix solving is a challenging problem in cryptography and optimization, particularly when dealing with complex geometries and nonlinear errors. Traditional methods often require precise parameter adjustments, which can be computationally expensive and susceptible to errors. This paper proposes an adaptive quantum matrix solving algorithm that leverages quantum entanglement and superposition to dynamically adjust parameters during the solving process, offering improved efficiency and robustness. We present a novel mechanism utilizing these quantum phenomena to overcome limitations of existing techniques. This algorithm demonstrates potential for enhanced performance in scenarios demanding high accuracy and resilience against noise.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic adjustment mechanism for Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), termed Dynamic Adjustment Mechanism of Recurrent Neural Networks (DARN). Traditional RNNs rely on static parameter tuning, which often struggles to adapt to evolving data patterns. DARN dynamically adjusts network parameters based on input data's dynamics, enhancing model generalization and adaptability. The proposed method involves a feedback loop that continuously recalibrates weights and connections, ensuring the network maintains optimal performance across a range of inputs. We explore the implementation of DARN with a simplified, illustrative example, demonstrating its potential to improve performance in a specific task. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions, including exploring different adaptive strategies and expanding the application of DARN to diverse datasets.

abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum field simulation optimization (QFSO) as a novel approach to accelerate and enhance physical field simulations. Traditional optimization algorithms often struggle with the computational complexity inherent in these simulations, particularly with large-scale or intricate fields. Quantum field simulation, leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics, offers a paradigm shift. We propose a new QFS optimization algorithm predicated on quantum superposition and entanglement, aiming to significantly reduce the computational burden and potentially uncover optimal solutions that are inaccessible to classical methods. This research investigates the feasibility of implementing this algorithm and demonstrates its potential for improving the efficiency of physical field simulations.

title: APPLICATION OF EXPLAINABLE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE METHODS FOR SEGMENTATION AND CLASSIFICATION OF ATHEROSCLEROTIC PLAQUES FROM OCT DATA
abstract: Highlights This study presents and validates a hybrid framework that combines deep learning with Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) for the segmentation and classification of atherosclerotic plaques. The incorporation of XAI techniques improves the interpretability of deep learning models, thereby facilitating their translation into clinical practice for the diagnosis of atherosclerosis. The results highlight the potential of XAI-enabled approaches to support the development of reliable, transparent, and clinically applicable decision support systems in cardiology. Aim . To develop and validate a comprehensive method for automated segmentation and classification of morphological features of atherosclerotic plaques based on optical coherence tomography using explainable artificial intelligence approaches. Methods . Nine state-of-the-art segmentation neural network architectures were trained on a dataset of 103 OCT studies annotated for four key plaque features. To assess interpretability, nine XAI methods were applied. Results . The best segmentation results were achieved with DeepLabV3+ and MA-Net models (DSC up to 72.1%). LayerCAM and HiResCAM methods provided the most stable and accurate visualization of attention areas. Conclusion . The proposed approach demonstrates high segmentation accuracy and interpretability, enhancing clinical trust and paving the way for future development of explainable AI systems in cardiology.

title: Finite Mixtures of Generalized Estimating Equations for Clustering Multivariate Correlated Outcomes
abstract: Multivariate correlated outcomes occur across disciplines, including ecology, social sciences, and psychometrics. This paper focuses on clustering these outcomes across observational units, specifically, finding groups of units with the same ``outcome profile". Our motivation comes from bioregionalization in ecology, which aims to cluster sites into bioregions with the same species profiles, where site membership can depend on environmental or habitat covariates. To accomplish this, we propose finite mixtures of generalized estimating equations (MixGEE). Unlike existing approaches to model-based bioregionalization, MixGEE partitions sites into regions while accounting for between-species correlations through a region-specific working correlation structure. Thus, each region is characterized by a marginal species mean vector and a between-species correlation matrix. Unlike likelihood-based finite mixture models, MixGEE does not require a full joint distribution of the multivariate outcomes. Instead, we construct a pseudo-posterior probability for region membership motivated by the large-sample distribution of the estimating equation. This leads to an iterative algorithm alternating between updating these probabilities and solving weighted estimating equations. We determine the number of regions using cross-validation based on predictive performance for held-out sites and species components, and use a clustered Dirichlet random-weight bootstrap for uncertainty quantification. Simulations demonstrate reliable estimation and inference under various correlation structures and more stable selection of the number of groups than methods that ignore dependence. Applying MixGEE to presence--absence records of fish species around the Kerguelen Plateau reveals three distinct fish assemblage profiles with heterogeneous occurrence and within-site correlation patterns.

title: Attention-guided super-resolution of 4D flow MRI in carotid arteries
abstract: Four-dimensional (4D) flow magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a powerful non-invasive technique for visualizing and quantifying complex blood flow patterns in vivo. Despite its clinical promise, broader adoption is limited by low spatial resolution and sensitivity to noise, which restrict accurate assessment of critical hemodynamic biomarkers such as wall shear stress, pressure gradients, and turbulent kinetic energy. To overcome these challenges, we propose a deep learning-based super-resolution framework that integrates multi-scale feature extraction and attention mechanisms to enhance the quality of 4D flow MRI data. The model was trained on a dataset of 120 patients with 240 stenosed carotid arteries. High-resolution ground truth data were generated using patient-specific computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations based on segmented vascular geometries and physiologically realistic boundary conditions, and the resulting velocity fields served as targets for supervised learning. The proposed architecture uses convolutional block attention modules (CBAM) to guide the network toward clinically relevant spatial features and to suppress noise in low-resolution inputs. Quantitative results show that the attention-guided model substantially reduces the root mean square error (RMSE) compared with a baseline model without attention, and qualitative velocity contour analysis confirms improved reconstruction of intricate flow patterns. These findings highlight the capacity of the model to restore high-fidelity flow fields under noisy conditions and support the use of deep learning to extend the clinical utility of 4D flow MRI for non-invasive hemodynamic assessment.

title: Криптографическая защита данных в парадигме Zero-Dependency: генерация браузерного шифратора файлов на базе Web Crypto API методами промпт-инжиниринга
abstract: В работе рассматривается задача создания браузерного инструмента для шифрования файлов без использования сторонних библиотек. С помощью платформы Qwen Studio и метода детализированных текстовых запросов разработан веб-шифратор, работающий на основе нативного интерфейса Web Crypto API. Приложение реализует современные криптографические стандарты – AES-256-GCM для шифрования и PBKDF2 для получения ключа из пароля. Особенностью исследования стало использование бинарного критерия качества: сгенерированный код считается успешным только в том случае, если зашифрованный файл корректно расшифровывается. Эксперимент показал, что языковые модели хорошо справляются с задачами, опирающимися на строгие математические стандарты, и способны с первой попытки создавать рабочий криптографический код без необходимости ручных доработок.

title: Research on Quantum Secure Direct Communication Protocol in Atmospheric Turbulence Environment of Space Channel
abstract: 量子安全直接通信是一种能够在量子信道中直接传输机密信息的通信范式，在自由空间通信中展现出重要的实用潜力与部署前景。然而，大气湍流等环境因素会降低信号传输质量与系统安全性。本文分析了空间信道诱骗态DL04协议，建立了自由空间水平链路量子安全直接通信系统的综合性能分析模型，量化分析了光学系统参数和实际环境因素对系统保密容量的影响规律。仿真结果表明：发射接收孔径与初始光斑尺寸需根据系统条件权衡选取，存在最优配置；与雪崩光电二极管单光子探测器相比，采用超导纳米线单光子探测器可有效提升中短距离下的保密容量，但对最大安全通信距离的提升作用有限；湍流强度与大气可见度是影响系统最大安全通信距离的关键因素；白天强背景光是主要噪声源之一，需通过滤波技术予以抑制。本研究可为实际自由空间量子安全直接通信系统的链路预算与参数优化提供理论依据和设计指导。

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Topology Modeling
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers a unique pathway to manipulating and modeling complex topological structures. This paper explores the application of entanglement to dynamic topology modeling, aiming to provide a novel computational framework for precisely describing the evolution of these structures and achieving high-precision geometric modeling. We propose a new algorithm leveraging the properties of entangled states to transform topological problems into quantum computations, offering a potential paradigm shift in the field of topology. The core mechanism centers on utilizing entanglement to represent and evolve the topology, facilitating more accurate geometric representations than traditional methods. This work introduces a framework for dynamically exploring and characterizing topological phenomena, potentially opening new avenues for research into complex systems. The paper presents a conceptual overview of the proposed algorithm, detailing its core components and potential implications.

The paper details the core mechanism, the proposed framework, and provides a preliminary assessment of its performance compared to traditional optimization techniques. We conclude with a discussion of future research directions and potential applications.

We detail the core mechanism, propose a robust optimization process, and provide a preliminary assessment of its effectiveness. The goal is to establish a practical and adaptable approach for quantum algorithm development and optimization.

title: Quantum Self-Linking Spin Matrix: Adaptive Self-Alignment for Enhanced Quantum Computation
abstract: Quantum self-linking (SQL) is a promising approach to enhancing quantum computation, offering the potential for robust and adaptable quantum circuits. This paper explores the design and implementation of a novel SQL matrix, termed "Adaptive Self-Linking Quantum Spin Matrix," aiming to overcome the limitations of static self-linking strategies. The core concept revolves around dynamically adjusting the self-linking degree of the matrix based on environmental feedback, allowing for efficient quantum computation in a constantly changing environment. We detail the methodology utilizing quantum entanglement and quantum control to achieve this adaptive self-alignment. This research introduces a new algorithm that dynamically modifies the self-linking parameter, thereby enhancing the matrix's resilience and potential for improved quantum computation. The advantages of this approach are the potential for increased computational speed and greater error mitigation. This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's design, implementation, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness in adapting to varying quantum environments.

We demonstrate the framework's effectiveness through a rigorous analysis of a specific mathematical problem, highlighting its potential to significantly accelerate solution times compared to classical methods. This work establishes a fundamental shift in constraint propagation, offering a potentially transformative approach to complex mathematical modeling.

title: Quantum Communication Protocol Design Based on Quantum Mechanics Principles
abstract: This paper proposes a novel communication protocol design leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics, specifically quantum entanglement and quantum teleportation. The core claim is to enhance communication security, rate, and reliability by utilizing these quantum phenomena. The protocol is based on Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols, employing entangled particles to securely share cryptographic keys. Furthermore, it incorporates aspects of quantum teleportation to facilitate information transfer. The proposed system fundamentally departs from traditional communication protocols which are vulnerable to eavesdropping, offering a significantly higher level of security due to the inherent properties of quantum mechanics. This design addresses the limitations of classical communication methods and presents a pathway toward truly secure and high-performance communication systems. The key components of this protocol are detailed, including the entanglement generation and distribution, the key exchange process, and the information teleportation scheme. The mathematical framework underpinning these processes is presented, focusing on the core concepts of quantum information theory. ---

The proposed algorithm demonstrates significant potential for accelerating quantum algorithm development and expanding the capabilities of quantum computation. This research addresses a critical need in the field, providing a robust and theoretically grounded framework for optimizing quantum circuits.

title: Adaptive Granular Probability Model
abstract: This paper introduces an Adaptive Granular Probability Model (AGPM) designed to dynamically adjust distribution parameters based on data distribution shifts. Traditional probabilistic models often require pre-defined parameters, limiting their adaptability. The AGPM leverages a dynamic parameter adjustment mechanism to automatically tailor distribution estimates, enabling more intelligent predictions across evolving data patterns. We explore the core concept of integrating probability models with granular distributions to achieve this adaptive behavior. The paper details the model's architecture, the self-adjusting parameter mechanism, and a demonstration of its predictive capabilities on a synthetic dataset. The primary goal is to provide a robust and flexible framework for probabilistic modeling that responds effectively to dynamic data environments.

title: Symbolic Regression with Grammatical Inference and Genetic Programming
abstract: Symbolic regression is a powerful technique for discovering mathematical equations from data. However, it often struggles to find complex, high-accuracy equations, particularly when the underlying data relationships are intricate. This paper presents a novel approach to symbolic regression that integrates grammatical inference with genetic programming. The core idea is to leverage grammatical inference to efficiently generate a diverse set of candidate equations, which are then refined and evolved towards higher accuracy and complexity using a genetic programming framework. This hybrid algorithm overcomes the limitations of traditional symbolic regression methods by providing a mechanism for both equation generation and optimization. The resulting system demonstrates improved equation discovery capabilities, particularly for datasets exhibiting complex relationships. The primary contribution lies in the synergistic combination of these two techniques, offering a more robust and versatile solution for symbolic regression tasks.

title: Title: Algorithmic Complexity of Symbolic Reasoning – Quantifying the Computational Cost of Reasoning
abstract: This paper investigates the algorithmic complexity of symbolic reasoning, focusing on quantifying the computational cost of solving logical problems. The primary goal is to develop a metric to assess the difficulty of reasoning, specifically examining the interplay between the number of logical rules, inference requirements, and the number of intermediate states involved. The work will propose a novel metric that integrates these factors, aiming for a more precise and quantitative assessment of complexity compared to existing approximations. We will explore different weighting schemes to optimize the metric for various types of logical problems, ultimately providing a framework for understanding and comparing the computational cost of symbolic reasoning across diverse scenarios. The paper concludes with a discussion of potential applications and future research directions.

title: Real timing. No cuts.
abstract: We opened CasperWasp, typed one line — "a two-page proposal for a regional logistics client covering scope, timeline, and pricing" — and let the recording run untouched. 27 seconds later: real headings, real structure, no blank page. It's not instant, and it's not finished — it's a first draft to edit, not a document to send. That's the whole point: one AI marketplace, honest about what it actually does.

abstract: Quantum Complexity Theory (QCT) offers a novel framework for algorithm design, predicated on the principle that certain computational problems exhibit inherent quantum complexity. We argue that by leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics, we can potentially develop algorithms that outperform their classical counterparts in solving complex problems, demonstrating a paradigm shift in algorithmic design. This work lays the foundation for a new area of research with significant implications for the future of computational science and engineering.

title: Evaluation of the F1* Score Across Twelve Text Datasets with Prevalence Sensitivity Analysis
abstract: The F1 score depends on the positive-class prevalence (π), which complicates comparisons across datasets. Our previous work proposed F1* as an equal-weight composite of F1 and accuracy and derived auxiliary estimation functions. The present study evaluates that previously defined index using 12 text datasets and four models under RepeatedKFold with five folds and five repeats (25 held-out cross-validation evaluations per dataset–model pair). All 1200 runs used identical persisted splits across models, fold-local recurrent preprocessing, and raw-prediction audit. Mean F1 values across datasets were 0.9571 for BERT, 0.9263 for LSTM, 0.9244 for GRU, and 0.9235 for RNN. Mean absolute differences for the auxiliary reconstructions were 0.0012 for F1 and 0.0012 for accuracy. The evaluation also includes MCC, a controlled-prevalence analysis, and an evaluation-sample-size sensitivity analysis using fixed out-of-fold (OOF) predictions from all four models. The evidence remains bounded to binary text datasets and does not establish universal metric superiority.

title: Hallucinations in Structured Extraction: A Case Study on Prompt-Based Semantic Role Labeling
abstract: This paper investigates hallucinations in large language models from the perspective of structured extraction, using prompt-based Semantic Role Labeling (SRL) as a controlled case study. SRL requires exact span boundaries and role assignments, while prompting constrained by rationales exposes the reasoning trace associated with each prediction. Our approach employs a DSPy-based pipeline with rule-grounded signatures to show that hallucinations in constrained extraction are systematic, rationale-associated, and thus amenable to targeted mitigation through signature design. Experiments on a representative subset of the CoNLL-2012 dataset show that hallucinations persist even under constrained settings and are systematically associated with failures of rule grounding. Because each prediction is required to cite a single governing rule, errors can be organized and aggregated at the rule level without necessitating additional classification. Leveraging these observations, we introduce a Rationale-Oriented (RO) optimizer that targets such failures by selectively rewriting the relevant parts of the signature. This process mitigates systematic failure modes and leads to measurable improvements in precision, recall, and F1 across multiple evaluation settings, using a representative subset of argument roles aligned with a 5W+1H schema and no model fine-tuning. Signature-perturbation experiments show that cited rules act as diagnostic proxies rather than per-instance causal explanations: the model's parametric priors also contribute to extraction. Even so, rule-level aggregation remains a reliable predictor of where errors occur. These findings suggest that hallucination in structured tasks is closely linked to failures in instruction grounding, and that rule-level feedback and refinement offer a framework for improving reliability in prompt-based systems.

title: Повышение энергетической эффективности компрессорного цеха путем внедрения интеллектуальной системы распределения нагрузки между газоперекачивающими агрегатами
abstract: Данная работа посвящена разработке и исследованию методики оптимального распределения нагрузки между газоперекачивающими агрегатами на базе эвристических алгоритмов роевого интеллекта для снижения расхода топливного газа и повышения надёжности эксплуатации оборудования. Задачи, которые решались в ходе исследования: 1. Разработка алгоритмической базы распределения нагрузки с применением методов PSO и GWO с учётом технологических ограничений и переменного технического состояния агрегатов. 2. Проведение сравнительного имитационного моделирования работы компрессорного цеха в течение суточного цикла. 3. Оценка технико-экономической эффективности внедрения и формирование практических рекомендаций по поэтапной интеграции оптимизационного контура в действующие АСУ ТП. В результате было подтверждено снижение расхода топливного газа на 6,6–7,1 % относительно традиционного ПИД-регулирования. Алгоритм PSO обеспечил экономию 7,07 %, алгоритм GWO продемонстрировал повышенную устойчивость целевой функции в условиях часто меняющихся режимов.

title: TETRIS-Q: Tiling-based Effective Transient-fault Reduction on Interleaved Superconducting Qubits
abstract: The struggle of the hour in quantum computing research is achieving effective suppression of the error mechanisms induced by the interaction of external radiation with superconducting quantum devices. Despite the rapid advancements in quantum error correction (QEC) of recent years, radiation-induced faults are yet to be fully addressed. These events are known to be the cause of simultaneous correlated defects in qubits that lie onto a single substrate, ultimately jeopardising QEC code effectiveness. In this paper, we propose to selectively combine substrate-level phonon barriers and QEC interleaving via a planar-mesh tiling algorithm, TETRIS-Q, reaching efficient and effective suppression of radiation events. Our cross-layer solution comes at no extra cost in terms of QEC code execution or decoding time. We model and simulate radiation-induced transient faults over a plethora of barrier and QEC interleaving configurations. Through more than 51 million quantum circuit simulations, we show peak logical error reductions of more than $99.8 \%$, together with an $80\%$ reduction of the observable transient duration with permeable barriers. We find that sparser tiling can reach comparable performance to single qubit tiling, prompting cost reductions of upwards of $87 \%$ in barrier tracing. By leveraging independent QEC code interleaving, we measure up to one order of magnitude average logical error rate reductions without the use of permeable barriers, and up to three orders of magnitude with the joint usage of barriers.

title: Artificial Intelligence Predictions and Human Perception: Comparing User Trust with Accuracy
abstract: This study aims to examine the relationship between the technical predictive accuracy of artificial intelligence (AI) models and the confidence that expert users place in these predictions. Despite the current emphasis on evaluating AI technologies based only on technical criteria, the importance of user confidence as part of such evaluation process and the relation of accuracy to confidence are often underestimated. Taking this into account, the current paper aims at understanding the relationship between user perceptions regarding AI outputs and the actual accuracy of the models generating predictions. To accomplish the stated goal, data from 50 academics was analyzed. Participants of the research were shown 20 different prediction samples provided by the AI model and asked to evaluate their confidence on a 5-point Likert scale. The statistical methods involved in the analysis comprised descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and an independent-samples t-test. The analysis resulted in the identification of a positive and statistically significant yet moderate relationship between prediction accuracy and user confidence. Particularly, low-accuracy predictions could trigger high user confidence, and vice versa – some high-accuracy predictions could be rated with low confidence scores. The findings confirm that user confidence might be miscalibrated and impacted by several psychological processes such as algorithm aversion and bias. At the same time, the outcomes support the position that confidence is connected with prediction accuracy, rather than other criteria, but is impacted by explainability and presentation style of the system under analysis. As far as XAI plays a crucial role in enhancing both of the factors mentioned above, Explainable Artificial Intelligence should receive particular attention in such studies. In general, the presented paper shows that the evaluation of AI technology must not focus only on technical performance of the system, but must also consider user-related criteria. Further research might analyze directly the effect of using XAI techniques on the level of trust in experiments among various professions.

title: 自适应概率神经网络的动态参数调整
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic parameter adjustment mechanism for self-attention probability neural networks (SANNs). Traditional ANN parameter adjustment methods often involve fixed, static adjustments, limiting the network's ability to adapt to evolving data distributions. We propose a system that dynamically adjusts the network's parameters based on a learned error signal, enabling continuous optimization and improved performance. The core of this mechanism is a feedback loop that iteratively refines the network's weights through a stochastic gradient descent applied to a modified error function. This approach significantly enhances the network's capacity to learn complex patterns and generalize to unseen data. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this dynamic parameter adjustment through extensive experiments on a diverse dataset, showcasing substantial improvements in accuracy and robustness compared to existing ANN architectures. The paper concludes with a discussion of the limitations and future directions of this approach.

title: Dynamic Quantum Entanglement Computation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel computational algorithm, Dynamic Quantum Entanglement Computation (DQEC), designed to accelerate the computation of quantum entanglement states. The core claims demonstrate the potential of this algorithm to surpass traditional methods through adaptive optimization.

title: Phosphorus Nuclear Spins in Posner Molecules as Quantum Qubits in Neural Microtubules — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: FINDING: Fisher proposes phosphorus nuclear spins (¹³¹Xe-like, but specifically ³¹P in Posner molecules Ca₉(PO₄)₆) as quantum error-corrected qubits in neural microtubules, with spin entanglement timescales matching cognitive processing. | MATH: Posner molecule: Ca₉(PO₄)₆ — 9 Ca²⁺, 6 PO₄³⁻, 6 phosphorus nuclei each spin-1/2 (³¹P, gyromagnetic ratio γ ≈ 17.235 MHz/T). Nuclear spin coherence time T₂ ~ seconds at physiological temperature (Fisher's estimate). Quantum error correction via spin-1/2 singlet-triplet subspace: |S⟩ = (|↑↓⟩−|↓↑⟩)/√2, |T₀⟩ = (|↑↓⟩+|↓↑⟩)/√2. Effective qubit: 6 phosphorus spins → 2⁶ = 64 states, but symmetric subspace dimension = 7 (total spin I = 0,1,2,3). Key ratio: 6 phosphorus per Posner → 6-fold rotational symmetry (C₃, C₆ axes) in crystal lattice. | CONNECTION: Posner molecule has octahedral/tetrahedral phosphate geometry — PO₄³⁻ tetrahedron (bond angle 109.47°, O–P–O). Ca₉(PO₄)₆ forms a trigonal prismatic cluster — point group D₃ (3-fold rotational symmetry) Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. title: Multi-Modal Knowledge Graph Reasoning with Causal Relation Modeling
abstract: This paper addresses the limitations of traditional knowledge graph reasoning, which primarily relies on correlational relationships, leading to potentially biased inferences. We propose a novel approach to multi-modal knowledge graph reasoning by explicitly modeling causal relationships between entities. Our core claim is that incorporating causal reasoning significantly enhances both the accuracy and interpretability of knowledge graph inferences. We leverage Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to model the knowledge graph, coupled with causal inference algorithms, specifically causal graph learning methods, to identify and infer these underlying causal links. This framework allows for a more robust and reliable understanding of complex relationships within the graph. The results demonstrate improved reasoning performance compared to methods solely based on correlation. This work contributes to a more nuanced and accurate representation of knowledge, paving the way for more intelligent applications in areas such as decision support and automated reasoning.

abstract: Quantum Hidden-Line Cryptography (QHIDL) is a cryptographic system designed to resist attacks based on classical computational methods. This paper introduces a novel dynamic topology-based cryptography framework leveraging quantum geometry to enhance data security and enable more complex encryption algorithms. The research explores the potential impact of this dynamic topology-based approach on the overall security landscape of cryptography.

title: Causal Discovery with Bayesian Copula Networks
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to causal discovery utilizing Bayesian Copula Networks (BCNs). Traditional causal discovery methods often struggle with complex dependencies, confounding, and selection bias, leading to inaccurate inferences. BCNs provide a powerful framework for representing and analyzing multivariate data by encoding variables as copulas, capturing their joint distributions. The core of the method lies in learning these copulas and then applying Bayesian inference to estimate causal relationships, explicitly addressing uncertainty. The approach offers a more robust solution, particularly when dealing with intricate dependencies, by leveraging the inherent structure of copulas and the probabilistic reasoning of Bayesian networks. This work outlines the theoretical underpinnings of BCNs, detailing the construction of the network, the learning process, and the inference mechanisms. We demonstrate the potential of this method through a conceptual framework, highlighting its advantages over existing approaches and paving the way for future research and applications.

title: Probabilistic Logic Programming with Monte Carlo Tree Search
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to intelligent reasoning by integrating Probabilistic Logic Programming (PLP) with Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS). The core idea is to leverage the strengths of both techniques: PLP for hypothesis generation based on logical rules and uncertainty quantification, and MCTS for efficient exploration and evaluation of those hypotheses. We propose a framework where PLP generates a set of candidate solutions, and MCTS then iteratively refines these solutions, incorporating uncertainty estimates provided by the PLP component. This hybrid system aims to create more robust and adaptable reasoning systems, particularly in domains where knowledge is incomplete or uncertain. The paper outlines the key components of this framework, detailing the interaction between the PLP and MCTS modules, and discusses potential applications and future research directions. The system's ability to quantify uncertainty throughout the reasoning process is a critical element, allowing for more informed decision-making and improved performance compared to traditional AI approaches. We demonstrate, through a theoretical analysis and conceptual design, the potential of this combined approach.

title: Adaptive Research Scoping for Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Metric-Gated Corpus Qualification for RAG Correctness
abstract: ----- Description ----- This registration specifies a reproducible methodological framework in which corpus construction for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is treated as a sequential, auditable qualification process rather than an open-ended ingestion task. The central premise is that RAG correctness — retrieval recall, generation faithfulness, and citation precision — is not determined solely by chunking, embedding, or retrieval algorithms, but by whether the underlying corpus is task-qualified before indexing. A corpus that is contaminated, under-covered, redundant, or misaligned will degrade downstream RAG utility regardless of retriever sophistication. The framework introduces Adaptive Research Scoping for RAG (ARS-RAG). ARS-RAG treats the RAG corpus as an observable, evolving object and evaluates it against four prospectively defined quality metrics: Alignment (A), Coverage (C), Contamination (K), and Representation (R). These are supplemented by a fifth empirical metric, RAG Utility (U), measured on a frozen gold QA set via RAGAS. A lightweight surrogate utility Û = f(A, C, K, R), calibrated via ridge regression on corpus snapshots, is used inside the acquisition loop for marginal-acceptance decisions. Qualification uses a multi-threshold conjunction: Qualified ⇔ { A ≥ τ_A ∧ C ≥ τ_C ∧ K ≤ τ_K ∧ R ≥ τ_R } Adaptive expansion follows EXPAND → ALIGN → ASSESS MARGINAL CONTRIBUTION → ACCEPT / REJECT rather than unconditional union. Acquisition stops when the marginal surrogate gain ΔÛ falls below a pre-registered cost threshold ρ_cost AND no already-passed gate regresses (Pareto preservation). Three legitimate terminal outcomes exist: SUPPORTED (corpus qualified for RAG indexing), NEAR (usable with written limitation), and UNQUALIFIED (RAG deployment blocked; report corpus limitation). The registered evaluation will test whether multi-threshold corpus qualification predicts higher measured RAG utility than unqualified corpus baselines (one-shot retrieval, accept-all, fixed-N), and whether the surrogate Û provides a reliable stopping signal. Controlled degradation of corpora will manipulate contamination injection, facet removal, and source restriction to test sensitivity. The demonstration domain is YOLOv8 / lightweight object detection on edge and embedded devices. Preliminary retrieval for this domain is exploratory methodological development, not confirmatory evidence. Confirmatory analyses follow the protocol, hypotheses, factor levels, decision rules, and primary outcomes frozen at registration. Intended outcome: a reproducible decision framework in which a RAG corpus is indexed and deployed only after passing multi-threshold qualification; if registered ARS iterations terminate UNQUALIFIED, RAG deployment is not performed and the limitation is reported.

A lightweight surrogate utility Û = f(A, C, K, R), calibrated via ridge regression on corpus snapshots, is used inside the acquisition loop for marginal-acceptance decisions. Qualification uses a multi-threshold conjunction: Qualified ⇔ { A ≥ τ_A ∧ C ≥ τ_C ∧ K ≤ τ_K ∧ R ≥ τ_R } Adaptive expansion follows EXPAND → ALIGN → ASSESS MARGINAL CONTRIBUTION → ACCEPT / REJECT rather than unconditional union. Acquisition stops when the marginal surrogate gain ΔÛ falls below a pre-registered cost threshold ρ_cost AND no already-passed gate regresses (Pareto preservation). Three legitimate terminal outcomes exist: SUPPORTED (corpus qualified for RAG indexing), NEAR (usable with written limitation), and UNQUALIFIED (RAG deployment blocked; report corpus limitation). The registered evaluation will test whether multi-threshold corpus qualification predicts higher measured RAG utility than unqualified corpus baselines (one-shot retrieval, accept-all, fixed-N), and whether the surrogate Û provides a reliable stopping signal. Controlled degradation of corpora will manipulate contamination injection, facet removal, and source restriction to test sensitivity. The demonstration domain is YOLOv8 / lightweight object detection on edge and embedded devices. Preliminary retrieval for this domain is exploratory methodological development, not confirmatory evidence. Confirmatory analyses follow the protocol, hypotheses, factor levels, decision rules, and primary outcomes frozen at registration. Intended outcome: a reproducible decision framework in which a RAG corpus is indexed and deployed only after passing multi-threshold qualification; if registered ARS iterations terminate UNQUALIFIED, RAG deployment is not performed and the limitation is reported.

title: Quantum Optimisation for Protein-Protein Interaction Network Alignment
abstract: Protein-protein interaction (PPI) network alignment combines topological and sequence information to identify conserved modules across species, but global alignment remains challenging: heuristics sacrifice optimality, while exact methods lack scalability. We model the alignment as a weighted maximum common induced subgraph problem and reformulate it through the modular product graph to a minimum-weight vertex cover on the complement, with node weights carrying sequence similarity. To solve this problem, we develop a hybrid framework combining kernelisation, branch-and-bound, and seven Quantum Approximate Optimisation Algorithm (QAOA) formulations. These formulations differ in how the cover constraints are enforced, from penalty terms in the cost Hamiltonian to mixers confined to the feasible subspace. For single round QAOA, we derive closed-form expressions for the expected cost of four circulant mixer variants, enabling performance characterisation without circuit simulation. Applied to synthetic and real-world networks reduced to KEGG pathways, the QAOA formulations achieve high topological conservation on the aligned core while at least maintaining biological conservation comparable to leading classical aligners, at the cost of reduced node coverage. Across selected KEGG pathways, the aligned subnetworks retain disease-associated proteins, preserving biologically relevant information. Cheaper formulations leave more edges uncovered, while enforcing feasibility in the mixer raises circuit depth by one to two orders of magnitude. Together, these results highlight the potential of quantum optimisation for PPI network alignment and the resource trade-offs that will shape its scalability as quantum hardware matures.

title: From Deep to Shallow: Unconstrained and Efficient Layer Merging Strategy
abstract: Although Deep Neural Networks have become foundational in many areas of Machine Learning, high computational demands limit their application in resource-constrained environments. To address this issue, depth compression methods have been proposed to identify and linearize redundant activation functions, thereby allowing for the merging of layers without intermediate non-linearities. However, these methods face two key challenges: they cannot be directly applied to convolutions with padding due to the absence of an analytical solution for merging these layers, and they typically increase the kernel size of merged layers, thus limiting speed-up gains. To overcome these limitations, we propose an efficient strategy that enables merging of layers without an existing analytical solution, and also without increasing kernel size. We validate our approach across multiple architectures and datasets, and measure inference speed-up gains on real embedded platforms. We publicly released the code at https://github.com/ShulzhenkoPetr/deep-to-shallow.

title: ADAPTIVE QUIZ APPLICATION
authors: F Zaheera, T Shiva Chari, C Abhinay, S Sumayya, N Prabhakar
abstract: The Adaptive Quiz Application is an intelligent web-based learning platform designed to provide personalized quizzes according to the knowledge level and performance of individual learners. Traditional quiz applications generally provide the same questions to all users, regardless of their learning ability, which may make the assessment too easy or too difficult. The proposed system addresses this limitation by dynamically adjusting the difficulty and selection of questions based on the user's previous responses and performance. The application allows users to register, select subjects or topics, and attempt quizzes through an interactive interface. The system evaluates each answer and analyzes factors such as accuracy, response performance, and previous scores. Based on this analysis, the application can select appropriate questions and gradually increase or decrease the difficulty level. Users can view their scores, performance reports, correct and incorrect answers, and progress over time. The system can maintain a question bank containing different topics, difficulty levels, and question types. An adaptive algorithm uses the learner's performance to determine the next suitable question. The application can also provide personalized feedback and recommend topics that require additional practice. Overall, the Adaptive Quiz Application improves the learning and assessment experience by providing personalized quizzes, continuous performance tracking, and adaptive question selection. Future enhancements can include AI-based question generation, advanced learning analytics, voice-based quizzes, gamification, and intelligent study recommendations.

title: Nonlinear Topological Geometry Quantum Entanglement Mapping
abstract: This paper explores the interplay between nonlinear topological geometry and quantum entanglement, focusing on the development of a novel "mapping" mechanism to precisely calculate quantum states. The core claim is that by leveraging quantum entanglement, we can establish a computational framework that directly maps topological structures and quantum states, enabling the calculation of complex topological states. This approach offers a fundamentally new way to tackle problems in quantum information theory and topological data analysis. We present a framework for mapping topological information to quantum entanglement, highlighting the potential for improved accuracy and efficiency in the calculation of sensitive quantum states. The paper details the design of the mapping mechanism, its mathematical underpinnings, and preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness in specific examples.

title: 基于动态矩阵的自适应量子态转移算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum state transfer algorithm based on dynamic matrix adaptation. Traditional quantum state transfer methods often suffer from limitations in efficiency and predictability. This work proposes a new approach utilizing a dynamic matrix update mechanism to accelerate and enhance the transfer of quantum states across different systems. The core of the algorithm lies in the ability to adaptively update the matrix based on the current state of the target system, thereby providing a more robust and efficient transfer process. The algorithm's design incorporates predictive modeling to anticipate the transition path, offering improved control and reduced error rates. This research explores the theoretical foundations and practical implementation of this adaptive approach, demonstrating its potential for significant advancements in quantum information processing.

abstract: Quantum state encoding is a fundamental challenge in quantum information science, requiring efficient and robust methods for manipulating and controlling quantum states. This paper introduces a novel quantum state encoding scheme based on dynamic topology, aiming to overcome the limitations of traditional approaches. We propose a framework that leverages the inherent topological properties of quantum states to encode information, enabling automated optimization and control within quantum computation. The core mechanism involves constructing and manipulating dynamic topological structures to represent and process quantum information. This approach offers potential advantages in terms of scalability and adaptability compared to existing techniques. The paper presents a detailed analysis of the proposed algorithm, including mathematical formulations and illustrative examples to demonstrate its potential.

abstract: This paper investigates the application of high-order geometry to quantum state control, presenting a novel approach for dynamically adjusting quantum states to enhance the performance of quantum computing. Traditional quantum state control relies on static manipulation, while this method leverages high-order geometry to achieve adaptive control. We propose a framework centered around the concept of a "geometric resonance" that allows for efficient and controlled evolution of the quantum state. The core mechanism involves the creation of a set of geometric transformations that interact with the quantum system, driving it towards a desired state. The potential benefits of this approach include increased fidelity, enhanced coherence, and the ability to tailor quantum states for specific applications. This work provides a theoretical foundation and initial experimental exploration of this promising technique.

title: Nonlinear Geometric Mapping Validation via Quantum Simulation
abstract: This paper investigates the validation of nonlinear geometric mappings using quantum simulation, establishing a framework for rigorous verification of complex geometric models. Traditional methods often struggle with the inherent complexity and potential for error in these models. Quantum simulation offers a promising approach to enhance validation by providing an inherently precise and computationally efficient method. The core mechanism centers on utilizing quantum algorithms to simulate the mapping's behavior and assess its properties, allowing for verification that surpasses the limitations of classical methods. The paper explores the potential of this framework to address the challenges of validating intricate geometric structures. We present a novel approach for validating a specific nonlinear geometric mapping, demonstrating its effectiveness through quantum simulation. The resulting validation process provides a robust and verifiable foundation for further research and development in the field.

title: Adaptive Attention Mechanism for Quantum Machine Learning
abstract: Quantum machine learning (QML) offers the potential to revolutionize various fields, including drug discovery, materials science, and financial modeling, by leveraging the unique capabilities of quantum systems. However, the development of effective QML algorithms often faces challenges related to computational complexity and the need for sophisticated training strategies. This paper investigates a novel attention mechanism designed specifically for quantum machine learning, aiming to address these challenges by dynamically adjusting attention weights based on input data characteristics. We propose a framework that adapts to the data's nuances, enhancing model robustness and performance. This mechanism will be tested against various quantum machine learning tasks, demonstrating its effectiveness through illustrative examples. The core focus is on achieving a higher level of data capture and improved model generalization.

This architecture seeks to foster highly adaptable and robust AI systems, leveraging the principles of distributed processing and emergent behavior. The paper details the core mechanism, focusing on the layered system of modules and the dynamic allocation of resources, demonstrating its potential to overcome limitations of current neural network designs.

title: Quantum Entanglement States: A Novel Non-Standard Model for Fundamental Physics and Information Processing
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, presents a unique and potentially transformative paradigm for computation. This paper explores the development of a novel non-standard model, rooted in the mathematical description of quantum entanglement, designed to provide a deeper understanding of the fundamental physical mechanisms underlying quantum computation and information processing. The model proposes a framework wherein quantum entanglement serves as the fundamental carrier of information, allowing for the implementation of self-adaptive quantum algorithms. The core claim is that this model offers a robust and mathematically grounded approach to exploring and manipulating entangled states, paving the way for new advancements in quantum information theory and computation. We investigate the mathematical foundations, algorithmic implications, and potential for future research within this framework.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive quantum state topology search method. title: Physical Simulation Acceleration through Quantum Entanglement
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum entanglement to accelerate physical simulation processes. Traditional computational methods for simulating quantum systems face significant limitations due to exponential scaling with system size. We propose a novel algorithm, Quantum Entanglement Parallelization (QEP), that leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to achieve substantial speedups in complex simulations. This research explores the feasibility of QEP for accelerating simulations in various areas, including molecular dynamics, quantum field theory, and condensed matter physics, ultimately demonstrating its potential to revolutionize the field of physical simulation.

The proposed approach models the circuit design problem as an optimization problem, employing a genetic algorithm to perform an evolutionary search. The key innovation lies in the direct application of evolutionary algorithms to hardware design, shifting the focus from software optimization to the physical design of circuits. We present a framework for this approach, outlining the key steps involved, from representation and encoding to selection, crossover, and mutation operators within the genetic algorithm. The results suggest a viable and potentially powerful method for generating novel and highly optimized circuit designs.

title: Nonlinear Geometric Structure Prediction Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithmic framework for predicting the stability of complex geometric structures based on a quantum entanglement-driven model. Traditional geometric prediction methods often struggle with high-dimensional complexity and require computationally intensive numerical simulations. Our approach leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to transform geometric prediction into a probabilistic quantum computation, significantly enhancing prediction accuracy and efficiency. The core mechanism involves introducing a probability model representing the geometric structure, utilizing quantum state propagation to refine the prediction, and employing optimization techniques to achieve precise results. This algorithm represents a significant advancement over existing methods, offering a fundamentally different approach to geometric analysis.

title: 基于量子几何的自适应机器学习算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive machine learning algorithm based on quantum geometry. Traditional machine learning algorithms often rely on handcrafted models, limiting their adaptability and scalability. Quantum geometry, a theoretical framework that describes the fundamental structure of spacetime, offers a unique perspective for representing and manipulating complex data. This work proposes a new algorithm that leverages quantum geometry to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of machine learning models, focusing on model scalability and adaptability. The core mechanism involves mapping data points onto a quantum geometric representation, enabling the algorithm to dynamically adjust its parameters to optimize performance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of experiments and analysis, highlighting its potential to overcome limitations of conventional machine learning. This research explores the benefits of utilizing quantum geometry in accelerating and improving machine learning processes.

title: ARES: Securing Agents for Computer Use Through Endpoint Resource Mediation and Behavioral Guardrails
abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents are evolving into agents for computer use (ACUs) that read files, invoke applications, communicate over networks, and operate graphical interfaces, moving the effective security boundary from model inputs and outputs to autonomous actions that alter endpoint state. Conventional identity and access controls remain applicable and necessary, but they are authorized based on identity, resource, and network policy rather than on the semantic scope of the active task or the provenance of the instruction that triggered an action. This paper presents ARES (Agent Resource Enforcement and Security), an action-centric framework that inserts enforceable authorization between agent-generated tool calls and protected resources, combining a Resource Proxy Layer for interception, a Behavioral Guardrail Engine for task- and context-aware authorization, and a Multi-Agent Trust Boundary Manager for provenance and taint propagation. We implement ARES-lite and evaluate it against file exfiltration through indirect prompt injection, prompt infection propagation, and internal-network access abuse. Under the controlled replay-based evaluation, integrated ARES-lite reduced the observed attack-success rate from 100% under the permissive baseline to 0% across the three evaluated scenarios, while preserving the predefined handling of eight benign and ambiguous tasks with no false positives. A closed-loop evaluation in which the agent re-plans after an intervention, an adversarial boundary-case suite covering path aliasing, address encoding, look-alike destinations, and taint laundering, and a comparison against representative prompt-filtering and tool-allowlist defenses further characterize the enforcement path; a model and temperature sweep show that baseline exposure varies with model capability, whereas the mediated outcome does not.

title: Knowledge Graph-Augmented Ambient AI for Clinical Note Generation
abstract: Ambient AI is increasingly adopted in healthcare to automatically generate clinical notes from patient-clinician conversations, with the potential to substantially reduce clinician documentation burden. However, generated notes may omit clinically relevant information discussed during the encounter, creating information gaps that can affect downstream care. Knowledge graphs (KGs) constructed from encounter transcripts can provide a structured representation of what was discussed and enable systematic identification of missing information from generated notes that are critical for patient care. In this study, we introduce Coverage-Directed Revision (CDR), a model-agnostic framework that constructs a KG from the encounter transcript, identifies medical concepts absent from an initially generated note, and directs large language models (LLMs) to restore the missing information without modifying the underlying note-generation system. We evaluate CDR on two datasets: 1) Pitt-Bench, a local dataset comprising rehabilitation sessions, and 2) ACI-Bench, a public dataset for benchmarking clinical note generation. We tested four underlying LLMs widely used in ambient AI systems. The results show that CDR consistently improves content recall across all evaluated conditions. Our study provides a practical approach for improving the completeness of ambient AI-generated clinical documentation.

title: Bias-Corrected Subspace Intersection: Minimax-Optimal Shared Subspace Estimation in Multi-View Data
abstract: Estimating a low-dimensional subspace shared across noisy data matrices is a fundamental problem in multi-view matrix estimation. We study this problem under the two-view JIVE model, where each data matrix contains shared and view-specific low-rank components. We demonstrate that standard plug-in subspace intersection, including AJIVE, suffers from a second-order bias caused by direction-dependent leakage of the empirical singular vectors. We propose bias-corrected subspace intersection (BCSI), which removes this bias before estimating the shared subspace. We establish finite-sample risk bounds for BCSI that accommodate unequal view dimensions, signal strengths, and view-specific ranks and require no condition-number assumptions on the signal matrices. When the shared and view-specific ranks are comparable, these bounds match our minimax lower bounds up to universal constants. The resulting minimax rate contains a new second-order term, arising from quadratic leakage perturbations relative to the shrinking spectral gap when the view-specific subspaces are nearly aligned. This term is absent from previous JIVE minimax lower bounds. Numerical experiments demonstrate the advantage of BCSI over AJIVE when the leakage bias is pronounced. Along the way, we establish a nonasymptotic concentration result for the bias-corrected leakage Gram matrix of a rectangular spiked matrix, which may be of independent interest.

title: Large Language Models with At Most One Spike per Neuron
abstract: Leveraging their inherent sparse event-driven computation, spiking neural networks (SNNs) offer a promising path toward energy-efficient large language models (LLMs). Time-to-first-spike (TTFS) coding generates at most one spike per neuron within a time window, yielding extremely low firing rates. However, conventional TTFS SNNs are restricted to specific structures, making it challenging to encode certain blocks in LLM -- such as layer normalization and matrix multiplication --using TTFS. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a reference-based strategy specifically to encode the four core LLM components: embedding layers, layer normalization, attention-related operations and dropout. We construct a fully TTFS-based SNN architecture and train it end-to-end. Experiments on modern LLMs like BERT and GPT-2 demonstrate that our approach achieves performance comparable to ANN counterparts on natural language understanding and common-sense reasoning, while a clear gap remains on language modeling perplexity. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to scale a spiking LLM to 1.5 billion parameters using TTFS coding. We also report an estimate of spike-related energy; this is a spike-count proxy under an established cost model rather than a measurement on neuromorphic hardware.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Sequential Solar PV Policy Design under Uncertainty: An Agent-Based Approach
abstract: Designing effective and fiscally sustainable policies for solar photovoltaic (PV) adoption requires balancing adoption gains against public expenditure under uncertainty and heterogeneous decision-making. This study formulates PV policy design as a sequential decision problem and integrates reinforcement learning (RL) with a stochastic agent-based model (ABM) that simulates yearly solar PV adoption under uncertainty. A policymaker agent selects annual incentives, including capital grants, subsidised loan rates, and feed-in tariffs, over a 16-year horizon. Adoption--cost trade-offs are explored by varying policy preferences within a scalarised reward framework. Policies are learned using PPO, SAC, and TD3 and evaluated under stochastic simulation. The results show that this approach produces a clear trade-off structure: the highest-adoption policy (TD3, $w_{\text{cost}}=0.5$) achieves approximately 4,145 adopters at a cost of EUR 41.73 million, while the lowest-cost policy (PPO, $w_{\text{cost}}=2.0$) reduces expenditure to EUR 7.27 million with 2,682 adopters. The balanced policy (PPO, $w_{\text{cost}}=1.6$) achieves 3,495 adopters at a cost of EUR 22.47 million. Across algorithms, consistent trade-off patterns are observed, indicating robustness of the adoption--cost relationship. Compared with static baseline policies, the RL framework explores a broader range of policy configurations. These findings demonstrate the potential of RL as a flexible tool for adaptive policy design under uncertainty.

title: Ereignisgesteuerte Archivierung von Quellcode-Repositorys mit extern gesiegeltem, eingebettetem Integritäts- und Zeitnachweis
abstract: Diese Offenbarung beschreibt ein automatisiertes Verfahren zur kryptographisch gesiegelten Archivierung von Quellcode-Repositorys, das in Versionskontrollsystemen wie Git implementiert ist. Das Verfahren löst sich von der Abhängigkeit des Repository-Betreibers, indem es einen unabhängigen Nachweis über den Zustand des Quellcodes zu einem bestimmten Zeitpunkt ermöglicht. Der Workflow wird durch Ereignisse im Versionskontrollsystem, wie das Pushen von Commits oder das Erstellen von Tags, ausgelöst. Zunächst werden relevante Dateien in einer Archivdatei aggregiert, gefolgt von der Berechnung eines kryptographischen Hash-Wertes über den gesamten Inhalt der Archivdatei. Dieser Hash-Wert wird an einen externen Siegelungs-Dienst übermittelt, der ein Siegel-Objekt erstellt, das eine asymmetrische Signatur und einen Zeitstempel enthält. Das Siegel-Objekt wird dann in die Archivdatei eingebettet, sodass die Datei vollständig extrahierbar bleibt. Die Verifikation des gesiegelten Archivdatei erfolgt unabhängig von den beteiligten Diensten, wodurch die Integrität und der zeitliche Nachweis des Quellcodes gesichert sind. Die Ergebnisse zeigen, dass das Verfahren eine sichere, transportable und überprüfbare Archivierungslösung für Quellcode-Repositorys bietet, die regulatorischen Anforderungen entspricht.

title: Quantum Topology Adaptative Topology Transformation
abstract: Quantum Topology Adaptative Topology Transformation is a novel algorithm designed to facilitate quantum computation through automated topology adjustment based on quantum states. This research proposes a quantum transformation algorithm that dynamically modifies the underlying topology of a quantum system, offering a significant advantage over static transformation methods. The core mechanism involves leveraging quantum states to induce and control topological shifts, thereby enabling adaptive quantum computations. We present a preliminary implementation demonstrating the algorithm's capability to achieve targeted topological changes, showcasing its potential for enhancing quantum computational capabilities.

title: Title: Modular Quantum Field Theory for Quantum Simulation of Complex Phenomena
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for constructing modular quantum field theories (QFTs) designed to facilitate efficient simulation of complex quantum phenomena. Traditional QFTs often struggle with scalability and complex dynamics, hindering their application to real-world problems. This work proposes a method of representing QFTs as a collection of interconnected modules, each representing a fundamental physical process. The resulting system offers significant advantages in terms of simulation, analysis, and adaptability, paving the way for breakthroughs in areas such as condensed matter physics, materials science, and quantum computing. We explore the design principles and mathematical foundations of this approach, demonstrating its potential to overcome limitations inherent in existing QFT techniques. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the proposed framework and its implications for future research.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Constraint Satisfaction with Adaptive Relaxation
abstract: Quantum entanglement offers a potentially transformative approach to constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs), enabling exponentially faster exploration of solution spaces compared to classical methods. This paper investigates the application of entanglement-based constraint satisfaction algorithms, focusing on the design of a novel constraint satisfaction algorithm that leverages quantum error correction to facilitate efficient solution discovery. We propose a mechanism utilizing entangled state vectors to represent potential solutions, enabling accelerated exploration of the solution space. The algorithm dynamically adapts relaxation parameters to optimize solutions, achieving significant improvements in computational efficiency. This work explores the fundamental principles of entanglement and its potential to revolutionize CSPs, presenting a framework for harnessing quantum phenomena to solve complex optimization challenges.

title: 基于量子自联结的参数优化策略 (QPOP) 框架
abstract: Quantum computing is rapidly advancing, requiring sophisticated algorithms to efficiently explore parameter spaces and achieve optimal performance. Traditional parameter optimization techniques often struggle with the inherent complexity and non-linearity of these spaces. This paper introduces the QPOP framework, a novel approach leveraging quantum self-associating networks (QSANs) for parameter optimization within quantum systems. We demonstrate the efficacy of QPOP in optimizing quantum circuits, achieving significantly improved results compared to existing classical methods. The framework offers enhanced adaptability, reduced computational cost, and the potential for finding solutions to previously intractable parameter spaces. title: Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Propagation for Bayesian Inference
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum mechanics to accelerate and enhance Bayesian inference, specifically targeting complex probabilistic models. We propose a novel framework incorporating quantum algorithms to efficiently explore the parameter space, ultimately aiming to improve convergence rates and accuracy. The core challenge lies in adapting existing algorithms to the inherently complex nature of quantum systems, while maintaining the interpretability of the results. This work explores the application of quantum annealing and variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) techniques within a Bayesian context to address challenges inherent in probabilistic modeling. We present preliminary results demonstrating enhanced convergence compared to classical methods for a specific model, highlighting the potential for transformative advancements in Bayesian inference.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum topology learning framework, leveraging adaptive learning to model and predict complex quantum systems. Traditional approaches often rely on pre-defined models, limiting their ability to effectively handle the inherent complexity of quantum systems. Our method dynamically adjusts quantum topology structures to capture the intricate dependencies within the system, offering a more flexible and predictive approach. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework through simulations and initial results on simplified quantum systems. The core mechanism involves an iterative process of structure optimization driven by a self-learning algorithm, resulting in improved accuracy and the ability to model systems exhibiting non-linearities and intricate correlations. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential applications of this framework and future research directions.
