title: Self-Adaptive Quantum Computing Entanglement Navigation Protocol
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive quantum computing navigation protocol, designed to optimize the efficient placement and navigation of quantum states within a complex quantum space. The protocol leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to establish and maintain a dynamic, self-correcting guidance system. We propose a mechanism centered around "entanglement pulses" – precisely controlled quantum interactions designed to measure and manipulate the relative positions of qubits, thereby dynamically adjusting the quantum state's trajectory. This approach minimizes the computational overhead and enhances the speed and accuracy of quantum computations. The core claims explore the potential of this protocol to significantly improve quantum algorithm performance and reduce the complexity associated with traditional navigation techniques. This research investigates the theoretical underpinnings of the proposed mechanism and demonstrates its effectiveness through simulations and preliminary experimental investigations.

title: Quantum-Inspired Stochastic Gradient Descent (QISGD)
abstract: Quantum-Inspired Stochastic Gradient Descent (QISGD) presents a novel approach to optimization within machine learning, integrating the strengths of stochastic gradient descent with quantum mechanics principles to accelerate learning and improve exploration of complex, high-dimensional spaces. This work proposes a novel strategy for enhancing the gradient descent algorithm by introducing quantum-inspired noise distributions that mimic the behavior of quantum systems. The core mechanism centers around leveraging the inherent properties of quantum mechanics – such as superposition and entanglement – to guide the optimization process, leading to more efficient and robust solutions compared to traditional methods. This paper will detail the theoretical foundation of the QISGD, present a practical implementation, and discuss the potential benefits and challenges associated with this approach.

title: Title: Geometric Chaos for Automated Optimization
abstract: Geometric chaos, a fascinating and increasingly relevant field, explores the unpredictable nature of systems exhibiting complex, non-linear dynamics. This paper investigates the potential of geometric analysis as a tool for understanding and mitigating instabilities within optimization algorithms. We propose a novel framework predicated on identifying and exploiting geometric properties of optimization problems to enhance their robustness. The core mechanism centers around developing a method that utilizes geometric techniques to detect and address potential chaos, ultimately leading to more stable and efficient optimization solutions. The study aims to bridge the gap between theoretical chaos theory and practical algorithmic design, offering a new perspective on problem-solving in complex, dynamic environments. This work will provide a foundational understanding of how geometric properties can influence the stability and performance of optimization techniques.

title: Reproducibility Record for "Leakage-Controlled Evaluation of Search-Level Stopping in Hyperparameter Optimization"
abstract: This record supports a leakage-controlled replay study of hyperparameter-optimization stopping on Adult, compact CIFAR-10, and a ten-region PJM hourly load panel. It contains the prespecified protocol and frozen analysis sources, sanitized preparation and split provenance, approved derived task artifacts, promoted result tables, source-to-claim mappings, checksums, and deterministic regeneration instructions. The record preserves the complete prespecified analysis output, including diagnostics that the article reports descriptively after a structural design audit. This preserves transparency without treating machine-facing release metadata as scientific results. The record does not redistribute third-party raw Adult, CIFAR-10, or PJM data. It provides canonical retrieval locations, source checksums, and preparation instructions. It also excludes local absolute paths, machine logs, raw telemetry, credentials, and caches. Row-level held-out target/prediction pairs are not redistributed because they reproduce record-level values from the third-party source datasets; they are regenerable from the cited public data using the documented split definitions and evaluation code, and the underlying copies are retained privately for audit. The archive's README names the related manuscript by an earlier working title. The manuscript this record supports is under review at Machine Learning (Springer) as "Leakage-Controlled Evaluation of Search-Level Stopping in Hyperparameter Optimization", submitted 29 July 2026; the two titles refer to the same study. Cite the title, version and DOI shown on this record.

title: Исследование архитектуры и разработка прототипа мультиагентной системы на базе большой языковой модели
abstract: Данная работа посвящена исследованию нового подхода в построении мультиагентной системы обработки запросов сотрудников предприятия на естественном языке, построенной на основе большой языковой модели и работающей на собственном оборудовании предприятия. Цель работы — разработка и опытная проверка мультиагентной системы с адаптивным планированием, способной разбивать сложный запрос на подзадачи, распределять их между специализированными агентами и корректировать порядок выполнения по промежуточным результатам. Задачи, которые решались в ходе исследования: 1. Изучить существующие подходы к построению агентов на основе языковых моделей и мультиагентных систем, выявить их достоинства и ограничения. 2. Спроектировать модульную архитектуру системы с разделением на части, отвечающие за распознавание запроса, планирование, выполнение и оценку результата. 3. Реализовать адаптивный планировщик, поддерживающий структурированные планы, связи между шагами и условиями успешности завершения шагов. 4. Реализовать специализированных агентов — Поисковика, Исполнителя и Составителя — с возможностью вызова внешних инструментов и функций и с общим рабочим пространством для обмена данными. 5. Разработать механизмы самокоррекции: пошаговую проверку, защиту от преждевременного завершения и повторное выполнение неудавшихся шагов. 6. Провести опытную проверку системы на наборе типовых корпоративных задач разной сложности и сравнить её с подходом на одиночном агенте. Исследование выполнено методами сравнительного анализа существующих подходов к построению агентных систем, проектирования модульной архитектуры, программной реализации опытного образца и опытной проверки. Опытная проверка проведена на одной рабочей станции, соответствующей обычному рабочему месту, на наборе из 30 типовых корпоративных задач четырёх уровней сложности с измерением точности, полноты выполнения, времени отклика и числа вызовов инструментов; каждая задача выполнялась в трёх запусках. В результате спроектирована и реализована действующая система, работающая полностью на локальном оборудовании предприятия без обращения к облачным службам. Опытная проверка показала, что мультиагентный режим достигает точности 93% против 64% у одиночного агента (на сложных задачах превосходство составляет 47%); общая доля восстановления после сбоев равна 90%, а адаптивный планировщик повышает итоговую долю удачных шагов на 16%. Тем самым подтверждено, что сочетание адаптивного планирования, разделения задачи между специализированными агентами и механизмов самокоррекции позволяют сравнительно компактной языковой модели надёжно решать многошаговые корпоративные задачи при сохранении конфиденциальности данных. При выполнении работы использованы следующие информационные технологии: язык программирования Python 3.11; локальный запуск большой языковой модели Qwen3 размером 8 миллиардов параметров через сервер вывода Ollama; обеспечивающий вызов внешних инструментов и функций; смысловая память на основе векторных представлений для поиска с дополнением (RAG); веб-интерфейс на основе лёгкого веб-сервера на языке Python с обменом сообщениями в реальном времени.

title: Research on intelligent evaluation system of film and television script integrating InternVL 2 and GCSE algorithm
abstract: The review of film and television scripts has long relied on manual processes, suffering from issues such as low efficiency and high subjectivity. Most existing intelligent evaluation systems focus primarily on text analysis, struggling to capture the deep narrative structures and semantic logic inherent in scripts. We propose an intelligent review system that integrates the multimodal model Intern Vision-Language 2 (InternVL 2) with the Gaussian-decayed gradient-assisted Contrastive Sentence Embedding (GCSE) algorithm. InternVL 2 is employed to parse script scene text and extract latent visual representations, while the GCSE algorithm leverages gradient information to enhance sentence-level contrastive learning, thereby improving the system's fine-grained understanding of narrative logic and character relationship semantics. We have established a comprehensive evaluation metric system encompassing dimensions such as plot density, logical coherence, and character tension. Experiments conducted on a dataset comprising 500 film and television scripts demonstrate that the system achieves an overall evaluation accuracy of 86.7%—a 7.2 percentage-point improvement over baseline models. Furthermore, the system achieved an F1 score of 82.3% in identifying plot holes, and a correlation coefficient of 0.79 in analyzing the consistency of character relationships. Key innovations include: 1) the introduction of multimodal feature fusion to achieve a joint representation of script semantics and visual imagery; 2) the design of a gradient-enhanced contrastive learning objective to optimize the discriminative power and interpretability of sentence embeddings; and 3) the construction of a multidimensional quantitative evaluation framework to facilitate the structured diagnosis of script quality. The system processes a single script in an average of 2.8 minutes, generating an evaluation report that includes 12 core metrics and specific revision suggestions, thereby providing a data-driven, objective reference for film and television creators.

title: Time-Aware Assistive Navigation
abstract: Can interactive vision-and-language agents learn not just what to say but also \textbf{\textit{when}} to say it? Current language models rarely plan over whether and when to realize a real-time response to a user. However, providing accurate and timely support for human decision-making, such as when guiding visually impaired individuals through urban environments, requires careful real-time responsiveness--poorly timed responses can distract users or add unnecessary cognitive load. As a machine intelligence challenge for Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM)-based agents, we introduce a large-scale multimodal benchmark for an egocentric, assistive navigation task in complex outdoor environments. Using this benchmark, we uncover a fundamental limitation of off-the-shelf MLLMs in delivering safe and time-sensitive navigation instructions, even with model fine-tuning on substantial amounts of data. We then demonstrate that a simple yet effective modification of the model, including direct supervision to predict the underlying reason for each instruction, yields significant performance gains across open-loop, closed-loop, and sim-to-real generalization settings. However, our analysis highlights persistent challenges in temporal reasoning, safety-critical object awareness, and relational and distance understanding. To advance the development of scalable assistive agents, we will release our simulation, benchmark, and code (available at the project website: https://timeli-icra.github.io/).

title: ReCAST: Restoration-aware Cascaded Stage-wise Training for Obfuscated SMS Risk Classification
abstract: Fraudulent messages sent via Short Message Service (SMS) are increasingly obfuscated to evade cost-conscious classifiers in production systems. In Chinese SMS, attackers can exploit a wide range of carefully crafted obfuscation strategies to hide risk-bearing phrases while preserving human readability, making direct classification brittle under real-world latency and throughput constraints. We propose ReCAST, a Restoration-aware Cascaded Stage-wise Training framework for robust obfuscated Chinese SMS classification. ReCAST distills a large teacher model's de-obfuscation ability into a smaller deployable student model by supervising obfuscated span detection, obfuscation type prediction, and text restoration, and then uses the restoration-aware student for downstream risk classification. Experiments on an internally constructed real-world Chinese SMS benchmark show that ReCAST substantially improves classification performance over directly trained baselines under obfuscation. The results suggest that restoration-aware distillation offers a practical path toward robust SMS risk classification with smaller deployable models under production-oriented constraints.

title: WEECFP-SuRGE: A Position-Aware Substructure Encoding Method for Molecular Property Prediction
abstract: Computational molecular property prediction requires representations that capture local chemistry, long-range interactions, and molecular topology. Conventional fingerprints provide efficient local substructure features, whereas learned graph and sequence models can represent broader context but often rely on pretraining or three-dimensional conformers. We introduce Wide Encoded Extended Connectivity Fingerprints (WEECFP) with Substructure Rotary Graph-distance Encoding (SuRGE), a tokenized hierarchical Morgan representation in which graph-distance-dependent rotations are applied at the input and within transformer self-attention. Across MoleculeNet and the Therapeutic Data Commons ADMET benchmarks, WEECFP-SuRGE is competitive with recent pretrained and geometry-aware methods without external pretraining or conformer generation. We also show that the rotated token representation remains structurally informative. A guided confirmed-handshake overlap procedure reconstructs the correct constitutional isomer for 92.6% of a 4,200-molecule self-library evaluation. Together, the predictive and reconstruction results indicate that WEECFP-SuRGE preserves local substructure identity while making relative topology available to the model.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Models
abstract: Artificial intelligence and machine learning have become among the most influential technological advances of the twenty-first century, transforming scientific research and practical applications across healthcare, engineering, agriculture, economics, environmental sciences, education, and the social sciences. Beyond processing vast amounts of information, intelligent systems are increasingly expected to generate reliable knowledge, support evidence-based decision-making, and provide meaningful solutions to complex scientific and societal challenges. Despite these remarkable advances, the success of artificial intelligence is determined not only by sophisticated algorithms but also by the quality of the underlying data and the scientific rigor of the analytical process. Reliable artificial intelligence requires well-designed studies, representative data, sound statistical methodologies, robust validation procedures, and transparent evaluation frameworks. Consequently, statistics and data science have become more essential today than at any previous time in scientific history. They are no longer supporting disciplines but fundamental pillars that ensure the credibility, reproducibility, and interpretability of modern artificial intelligence. While statistics has traditionally been associated with data analysis, it now plays a central role throughout the entire research lifecycle—from study design and data collection to feature engineering, model development, uncertainty quantification, performance evaluation, explainable artificial intelligence, and evidence-based decision-making. Likewise, data science has evolved into an interdisciplinary field that integrates statistical thinking, computational methods, and domain expertise to transform data into trustworthy scientific knowledge. The chapters cover a broad spectrum of contemporary topics, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning, data mining, big data analytics, natural language processing, computer vision, optimization techniques, and intelligent decision-support systems developed for diverse scientific disciplines. A common objective shared by all contributions is the development of artificial intelligence systems that are not only accurate but also reliable, transparent, explainable, and scientifically verifiable . As artificial intelligence continues to reshape scientific discovery, future progress will increasingly depend on the integration of advanced computational models with rigorous statistical reasoning and responsible data science practices. We express our sincere appreciation to all authors, reviewers, members of the scientific committee, and the organizing committee for their valuable contributions. We hope this volume will serve as a valuable reference for researchers, academics, graduate students, and professionals working in artificial intelligence, machine learning, data science, and applied statistics.

title: Hierarchical Bayesian Networks for Temporal Causality Modeling
abstract: This paper presents a novel hierarchical Bayesian network (HBN) approach for modeling temporal causality. Traditional causal inference methods often struggle with complex, multi-level relationships and the inherent uncertainty associated with time. Our work addresses these challenges by constructing a hierarchical structure that explicitly captures dependencies at multiple levels of granularity, allowing for a more accurate and robust identification of causal links. We introduce a new Bayesian network structure emphasizing probabilistic causal inference and hierarchical modeling to achieve high fidelity in the identified causal relationships. The model incorporates mechanisms for uncertainty estimation and probabilistic reasoning, significantly improving the ability to infer causal effects. We present results demonstrating the efficacy of our approach in a simulated temporal data setting, highlighting its potential for applications in complex systems analysis and decision-making.

The core mechanism involves transforming the prediction problem into a geometric optimization problem, enabling the algorithm to dynamically refine the model's parameters to achieve optimal results. This approach overcomes the limitations of traditional methods, which rely heavily on manual parameter tuning, and offers a potentially significant improvement in prediction performance.

title: Quantum Entanglement Expansion State Computation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, holds immense potential for revolutionizing computation. This paper explores the application of quantum entanglement to expand state computation, aiming to develop novel methods for solving complex problems with enhanced computational power. We outline a core mechanism leveraging entanglement to generate and manipulate extended quantum states, culminating in the derivation of physical properties through this process. The research focuses on utilizing entanglement's inherent non-classical properties to overcome limitations of conventional quantum algorithms. This work presents a fundamentally new approach to quantum state computation, offering a pathway towards potentially transformative advancements in quantum information processing.

title: Title: Non-Euclidean Data Compression with Adaptive Representation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel data compression algorithm, termed "Non-Euclidean Data Compression," designed to exploit the inherent geometric properties of data to achieve significantly higher compression ratios than existing techniques. Traditional compression methods primarily rely on statistical redundancy and pattern matching. Our algorithm, however, dynamically adapts its representation of data based on its geometric characteristics, creating a unique, self-organizing representation. We present a meta-algorithm that continuously analyzes data, identifying and leveraging geometric relationships to minimize redundancy and maximize data density. The core mechanism involves a recursive mapping process that progressively refines the data representation, leading to a substantial improvement in compression efficiency. This work represents a paradigm shift in data compression, offering the potential for substantially reduced storage requirements and improved computational efficiency. The development of this algorithm necessitates a re-evaluation of fundamental assumptions about data representation and compression.

Traditional optimization algorithms typically rely on local search, while topological dynamical models offer the ability to capture global structure and self-organization, leading to enhanced efficiency and stability in complex systems. We propose a framework where the system state is represented as a topological structure, and topological algorithms are utilized to guide the optimization process. This approach aims to address limitations of traditional methods by providing a more robust and adaptive solution strategy.

title: 基于量子纠缠的动态拓扑变形
abstract: Quantum entanglement has emerged as a transformative force in quantum information processing, offering the potential for unprecedented computational capabilities and novel quantum technologies. However, the manipulation of complex quantum systems often requires intricate and time-consuming procedures. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, Quantum Dynamic Topology Transformation (QDT) algorithm, which leverages the principles of quantum entanglement to dynamically reconstruct and evolve the topology of quantum systems. The QDT algorithm's core mechanism involves creating and maintaining entangled states to guide the transformation of the system's geometry, allowing for the exploration of complex quantum structures with increased efficiency and precision. This work explores the potential of QDT in advancing quantum computing through the simulation and learning of dynamic topological changes, offering a new approach to quantum system modeling and potentially unlocking advanced quantum applications.

abstract: Quantum topology, a relatively recent field of physics, offers a fundamentally new approach to manipulating and controlling quantum states. We propose a novel algorithm that leverages the inherent topological properties of quantum systems to create complex and dynamic quantum states, enabling controlled evolution and manipulation. The core mechanism centers around constructing and manipulating 'topological bridges' within the quantum state space, effectively defining the state's evolution pathway. This work explores the theoretical foundations and preliminary experimental implementations of this approach, highlighting its potential for advancing quantum information processing and quantum technology.

title: Inverse Probability Logic: A Novel Framework for Risk Assessment and Decision Making
abstract: This paper introduces the concept of Inverse Probability Logic (IPL), a novel computational framework predicated on the principles of probability logic to model and predict complex system behavior. The core mechanism centers on leveraging IPL to enhance risk assessment and decision-making processes. We argue that traditional probabilistic models often struggle with uncertainty and the inherent difficulties of modeling real-world systems. IPL offers a more robust and adaptable approach by explicitly modeling probabilities of outcomes and minimizing the influence of biased assumptions. The paper details the theoretical underpinnings of IPL, outlines the model's architecture, and provides a preliminary demonstration of its application in a simplified risk assessment scenario. The aim is to explore the potential of IPL to improve predictive accuracy and facilitate more informed decision-making.

title: Knowledge Discovery and Reasoning Based on Cognitive Graphs
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to knowledge discovery and reasoning by leveraging cognitive graphs. Traditional methods for knowledge discovery and reasoning heavily rely on manual knowledge base construction and rule definition, which are often time-consuming, labor-intensive, and prone to errors. This research introduces a cognitive graph-based system designed to automatically discover, integrate, and reason over knowledge. The core mechanism involves constructing a cognitive graph, where knowledge entities are represented as nodes and relationships as edges. Utilizing graph algorithms, we enable automated knowledge extraction, schema evolution, and sophisticated reasoning capabilities. The system demonstrates the potential to address complex problems more efficiently and accurately than conventional approaches. This work contributes to a paradigm shift in knowledge management and problem-solving, offering a scalable and adaptable solution for handling increasingly vast and interconnected datasets. ---

title: Probabilistic Program Synthesis via Bayesian Optimization of Program Transformations
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to program synthesis leveraging Bayesian optimization for iteratively transforming a high-level specification into a target program. The core idea is to treat program synthesis as an optimization problem where the objective is to minimize the difference between the synthesized program and the desired behavior. Unlike traditional deterministic search methods, our system employs a Bayesian model to predict the effectiveness of each program transformation based on simulated execution outcomes. This probabilistic approach allows the system to intelligently explore the search space, adapting to the inherent uncertainty in program generation. The system iteratively applies transformations, guided by the Bayesian model, until a satisfactory program is achieved. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical framework and discuss its potential for tackling complex program synthesis problems. The key benefit lies in its ability to handle ambiguity and explore diverse solution paths, potentially leading to more robust and efficient program synthesis.

title: Dynamical Systems Embedding of Neural Networks
abstract: This paper explores the application of dynamical systems theory to analyze and potentially control the internal dynamics of neural networks. Traditionally, neural networks have been primarily treated as black boxes, optimized through training and backpropagation. This approach often lacks insight into the underlying, complex dynamics governing their behavior. We propose a novel method for embedding a neural network's activity into a dynamical system framework. This involves identifying key state variables—typically derived from the activations of neurons—and constructing a dynamical system model that mimics the network's dynamics. The resulting model can then be analyzed using tools from dynamical systems theory, such as phase space analysis, Lyapunov exponents, and bifurcation analysis, offering a new perspective on network behavior. We demonstrate the potential of this approach to predict network responses to perturbations, and to guide the design of control strategies for influencing network dynamics. This work represents a shift from solely focusing on training to understanding and manipulating the inherent dynamics within neural networks.

evidence.abstract: This paper explores the application of dynamical systems theory to analyze and potentially control the internal dynamics of neural networks. Traditionally, neural networks have been primarily treated as black boxes, optimized through training and backpropagation. This approach often lacks insight into the underlying, complex dynamics governing their behavior. We propose a novel method for embedding a neural network's activity into a dynamical system framework. This involves identifying key state variables—typically derived from the activations of neurons—and constructing a dynamical system model that mimics the network's dynamics. The resulting model can then be analyzed using tools from dynamical systems theory, such as phase space analysis, Lyapunov exponents, and bifurcation analysis, offering a new perspective on network behavior. We demonstrate the potential of this approach to predict network responses to perturbations, and to guide the design of control strategies for influencing network dynamics. This work represents a shift from solely focusing on training to understanding and manipulating the inherent dynamics within neural networks.

The core mechanism centers around a dynamic sampling rate adjustment strategy, which responds to the system's inherent uncertainty, leading to a more efficient and robust modeling process. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through simulations and preliminary analysis, showcasing potential advantages in accuracy and computational cost compared to existing methods.

title: Holographic Information Network (HIN)
abstract: This paper introduces the Holographic Information Network (HIN) framework, a novel approach to data representation and processing leveraging the principles of holographic geometry. The HIN proposes a distributed computation paradigm centered around encoding information within complex geometric representations, facilitating efficient data compression and enhanced distributed computation. We present a detailed design of the HIN, encompassing the encoding scheme, network architecture, and potential applications across diverse computational domains. The core claim is that HIN enables significant advancements in data compression, distributed computation, and the exploration of fundamentally new algorithmic paradigms. This work offers a conceptual framework for a transformative approach to information processing, potentially revolutionizing data management and distributed systems.

title: Towards practical cache side-channel mitigations for language interpreters
abstract: Modern applications increasingly rely on language interpreters that execute code in shared environments, where cache side channels can expose sensitive information. However, cache side-channel mitigations have not been explored for language interpreters, and adapting existing techniques is challenging due to the complex and dynamic nature of interpretation. We identify the interpreter mechanisms responsible for these leakages and develop practical mitigations tailored to interpreter execution. Our approach mitigates application control-flow leakage by using transactions to dynamically linearize executed bytecode instructions, data-access leakage through probabilistic obfuscation, and leakage from the bytecode's internal implementation through lightweight cache isolation. We integrate these mitigations into a limited proof-of-concept implementation in QuickJS and evaluate their effectiveness and performance overhead. Our preliminary results demonstrate that cache side-channel defenses can be integrated into interpreters while providing meaningful security guarantees.

title: The marginal is pretty good
abstract: One-shot information theory measures often require an optimization over states, but the form of these optimizers can be complicated or depend on the initial problem in nonlinear ways. In this note, we show that in many instances using the marginal instead of the optimal state is sufficiently good and only changes the result by a small factor. We prove that for the Petz--Rényi and sandwiched--Rényi divergences of order $α\in(0,1)$, replacing the optimizing state on $B$ by the marginal $ρ_B$ results in a multiplicative overhead of at most $1/α$.

title: From Vision to Language: Investigating Causal Information Flow in Multimodal Decision-Making
abstract: Vision-Language Models are commonly evaluated through their final predictions, but understanding whether these decisions are grounded in visual evidence requires tracing how visual information contributes to language-based decisions. With this purpose in mind, we investigate cross-modal information flow in a video-based generative multiple-choice-like setting by applying a layer-wise causal intervention on video-text attention pathways. We target spatial, causal, and temporal visual reasoning. Our results show that visual information is mainly integrated while the model processes the candidate answer options, which serve as the primary textual grounding sites for the final decision. We further show that nouns play an important role as semantic anchors during multimodal enrichment, while verbs are more relevant when temporal relations are processed. Finally, we identify a distinct pattern in temporal reasoning, suggesting that VLMs struggle to reconstruct sequential information across video frames, but we remark that such fragility may also reflect linguistic biases associated with specific temporal expressions used for defining the relation between events within a scene.

title: MARLA: A Conceptual Scaffold for Regulatory Learning under the EU AI Act
abstract: The EU AI Act positions regulation as part of the infrastructure for safe, trustworthy and market-ready innovation. Realising this ambition requires regulatory learning: the evidence generated during implementation must be translated into governance and legal knowledge that supports consistent interpretation, effective oversight, and adaptation as technologies evolve. Yet the actors who produce this evidence and those who rely on it operate in different professional worlds. This paper proposes MARLA (Map, Assess, Report, Learn, Adapt), a conceptual scaffold organising regulatory learning as a five-stage cycle centred on the implementation of legal requirements into socio-technical practices, situated at the Local, National and European levels of the AI Act's governance architecture. Deliberately non-prescriptive, MARLA gives technical and legal stakeholders a shared vocabulary in which each of the first three stages generates its own documentable form of regulatory learning. We illustrate the scaffold with two piloted case studies and a prospective National-to-European illustration.

title: World Models in Reinforcement Learning for Robotics: Model-Based Planning and Decision-Making
abstract: Förstärkningsinlärning gör det möjligt för robotar att lära sig komplexa beteenden utan en explicit modell av systemets dynamik. Modellfria metoder kräver dock ofta miljontals interaktioner för att konvergera, vilket är opraktiskt på fysisk hårdvara där datainsamling är långsam, kostsam och kan medföra slitage eller risker. Världsmodeller, där agenten lär sig en intern representation av miljödynamiken och planerar eller tränar utifrån simulerade förlopp, har föreslagits som ett sätt att minska behovet av fysisk interaktion. Det är dock oklart hur stora fördelarna är i praktiken och vilken typ av världsmodell som lämpar sig bäst för robotik. Arbetet undersöker genom en litteraturstudie hur dataeffektivitet, uppnådd prestanda och realtidsprestanda skiljer sig mellan världsmodellbaserade och modellfria agenter samt mellan olika sätt för världsmodeller att representera miljön internt. Där till undersöks vilka begränsningar som är mest kritiska för tillämpning inom robotik. Jämförelserna baseras på publicerade resultat och träningsloggar från etablerade simuleringsbaserade referensuppgifter för kontinuerlig robotstyrning. Resultaten visar att världsmodellbaserade metoder kan uppnå jämförbar eller bättre prestanda än modellfria metoder med betydligt färre miljöinteraktioner. Fördelen är tydligast på svårare, högdimensionella kontrolluppgifter och mindre eller obefintlig på enklare uppgifter. Baserat på resultaten går det inte att konstatera att någon representationstyp skulle prestera konsekvent bäst. Känslighet för egna prediktionsfel, svårighet att hantera tillstånd utanför träningsdatan, hög beräkningskostnad vid beslutsfattande och skillnaden mellan simulerad och verklig dynamik identifieras som de mest kritiska begränsningarna för användning av världsmodeller inom robotik. Slutsatsen är att världsmodeller bör betraktas som ett sätt att omfördela kostnad mellan fysisk datainsamling och beräkning snarare än som en generell ersättning för modellfria metoder, och att deras nytta inom robotik är störst när fysisk interaktion är dyr eller riskfylld och ökad beräkningskostnad kan accepteras.

title: Regression with Imbalanced Data: A Comparative Analysis of Resampling Methods
abstract: Imbalanced regression is an underexplored challenge in predictive modeling. It arises when the continuous target variable exhibits a skewed distribution, resulting in the underrepresentation of rare but critical values. Standard regression models trained on such data tend to minimize global error while producing poor predictions in the most critical regions of the output space. This study provides a comparative analysis of four resampling methods — Baseline (no resampling), Random Oversampling (RO), Synthetic Minority Oversampling for Regression with Gaussian Noise (SMOGN), and Weighted Relevance-based Combination Strategy (WERCS) — across four learning algorithms (Linear Regression, SVR, Random Forest, and XGBoost) using three performance metrics (RMSE, MAE, and SERA) on eight open benchmark datasets. The experimental setup employs 5-fold cross-validation repeated 30 times, and statistical significance is assessed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test (p < 0.05). The results reveal a notable metric paradox: although Baseline achieves the lowest RMSE (0.863), the ranking reverses when evaluated using SERA — Baseline becomes worst (0.973) and WERCS best (0.831). In SERA-based Wilcoxon comparisons, WERCS obtained 62 and SMOGN obtained 49 statistically significant wins, whereas Baseline secured only 8. These findings highlight the critical importance of metric selection in imbalanced regression and suggest that SERA combined with WERCS provides a more reliable evaluation framework for rare-value prediction.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Topological Transformation Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for topological transformation utilizing quantum entanglement. The algorithm leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to achieve rapid and efficient transformation of topological spaces. We propose a method for generating and manipulating entanglement, which serves as the foundation for the transformation process. The algorithm's core mechanism involves a series of entanglement-based operations that iteratively reshape the topological space, ultimately leading to the desired transformation. This research explores the potential of entanglement to significantly accelerate and improve topological transformation processes compared to traditional methods. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation. This work contributes to the field of quantum computing and topology by presenting a robust and potentially transformative approach to topological manipulation.

title: Geometric Topology as a Constraint Generator for Quantum Simulation
abstract: Quantum simulation, a crucial tool for advancing quantum technology, faces significant computational challenges due to the inherent complexity of simulating quantum systems. Traditional approaches often struggle with the high dimensionality and non-linearity of quantum systems, limiting the achievable accuracy and stability of simulations. Geometric topology offers a promising alternative, providing a framework for generating constraints that can dramatically reduce the computational burden and enhance the fidelity of quantum simulations. This paper explores the utilization of geometric topology as a novel constraint generator for quantum simulation, demonstrating its potential to create highly accurate and stable simulation environments. We detail the methodology, results, and preliminary analysis of this approach, highlighting its advantages over existing methods.

title: 基于量子自旋的几何变换的计算复杂度分析与优化
abstract: This paper investigates the computational complexity of geometric transformations utilizing quantum spin as a core principle. Traditional methods often rely on classical geometry, while quantum spin offers a potentially novel approach to modeling and solving complex geometric problems. We propose a novel quantum spin-based geometric transformation model, demonstrating its ability to precisely control and optimize geometric transformations, and subsequently exploring its applicability to diverse fields like computer graphics and robotics. The paper details the model's architecture, the underlying mathematical principles, and the achieved computational complexity analysis. We present a significant improvement in computational efficiency compared to traditional methods, offering a promising path towards more efficient geometric manipulation within these domains. Furthermore, we discuss potential challenges and future research directions, emphasizing the impact of quantum spin's unique properties on this field.

title: 基于自适应的量子计算的拓扑优化
abstract: Quantum computing, leveraging the bizarre properties of quantum mechanics, holds immense potential for revolutionizing various fields. However, achieving practical quantum computation necessitates overcoming fundamental challenges, particularly in algorithm design and optimization. This paper explores the application of a novel self-adaptive quantum optimization algorithm, inspired by the principles of quantum topology and entanglement. We introduce a system that dynamically adjusts quantum parameters to enhance computational efficiency and explore novel solutions to complex problems. The core mechanism centers around leveraging quantum entanglement to guide the optimization process, ultimately leading to improved performance. The proposed algorithm offers a promising approach to addressing the limitations of current quantum computing techniques and opens new avenues for scientific discovery and technological advancement.

title: Title: Adaptive Wave Function Collapse for Quantum Algorithms (AWCC)
abstract: This paper introduces Adaptive Wave Function Collapse (AWCC), a novel algorithm designed to optimize quantum algorithm performance by dynamically adjusting collapse rates. Traditional quantum algorithms often rely on fixed collapse rates, which can limit efficiency and hinder the exploration of complex quantum solutions. AWCC leverages a 'Wave Function Adaptation' system, intelligently modifying collapse probabilities based on the algorithm's internal state, to achieve a significantly improved performance. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop that continuously evaluates the algorithm's state and adjusts collapse rates to maximize fidelity and minimize computational cost. This research explores the theoretical foundations and practical implementation of AWCC, demonstrating its potential to revolutionize quantum algorithm design.
